title: Synchrony Says Walmart to Drop Lawsuit Against Credit-Card Issuer
summary: Synchrony Financial announced that Walmart Inc. has agreed to dismiss a lawsuit against the bank, which had alleged that Synchrony breached terms of their credit-card deal. Walmart was seeking at least $800 million in damages. This development comes after Walmart decided last year to replace Synchrony as its exclusive credit-card issuer with Capital One Financial Corp.

title: Data-Center Market Is Booming Amid Shift to Cloud
summary: The data-center market is experiencing a boom driven by the shift to cloud computing, even as many businesses are moving IT operations online. This has led to increased demand and consolidation among data-center operators as co-location service providers acquire facilities to lease space to major cloud services like Amazon.com Inc. and Microsoft Corp. The sector is seeing more deals as data-center landlords and cloud providers seek more facilities.

title: Netflix Just Made a Truly Radical Change Affecting Millions of New Subscribers, and It's Totally Brilliant. (Or Maybe Insane--Time Will Tell)
summary: Netflix has implemented a significant change by no longer allowing new subscribers to pay via iTunes, aiming to avoid the substantial "Apple tax" of 15% to 30% on subscription revenue. This strategic move, which could save Netflix hundreds of millions, shifts new users to subscribe directly through the Netflix app, cutting Apple out of its commission. While potentially risking some new subscribers, Netflix is betting that its strong demand across platforms will outweigh any losses and make the decision financially brilliant in the long run.

title: Is Apple Still a ‘forever’ Company? How About Facebook?
summary: This article questions the "forever company" thesis for tech giants like Apple and Facebook, highlighting recent market shifts and challenges. It discusses how Apple's plunging shares due to demand issues in China and Nokia's past trajectory suggest even dominant companies face significant hurdles. The piece also explores the concept of S-curves in technology, suggesting that while current tech giants are strong, a new S-curve, potentially augmented reality or AI, could reset the competitive landscape.

title: ADT Unveils New Command and Control Security System, Replacing ADT Pulse
summary: ADT announced the launch of its new ADT Command Panel & Control Platform (ADT Command) at CES 2019, replacing the previous ADT Pulse system. This new smart home security system integrates with a suite of smart security and home automation products, including ADT Go, ADT Video Doorbell, and voice control with Amazon Alexa and Google Home, offering advanced features like geofencing technology and an interactive crime map. The system focuses on enhanced protection, control, and connectivity for customers.

title: Microsoft and Kroger want to show you Minority Report-style ads
summary: Microsoft and Kroger are partnering to develop high-tech grocery stores that will feature digital shelving displays with real-time pricing and personalized advertisements, reminiscent of "Minority Report." These ads will be tailored to individual customers based on demographics and, for opted-in users, previous purchase history, utilizing facial recognition and AI. While not cashierless like Amazon Go, the stores aim to enhance the shopping experience with guided navigation and in-app scanning for faster checkout.

title: For Many Builders, Smart Homes Now Come Standard
summary: New-home builders are increasingly integrating smart home technology as a standard feature due to its widespread adoption and affordability. Companies like Meritage Homes and Lennar are partnering with tech giants such as Amazon, Google, and Apple to offer various smart devices and services, aiming to meet consumer demand and differentiate new constructions from existing homes. This shift is driven by consumer expectations and the decreasing cost of smart home tech, making it a compelling baseline amenity for new builds.

title: Resideo Unveils A New Degree Of Whole Home Comfort At CES 2019
summary: Resideo announced its new Honeywell Home T-Series Smart Thermostats (T9 and T10 Pro) at CES 2019, featuring innovative wireless smart room sensors. These thermostats aim to provide whole-home comfort by adjusting temperatures where and when needed, optimizing for sleep at night and energy savings when away. The T9 model offers DIY installation, while the T10 Pro is professionally installed and includes humidity and ventilation controls.

title: Vuzix announces the launch of consumer version of its Blade augmented reality smart glasses
summary: Vuzix has launched the consumer version of its Blade augmented reality smart glasses for USD$999.99, featuring proprietary waveguide optics, a full-color display, and an HD camera. The glasses integrate with an Android-based OS, a companion app for customization and notifications, and are expected to ship in early February 2019. Vuzix is also partnering with Amazon for Alexa integration and AccuWeather for AR weather experiences, highlighting the Blade's potential for both prosumers and consumers as a step towards wearable computing.

title: Best Consumer Discretionary ETFs for Q1 2021
summary: This article identifies the best consumer discretionary ETFs for Q1 2021 based on performance over the past year. The top three ETFs highlighted are IBUY, ONLN, and NERD, which primarily focus on online retail and digital entertainment, showcasing their strong returns and key holdings. These ETFs provide diversified exposure to non-essential goods and services, a sector that has outperformed the broader market.

title: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos, Wife MacKenzie Set to Divorce
summary: Amazon.com Inc. CEO Jeff Bezos and his wife MacKenzie Bezos announced their decision to divorce after a long trial separation. The announcement comes as Amazon recently became Wall Street's most valuable company, and Jeff Bezos' fortune has soared to over $160 billion. The article also touches on Amazon's growth and diversification since its founding in 1994.

title: JP Morgan's Dimon hosted a private dinner for pharma executives, and a major topic was Amazon
summary: Jamie Dimon hosted a private dinner for pharmaceutical executives, including those from Eli Lilly, Pfizer, and Johnson & Johnson, ahead of J.P. Morgan's health-care conference. A major topic of discussion was Amazon's ambitions in the health-care market and the J.P. Morgan-Amazon-Berkshire Hathaway health partnership. Dimon expressed the group's desire to lower health-care costs, a sentiment echoed by attending executives like Eli Lilly CEO Dave Ricks, who encouraged corporate America to take a more active role in employee health benefits.

title: Exclusive: West Elm Hotel checks into Bay Area with Oakland groundbreaking
summary: The West Elm Hotel has broken ground in Uptown Oakland, marking the brand's entry into the Bay Area. This four-star hotel will be located near Square's new offices in Uptown Station and thousands of residential units under construction. The article highlights the trend of retailers expanding into the hotel industry.

title: The Bath & Body Works Semi-Annual Sale Is Ending Soon, So Snag Those $10 Candles While You Still Can
summary: The Bath & Body Works Semi-Annual Sale is coming to an end on January 18th, offering significant discounts of up to 75% off. Shoppers can find deals like $4 body care, $4 Wallflower refills, and 3-Wick Candles for $10, which were originally $25. The sale also brings back discontinued fragrances and provides an opportunity to stock up on new scents for the year.

title: JB Hunt acquires ‘big and bulky’ last-mile provider
summary: J.B. Hunt has acquired Cory 1st Choice Home Delivery for $100 million to expand its final mile delivery capabilities for "big and bulky" products, especially furniture. This strategic investment aims to address the growing demand in e-commerce for oversized items and mitigate issues like damaged deliveries. The acquisition includes 14 warehouses and leverages over 1,000 independent contractors to perform more than 2 million annual deliveries.

title: With Google project, Minnesota joins the boom in megasized data centers
summary: Minnesota is set to join the growing trend of megasized data centers with Google Inc.'s proposed project near the Sherco power generating station in Becker, Minn. This $600 million facility will consume significant electricity and contribute to the regional boom in "hyperscale" data centers being built by major tech companies. While these centers employ few people once operational, their construction phases provide hundreds of jobs, particularly for skilled electricians, and are critical for the infrastructure of cloud-based computing.

title: Walmart and CVS Split Over Pricing
summary: Walmart and CVS Health's partnership has ended due to a dispute over prescription drug pricing, leading CVS pharmacies to no longer include Walmart pharmacies in their network for most consumers. CVS stock fell 1.5 percent following the announcement, with CVS citing Walmart's requested rates as leading to higher costs for their clients and consumers. Despite the split, CVS stated its retail pharmacy network remains robust, with over 63,000 other pharmacies providing ample access for its members.

title: BlackRock’s Fink looks to a ‘deep bench’ to pick heir
summary: Larry Fink, BlackRock's CEO, is looking to his firm's "deep bench" of executives to name a successor, with Mark Wiedman's recent promotion positioning him at the top of the list. Despite this, other senior figures including Mark McCombe, Mark Wiseman, Rob Goldstein, Rob Kapito, and Rich Kushel remain in contention. The article details the backgrounds, key accomplishments, and potential challenges for each of these possible heirs to the leadership of the $6.4tn asset management group.

title: Sears staves off demise, but Volusia Mall store still closing
summary: Sears has secured a reprieve from bankruptcy thanks to a bid from its chairman, Eddie Lampert, which could save approximately 400 stores and tens of thousands of jobs. However, despite this broader development, the Sears department store at Volusia Mall is still slated to close in March as part of previously announced closures. This closure is one of 80 national locations Sears Holdings plans to shutter, while local Sears Hometown and Outlet stores, which are separate entities, will remain open.

title: Netflix beats on subscriber growth, but misses slightly on revenue — stock falls after hours
summary: Netflix reported mixed fourth-quarter 2018 earnings, beating EPS estimates and subscriber additions but falling short on revenue. The company’s stock dropped after hours due to the revenue miss and lower-than-expected guidance for Q1 2019. Despite increased content spending and cash burn, Netflix saw strong international subscriber growth and plans to improve free cash flow after 2019.

title: Semiconductor Company Wiliot Raises $30 Million, Demos Sticker-Sized Bluetooth Sensor Tag
summary: Wiliot, a fabless semiconductor company, has raised $30 million in Series B funding, bringing its total to $50 million, with investments from Amazon Web Services, Samsung Venture Investment Corp, and Avery Dennison. The company demonstrated its sticker-sized Bluetooth sensor tag, an ARM processor powered by ambient radio frequencies, at NRF 2019. This technology enables disposable, battery-free electronics for IoT, offering new ways for consumers and manufacturers to interact with products and track them in real-time.

title: Amazon pushing hard into ocean shipping, making it easier for Chinese goods to get to you
summary: Amazon has significantly expanded its ocean shipping services from China to the U.S., reportedly sending nearly 4.7 million cartons of consumer goods in the past year. This move is part of Amazon's broader strategy to control its entire transportation network, offering a soup-to-nuts service that eliminates middlemen for goods manufactured in China. Experts believe this development will transform the global e-commerce landscape and accelerate globalization by enabling small Chinese factories to sell directly to American consumers.

title: First battery-free Bluetooth sticker sensor tag demonstrated
summary: Wiliot, a semiconductor innovator, has demonstrated the first-ever sticker-sized, battery-free Bluetooth sensor tag powered by scavenging ambient radio frequencies. This technology allows for low-cost, disposable electronics capable of connecting products with packaging, enabling new IoT applications. AWS, Samsung, and Avery Dennison have invested in Wiliot, recognizing the potential of these tags for real-time tracking, interactive consumer engagement, and automated product management.

title: Corsair Vengeance 5180 gaming PC review: "A beautiful machine with performance to match"
summary: This article reviews the Corsair Vengeance 5180 gaming PC, highlighting its powerful components, excellent dual-chamber design, and brilliant RGB lighting. While acknowledging its large size and non-overclockable CPU, the review praises its performance at 1080p and 1440p and its overall value for gamers seeking a pre-built machine.

title: Starboard, Elliott Management Call on eBay to Shed StubHub, Classifieds
summary: Activist investors Starboard and Elliott Management are urging eBay to divest its StubHub ticketing and classified-ads businesses. This move comes as eBay's shares have underperformed, with the company struggling to redefine itself beyond its auction house origins and compete with e-commerce giants like Amazon. The proposed changes by these hedge funds could lead to a significant restructuring of the company.

title: 20 Things You Didn’t Know about Sierra Trading Post
summary: This article details 20 lesser-known facts about Sierra Trading Post, from its founding by Keith and Bobbi Richardson in 1986 to its acquisition by TJX Companies in 2012. It covers the company's growth, catalog innovations, relocation to Cheyenne, early online presence, community involvement, unique company culture, and the founders' passion for breeding German Shorthaired Pointers. The article highlights Sierra's commitment to quality outdoor products and its significant contributions to local economies.

title: Weis Markets rolls out aggressive price cuts
summary: Weis Markets has implemented its most aggressive price reduction program to date, cutting prices on over 7,000 products to compete with rivals like Giant, Wegmans, Aldi, and Walmart. This "Low, Low Price" program follows a previous $101 million investment in store upgrades and technology, and aims to attract price-sensitive shoppers and retain loyal customers amidst increasing competition and rising food prices. The company reported a significant profit increase of 200% in the same quarter of the prior year, suggesting a positive financial position for this strategic move.

title: Elliott pushes for organizational changes at eBay after taking $1.4B stake
summary: Activist hedge fund Elliott Management Corp. has acquired a $1.4 billion stake in eBay Inc. and is pushing for significant organizational changes, including the sale of its online classifieds unit and StubHub ticket marketplace. Elliott believes these units would be more valuable as independent companies and that the divestitures would allow eBay to focus more sharply on its core e-commerce marketplace. The firm also recommends operational improvements and believes these changes could nearly double eBay's stock price.

title: The Ultimate Digital Transformation: Microsoft Helps Kroger Become Tech Company
summary: Kroger, America's largest grocery retailer, is undergoing a significant digital transformation by partnering with Microsoft to become a technology company. They are developing and selling cloud-based "Retail as a Service" (RaaS) solutions, powered by Microsoft Azure and IoT, to other retailers. This initiative aims to redefine the shopping experience through innovations like paperless smart shelves and hyper-personalization, creating new revenue opportunities beyond traditional grocery operations.

title: Sonos Amp Streaming Amplifier Review
summary: The Sonos Amp streaming amplifier is reviewed, highlighting its versatility and ease of integration into Sonos multiroom audio systems, despite some limitations in EQ and sound with certain speakers. This new device replaces the Connect:Amp, offering enhanced features and design improvements based on extensive feedback from custom integrators and DIY enthusiasts, effectively bridging the gap between consumer preferences and professional installation needs.

title: Synchrony Says Walmart to Drop Lawsuit Against Credit-Card Issuer
summary: Synchrony Financial announced that Walmart Inc. has agreed to dismiss a lawsuit against the bank, which alleged that Synchrony breached the terms of their credit-card deal. Walmart had sought at least $800 million in damages. This development follows Walmart's decision last year to replace Synchrony as its exclusive credit-card issuer with Capital One Financial Corp.

title: JPMorgan spinoff Kadena puts blockchain on AWS—and on the table for small and medium-sized businesses
summary: Kadena, a JPMorgan spinoff, is making blockchain technology accessible to small and medium-sized businesses by moving its development platform to Amazon Web Services (AWS), aiming to reduce development costs. This move allows companies, including those in healthcare, to experiment with and implement rudimentary blockchain solutions with ease. The company hopes to democratize blockchain access, moving beyond the current landscape where adoption has been primarily by larger firms due to high development costs.

title: Amazon Stock Rises as the 'Scout' Delivery Robot Is Unveiled
summary: Amazon announced the launch of its new delivery robot, "Scout," a cooler-sized ground unit designed for autonomous package delivery, initially accompanied by an Amazon employee. This announcement led to a 0.91 percent rise in Amazon's stock prices. The article also mentions other strong performers in the Entrepreneur Index™, including NVIDIA Corp. and Analog Devices, while J.M. Smucker Company, OReilly Auto Parts, and Brown-Forman Corp saw declines.

title: REIT Warehouse Logistics Being Redefined by Prologis
summary: Prologis, a leading logistics REIT, is redefining warehouse logistics by developing multi-story distribution centers in urban areas to meet the rising demand for faster e-commerce delivery. Their "Georgetown Crossroads" project in Seattle, the first U.S. multi-story warehouse serviceable by tractor-trailer trucks, highlights a strategy to densify sites in land-constrained metropolitan areas. This approach addresses the need to be closer to consumers and overcomes the limitations of traditional single-story warehouses on city outskirts, though it involves higher land acquisition and construction costs.

title: Why You Should Include ETFs in Your Portfolio
summary: ETFs offer a convenient and easy way to diversify a portfolio, combining features of individual stocks and mutual funds. They allow investors to participate in entire sectors, avoid single stock risk, and benefit from lower fees and greater tax efficiency compared to traditional mutual funds. The article also covers how to choose and purchase ETFs, as well as several investing strategies.

title: Caterpillar, Nvidia Warnings Send Wall Street Tumbling
summary: U.S. stocks tumbled following warnings from Caterpillar and Nvidia, which highlighted concerns about a slowing Chinese economy and the impact of tariffs on corporate profits. Caterpillar missed profit estimates due to softening demand in China and rising costs, while Nvidia cut its revenue forecast due to weak demand and lower data center sales. This sent major indexes like the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite lower, despite overall positive earnings reports.

title: What’s Changed: 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Management Solutions for Analytics
summary: This article reviews the 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Management Solutions for Analytics (DMSA), highlighting key changes since the previous report. It discusses shifts in vendor positions, new entrants, and removals, focusing on the evolution of major players like Oracle, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, SAP, Teradata, IBM, Snowflake, Google, and MarkLogic. The article also touches upon the general trends in DMSA, emphasizing the growing importance of cloud and the diverse approaches taken by niche and leading providers.

title: FedEx Introduces Way for Retailers to Outrace Amazon in Delivery
summary: FedEx has introduced a new late-night shipping option for retailers, allowing them to offer next-day delivery for online orders placed as late as midnight. This initiative aims to help retailers compete with Amazon's fast delivery services, with FedEx emphasizing its growth strategy outside of its business with Amazon. The company sees potential in helping other businesses reduce delivery times and expects a significant increase in U.S. package volume by 2025.

title: Fidelity’s Steve Buller Built a Career on Actively Outperforming
summary: This article features an interview with Steve Buller, a long-serving portfolio manager at Fidelity Investments, discussing his two decades managing the Fidelity Real Estate Investment Portfolio Fund. Buller reflects on the fund's outperformance, the challenges of REIT acceptance, and how major market events have shaped his investment style. He also shares his insights on trending sectors, the impact of international sell-offs, and the future of fund management in a changing technological and financial landscape.

title: Activist Investors Urge eBay To Separate StubHub And Classifieds Businesses
summary: Activist investor Elliott Management Corporation is urging eBay to restructure by separating its StubHub and Classifieds businesses from its core Marketplace platform to unlock shareholder value. The proposal, supported by another hedge fund, Starboard Value LP, suggests this move, along with cost-cutting and increased share repurchases, could significantly boost eBay's stock performance. This push follows the successful PayPal spin-off in 2015, which was also championed by an activist investor.

title: Why Advanced Micro Devices might be important for service providers
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is becoming increasingly important for service providers due to its high-performance server processors like Epyc, which are crucial for hyperscale cloud players and data center updates. The company reported strong financial results in 2018, with significant growth in its data center business, and expects further adoption with its upcoming "Rome" processor, which offers improved performance and socket compatibility. As operators like AT&T, Sprint, and Comcast transform their networks with generic hardware, AMD's server technology is poised to play a key role in their data center evolution.

title: Plano's Tyler Technologies picks up big-name clients like NASA, Justice Department with latest acquisition
summary: Tyler Technologies announced its acquisition of MicroPact for approximately $185 million, adding major federal clients like NASA and the Department of Justice to its roster. This acquisition significantly expands Tyler Technologies' presence in the federal government sector, which previously constituted less than 1% of its business. The deal also brings new software products and insights from MicroPact's partner-driven business model to Tyler Technologies.

title: WeWork signs a deal for 11 floors in State Street’s longtime home
summary: WeWork has signed its largest Boston lease yet, taking 11 floors at One Lincoln Street, formerly State Street Corp.'s long-time home. This expansion will add 4,000 desks and bring WeWork's total Boston-area footprint to 1.1 million square feet, making it a major player in the local office market. However, questions remain about the sustainability of its rapid growth, especially given its reported losses and the potential impact of a future recession.

title: Amazon reports record-breaking holiday sales and earnings, but investors aren’t impressed
summary: Amazon reported record-breaking holiday sales and earnings for its fourth quarter, exceeding analyst expectations with $3 billion in profit and $72.4 billion in revenue. Despite these strong results, the company's stock declined due to a forecast of slowing growth and anticipated increased spending amid HQ2 expansion. This marks the second consecutive holiday quarter Amazon beat estimates, a feat not achieved since 2009.

title: Starbucks executive Rosalind Brewer joins Amazon board (Video)
summary: Rosalind Brewer, a Starbucks executive and 2018 PSBJ Women of Influence honoree, has joined Amazon's board. This appointment follows past criticism of Amazon, including from shareholder Rev. Jesse Jackson, regarding the lack of diversity on its executive team and board.

title: Amazon’s Long Island City HQ will send Altice USA packing
summary: Amazon's planned takeover of Savanna's One Court Square in Long Island City is forcing broadband giant Altice USA to relocate. Altice USA will move from One Court Square to The Paragon, a nearby converted warehouse, filling its entire 130,000 square feet. This move highlights the immediate impact of Amazon's presence on the Long Island City office and residential markets.

title: Amazon names Starbucks executive Rosalind Brewer to its board
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has appointed Rosalind Brewer, Starbucks Corp's Chief Operating Officer, to its board of directors, making her the first black director of the e-commerce giant. This appointment follows Amazon's commitment last year to increase diversity on its board. Brewer also joins Amazon's leadership development and compensation committee.

title: Could a proposed casino revive the York Galleria Mall?
summary: A proposed mini-casino by Penn National at the York Galleria Mall's former Sears site is hoped to revive the struggling mall, which has lost $30 million in assessed value over 20 years. The casino is expected to draw new interest, potentially attracting other businesses and generating up to $1 million annually for Springettsbury Township. This development aligns with a broader trend of malls redefining their roles as mixed-use hubs beyond traditional retail, adapting to societal changes and online shopping.

title: Grocery Wholesaler UNFI Reorganizes Pacific Northwest Distribution Network
summary: UNFI (United Natural Foods Inc.) is reorganizing its Pacific Northwest distribution network to improve synergies following its acquisition of Supervalu. The company plans to build a new 1.2 million-square-foot facility in Centralia, Wash., and expand a current Ridgefield, Wash., facility to 800,000 square feet, which will lead to the closure of three existing distribution centers. This optimization aims to enhance inventory management, logistics, and achieve synergy goals related to the Supervalu acquisition.

title: Amazon Eases Into Self-Driving Tech By Joining Aurora's $530 Million Funding Surge
summary: Aurora, a self-driving technology startup founded by leading researchers, secured over $530 million in Series B funding, with Amazon making a significant investment. The company aims to develop autonomous vehicle technology for other manufacturers rather than building its own fleet. This substantial funding injection underscores the capital-intensive nature of autonomous driving development and Amazon's interest in logistics and goods movement.

title: Scientists’ discovery could mean less-expensive smartphones, TVs
summary: USC chemists have developed a new copper-based compound that could replace rare and expensive iridium in smartphone and TV screens, potentially leading to cheaper devices without compromising visual quality. This discovery addresses the scarcity of iridium and solves the long-standing problem of short lifetimes for blue light emission in OLED technology. The new rigid copper compound exhibits efficient light emission comparable to iridium, opening new possibilities for display technology and energy-efficient lighting.

title: A Storm Is Coming to the Global Music Industry — and More than $100 Billion Is at Stake
summary: Vivendi is selling up to 50% of Universal Music Group, and its projected astronomical valuation could significantly impact the valuations of rivals Sony Music and Warner Music Group. Analysts from Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Exane BNP Paribas have provided valuations for UMG ranging from $29 billion to $42 billion, with a "bull case" scenario for Morgan Stanley suggesting even higher figures based on streaming growth. This potential Universal Music Group supersale could lead to a combined valuation for the "big three" music companies exceeding $100 billion, driven by intense market demand and optimistic streaming forecasts.

title: Opinion: Amazon should buy Netflix — and 9 other mergers we’d love to see
summary: Despite rising interest rates and market volatility, 2019 is expected to continue the trend of large-scale mergers and acquisitions, following five consecutive years of M&A activity exceeding $3 trillion. The article suggests several potential "mega-deals" that could occur, highlighting that corporate America remains undeterred in pursuing significant transactions. Examples given from 2018 include Cigna Corp.'s $54 billion purchase of Express Scripts and the pending $26 billion merger between Sprint Corp. and T-Mobile US.

title: Ryder System opens facilities due to e-commerce offering
summary: Ryder System has launched a new e-commerce fulfillment offering for manufacturers that conduct business online. This initiative includes opening two new multi-client facilities in California and Texas and expanding an existing warehouse in Pennsylvania, all expected to be fully operational by May. The service provides an alternative to third-party marketplaces, facilitating direct-to-consumer order fulfillment and demonstrating significant volume growth and shipping accuracy.

title: Google selects Equinix for submarine cable landing station in LA
summary: Google has chosen Equinix's LA4 data center as the landing point for its upcoming Curie submarine cable, which will connect the US with Chile. This marks the first direct submarine link between the two countries in 20 years. The cable, named after Marie Skłodowska Curie, will stretch over 10,000 km and aims to meet the increasing demand for high-capacity, low-latency global connectivity.

title: Ryder drives into Amazon Marketplace turf
summary: Ryder System Inc. is launching an e-commerce fulfillment solution to compete with platforms like Amazon, offering manufacturers direct control over their product fulfillment. The solution includes new multi-client facilities in California and Texas, and an expanded one in Pennsylvania, all slated to be operational by May. Ryder's initiative aims to provide manufacturers with greater control over inventory, pricing, and customer service while maintaining speed to market.

title: Alphabet Dethrones Amazon As Top U.S. Internet Company: Citi Report
summary: Citigroup has re-ranked Alphabet as the top U.S. internet company, surpassing Amazon, due to its strong growth in mobile search and YouTube, stock buybacks, and high valuation. Amazon's downgrade to fourth place is attributed to slower growth, regulatory challenges in India, and distractions from its HQ2 plans and CEO's personal issues. This re-ranking coincides with Google Cloud's aggressive investment in its sales division and increased competition with Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure.

title: FedEx Names Raj Subramaniam New President, COO
summary: FedEx Corp. has named Raj Subramaniam as its new president and chief operating officer, succeeding David Bronczek who is retiring. Subramaniam, who previously served as president and CEO of FedEx Express, will also become co-president and co-CEO of FedEx Services. His new role will commence on March 1, 2019, according to FedEx.

title: Walmart on a roll
summary: Walmart is experiencing strong growth, marked by a $1.7 million remodeling project at its Pueblo superstore and impressive holiday sales nationwide. The company reported its strongest holiday quarter in years, with a 4.2% jump in same-store sales and a 43% increase in e-commerce sales, signaling its growing competitiveness against online giants like Amazon. Walmart's success is attributed to a robust economy, strategic investments in store upgrades and employee wages, and an expanding online presence.

title: Walmart flexes in the fourth quarter, beats all expectations
summary: Walmart significantly exceeded Wall Street's expectations for its fiscal fourth quarter profits and sales, driven by strong e-commerce growth and robust performance across various product categories. This positive report defied a gloomy December government retail sales report, indicating that Walmart's strategic investments in online services and grocery pickup are widening its competitive advantage. The company's strong results suggest that consumers are benefiting from a stronger economy, enabling Walmart to attract a broader demographic and pose a more serious threat to Amazon in the online retail space.

title: Amazon.com, Inc. | Case Study
summary: This case study from MIT Sloan examines Amazon.com, Inc.'s financial strategy and growth over its first 20 years since its IPO. It highlights Amazon's focus on investing in expansion and R&D at the expense of short-term accounting earnings, aiming for long-term value creation. The study also discusses Amazon's use of cash flow performance measures in its non-GAAP disclosures and asks students to consider pathways to higher profitability.

title: Tilray to acquire Manitoba Harvest
summary: Tilray has acquired FHF Holdings, the parent company of hemp-based food company Manitoba Harvest, from Compass Group Diversified Holdings. This acquisition expands Tilray's product portfolio into natural foods and provides access to Manitoba Harvest's manufacturing facilities and retail network. Manitoba Harvest plans to launch CBD products this summer in legal US markets and later in Canada once edibles are legal, leveraging Tilray's expertise with cannabinoids.

title: Amazon.com 'Insourcing' Roils Freight Industry, Analysts Say
summary: Amazon's increasing "insourcing" of its freight operations is causing significant disruption in the trucking and logistics industry, leading to the bankruptcy of New England Motor Freight and a substantial revenue loss for XPO Logistics. Industry analysts and former Amazon employees suggest that Amazon aims to become a dominant third-party logistics (3PL) provider by handling more of its shipping needs internally. This strategy forces other carriers to re-evaluate their business models and prepares them for intensified competition.

title: Kemp 360 Vision analyzes F5, Nginx data
summary: Kemp Technologies has updated its 360 Vision predictive analytics service to include data from F5 Networks and Nginx load balancers, allowing for multivendor ADC ecosystem management. This SaaS application identifies potential problems and suggests remediation steps, with upcoming support for KVM, AWS, and Microsoft Azure. The update also adds automated load balancer deployment to Kemp 360 Central.

title: Former PepsiCo CEO Indra Nooyi Joins Amazon’s Board
summary: Former PepsiCo CEO Indra Nooyi has been elected to Amazon.com Inc.'s board of directors, joining its audit committee. Her appointment brings Amazon's board to 11 members, continuing a refresh of the panel. This marks the second new board appointee for Amazon this month.

title: Amazon adds former PepsiCo CEO Indra Nooyi to board
summary: Amazon.com Inc has appointed former PepsiCo Inc CEO Indra Nooyi to its board of directors, making her the second woman added to the board this month. Nooyi's appointment increases the number of women on Amazon's eleven-member board to five, aligning with the company's new policy to increase diversity. She will be part of the audit committee and has been granted 549 shares of common stock.

title: Indra Nooyi, former CEO of Pepsico, appointed to Amazon's board of directors
summary: Former PepsiCo CEO Indra Nooyi was appointed to Amazon's board of directors and its audit committee on February 25, 2019. This appointment follows her extensive career at PepsiCo, where she served as CEO and chairman. In connection with her election, Ms. Nooyi received a restricted stock unit award of 549 shares of Amazon common stock.

title: Target rips a page from Walmart, Amazon, welcoming outside sellers to website
summary: Target is launching Target+, an invite-only marketplace that will allow third-party sellers to offer a curated selection of products on its website, similar to Walmart and Amazon. This move aims to expand Target's online assortment while maintaining quality control by selectively inviting sellers. Shoppers using Target+ can still benefit from Red Card discounts, free shipping, and in-store returns for purchased items.

title: Target taking aim at Victoria's Secret with new lingerie brands
summary: Target is launching three new lingerie brands—Auden, Colsie, and Stars Above—to compete in the $12 billion lingerie market. This move directly targets Victoria's Secret by offering a more inclusive approach with diverse sizing and body-positive marketing, replacing its older Gilligan & O'Malley line. The new lines emphasize comfort and cater to a broad demographic, with all bras priced under $22.

title: The Value Chain Constraint
summary: This article analyzes how companies like Amazon, Walmart, Google, and Microsoft succeed or struggle based on their integration within specific value chains, rather than solely on technological innovation. It argues that sustainable differentiation comes from effectively integrating different component pieces of a value chain, and that straying too far from this core integration can lead even large tech companies to struggle in new markets despite massive resources. The author uses examples like Amazon's grocery struggles, Google Cloud's challenges, and Microsoft's enterprise success to illustrate the concept, and Netflix's transformation as an exception that proves the rule.

title: Icee to bring 200-plus jobs, headquarters to La Vergne
summary: Icee, the national frozen beverage company, is moving its corporate headquarters from California to La Vergne, Tennessee, creating over 200 new jobs with an average annual pay of $60,152. This $10.3 million investment includes a new 85,000-square-foot office and distribution center, supported by a seven-year property tax break valued at $690,275 from the Rutherford County Industrial Development Board. The company's decision was influenced by La Vergne's central location, business-friendly environment, and strong workforce development.

title: How Netflix created a $1 billion arms race for TV writers
summary: Netflix has instigated a highly competitive environment for TV writers and showrunners, signing major deals worth hundreds of millions of dollars with creators like Shonda Rhimes, Ryan Murphy, and Kenya Barris. This "arms race" is driven by streaming companies building original content libraries and traditional studios consolidating, leading to immense value placed on showrunners who can create intellectual property. The article explores the motivations behind these mega-deals, their structure (often including upfront payments in lieu of residuals), and the implications for both creators and the broader entertainment industry.

title: Etsy to offset carbon emissions from shipping its products
summary: Etsy announced its plan to offset carbon emissions from shipping products sold on its platform, starting with covering all U.S. e-commerce shipping emissions for one day. The company will purchase carbon offsets for ongoing shipping, focusing on projects like wind power and forest protection. This initiative aims to address the 98% of Etsy's total emissions that come from product shipping, despite Etsy not actively managing the shipping process itself.

title: JBG Smith reveals details on executive pay, Amazon bonuses
summary: JBG Smith CEO Matt Kelly received $11.3 million in total compensation in 2018, including a significant equity award of $6.6 billion. This substantial bonus was awarded for his pivotal role in securing Amazon.com Inc.'s second headquarters in Northern Virginia. The article also mentions that winning Amazon's HQ2 meant big bonuses for executives.

title: Alicia Boler-Davis Out, Gerald Johnson In As General Motors Exec VP Of Global Manufacturing
summary: General Motors has appointed Gerald Johnson as the new Executive Vice President of Global Manufacturing, effective April 1. Johnson replaces Alicia Boler-Davis, who is leaving the company to pursue other opportunities after 25 years of service. Mary Barra, GM Chairman and CEO, highlighted Johnson's strong leadership and experience as integral to the company's transformation and future mobility efforts.

title: Amazon to Launch New Grocery-Store Business
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is reportedly planning to open dozens of new grocery stores in major U.S. cities, expanding its presence in the food business beyond Whole Foods. The first store is anticipated to open in Los Angeles by the end of the year, with at least two more planned for early next year. This new chain will be distinct from the company's existing Whole Foods unit, indicating a diversified approach to the grocery market.

title: Verizon Acquires ProtectWise for Network Detection and Response Services -
summary: Verizon Communications has acquired ProtectWise, a provider of cloud-based Network Detection and Response (NDR) cybersecurity services. ProtectWise, founded in 2013, had raised roughly $67 million and was known for its partner-centric strategy. This acquisition enhances Verizon's ability to detect and respond to security threats, particularly as it expands its 5G footprint.

title: Mist Systems joins Juniper Networks
summary: Mist Systems has been acquired by Juniper Networks for over $400M, marking a significant milestone for the company and its founders, Sujai Hajela, Bob Friday, and Brett Galloway. Lightspeed Venture Partners, an early investor, highlights Mist Systems' revolutionary AI-driven wireless networking technology, which powers major enterprises. This acquisition is seen as a validation of Mist Systems' vision to disrupt the networking industry with its "AI for IT" solutions.

title: Tech Moves: Leafly hires Amazon Prime Video vet as CEO; Former F5 CEO joins ExtraHop Board
summary: Leafly, a marijuana review and discovery platform, has appointed Tim Leslie, former VP of Amazon Prime Video International, as its new CEO. Additionally, John McAdam, former CEO of F5 Networks, has joined the board of directors of hybrid cloud security startup ExtraHop. These moves highlight significant leadership changes in the Pacific Northwest tech community.

title: Forbes' billionaires list includes 20 from Michigan
summary: Forbes' annual list of the world's richest people includes 20 individuals with ties to Michigan, ten of whom currently reside in the state. The article highlights each Michigan-connected billionaire, detailing their net worth, global ranking, and their connection to the Great Lakes State. Notable figures include Larry Page, Steve Ballmer, and various business leaders from prominent Michigan companies like Meijer, Quicken Loans, and Stryker Corp.

title: HEINZ Debuts Two A-MAYO-ZING Condiments to Satisfy Saucy Fans
summary: HEINZ is launching two new condiment mashups, MAYOCUE (mayonnaise and barbecue sauce) and MAYOMUST (mayonnaise and mustard), following the success of MAYOCHUP. These new sauces aim to provide convenient and pre-mixed flavor combinations for consumers. The 16.5oz bottles will retail for $3.49 and will be available at major retailers and online.

title: Donald A. Brown, co-founder of The JBG Cos., dies
summary: Donald A. Brown, co-founder of The JBG Companies, has died at the age of 90. He was instrumental in launching the precursor to JBG Smith Properties, a company now known as Amazon.com Inc.'s landlord and development partner. The article reflects on his legacy and the transformation of JBG into a major real estate player.

title: Family Dollar was once considered “Amazon-proof.” Now it’s closing hundreds of stores.
summary: Dollar Tree, the parent company of budget stores Dollar Tree and Family Dollar, announced the closure of 390 Family Dollar stores in 2019 following attempts to revamp the brand, signaling the difficulty of turning around struggling retail in today's landscape. The closures highlight the challenges brick-and-mortar stores face against online competitors like Amazon and aggressive pricing from Walmart, even for discount retailers once thought to be "Amazon-proof." Despite a $2.3 billion loss linked to the closures, Dollar Tree plans renovations and new product introductions to stay competitive, as rivals like Amazon and Walmart expand into budget-friendly categories.

title: Costco builds 'fulfillment automation center' to expand e-commerce
summary: Costco has opened a "fulfillment automation center" to enhance its e-commerce capabilities, signaling increased investment in its online business. This move comes despite previous statements from its CFO expressing a preference for in-store shopping. The new center aims to support the company's expanding digital presence.

title: Salesforce at 20 offers lessons for startup success
summary: Salesforce celebrated its 20th anniversary, marking its evolution from a nascent startup challenging CRM giants to a SaaS powerhouse with an annual run rate exceeding $14 billion. The article delves into its origins in a San Francisco apartment, its growth through pioneering cloud software, and the visionary leadership of Marc Benioff and his team. Key lessons for startups include the importance of long-term vision, building trust, strong company culture, and strategic growth through acquisitions.

title: Costco Raises Minimum Wage to $15 an Hour
summary: Costco Wholesale is increasing its minimum wage for store workers to $15 an hour, marking the second such increase in less than a year. This announcement followed the company reporting higher than anticipated second-quarter financial earnings with significant increases in net sales and income. The move is part of a trend among retail giants like Target and Amazon to offer better wages and benefits to attract skilled workers.

title: C.H. Robinson CEO John Wiehoff Takes Work And Play Seriously
summary: John Wiehoff, CEO of C.H. Robinson, believes a "work hard, play hard" mentality is crucial for both personal success and building a strong company culture. During his 17-year tenure as CEO, C.H. Robinson's stock price increased nearly sixfold and revenue grew significantly, a testament to his leadership and focus on long-term vision and a sustainable culture. Wiehoff, who is retiring from his CEO role, emphasizes integrity, leadership, and a commitment to employees, customers, and a broad network of mentors.

title: Nvidia acquires Mellanox against growing AI, data competition
summary: Nvidia has acquired Mellanox Technologies Ltd. for $6.9 billion to strengthen its position in the rapidly growing and competitive market for AI and data-intensive computing platforms. This merger aims to bolster their combined capabilities against new rivals like Amazon and Cray, as both companies already have a significant presence in high-performance computing (HPC) with their integrated technologies. The acquisition is seen as a strategic move to address increasing competitive challenges in the HPC market.

title: F5 Networks paying $670M to acquire NGINX, a web server that runs a big chunk of the internet
summary: F5 Networks is acquiring NGINX, a popular web server, for $670 million. This acquisition aims to transition F5 from a hardware company to one focused on software and services for application infrastructure, bridging app development and security across various cloud environments. NGINX will retain its brand and open-source strategy, with its leadership joining F5.

title: F5 Networks Acquires NGINX For $670 Million
summary: F5 Networks has acquired NGINX, a popular open-source web server company, for approximately $670 million. This acquisition aims to strengthen F5's growth trajectory by accelerating its software and multi-cloud transformation, bridging NetOps and DevOps with consistent application services. NGINX will maintain its brand and leadership, leveraging F5's global sales and channel infrastructure.

title: Goodbye Growing Pains: Hanes’ New Babywear Delivers Comfort and Innovation for Baby, Convenience and Savings for Parents
summary: Hanes, America's No. 1 apparel brand, has launched its new Ultimate Baby line, including Flexy and Zippin collections, delivering comfort and innovation for babies and convenience and savings for parents. These collections feature adjustable cuffs, flexible fabrics, expandable necks, and protective zip covers, designed to grow with babies for their first 24 months, simplifying sizing to four categories. Available exclusively on Amazon, the line aims to address common parental challenges like outgrown clothing and difficult outfit changes, leveraging HanesBrands' "Innovate to Elevate" process.

title: Omada Health adds connected blood pressure and blood sugar monitors to platform
summary: Omada Health has introduced FDA-cleared and cellular-connected blood pressure cuffs and glucometers to its platform, allowing users to upload real-time vital readings for better health advice from coaches. These new devices, which also include free test strips for glucometers, are part of programs launched last year to support the treatment of patients with hypertension and Type 2 diabetes. This move aims to streamline the user experience, building on Omada’s existing connected scale for diabetes prevention and competing with companies like Livongo.

title: From Bentonville to Seoul, Jay Jorgensen Becomes General Counsel of South Korea's Coupang
summary: Jay Jorgensen, former executive vice president and global chief ethics and compliance officer of Walmart Inc., has been appointed as the new general counsel for Coupang, South Korea's largest and fastest-growing e-commerce company. This move brings Jorgensen's extensive experience in retail and compliance, including building a world-class program at Walmart, to the rapidly expanding South Korean e-commerce giant. Coupang, often referred to as the "Amazon of South Korea," is reportedly eyeing an initial public stock offering in 2019 or 2020.

title: Top gamer 'Ninja' made $1 million to promote EA's 'Apex Legends' launch - source
summary: Top gamer Tyler Blevins, known as "Ninja," was reportedly paid $1 million by Electronic Arts Inc. to promote the launch of their new game "Apex Legends." This significant payment highlights the intense competition in the battle royale genre and the growing influence of professional gamers in promotional strategies, with EA's stock price and market value rising significantly after the game's launch. The game amassed 10 million sign-ups in three days and 50 million users within a month, demonstrating the success of this influencer-based marketing approach.

title: Your U.S. Equity Fund Is More Global Than You Think
summary: This article examines how U.S. equity funds are more globally exposed than commonly perceived by analyzing revenue streams by region. Morningstar's new proprietary data reveals that many popular U.S. index-tracking ETFs have significant revenue exposure outside the United States, particularly in emerging Asian markets and the eurozone. The analysis highlights that relying on a company's headquarters or stock listing alone provides a flawed picture of a fund's true geographic allocation.

title: If you’re tracking the S&P 500 instead of this fund, you’re leaving money on the table
summary: This article suggests that investors tracking the S&P 500 might be missing out on better returns by overlooking the Invesco QQQ Trust. It highlights the Invesco QQQ Trust as a successful and diversified fund. The piece also addresses concerns about tech stock valuations, noting they are lower than before the dot-com bubble burst.

title: Former Toys R Us Headquarters In Wayne Sold
summary: The former 191-acre Toys R Us headquarters in Wayne, New Jersey, has been sold, with the new, unnamed buyer planning to enhance the site for multiple uses. The campus previously housed the toy company's headquarters for 16 years. This sale follows Toys R Us's Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing in March 2018, which led to the closure of all its U.S. stores.

title: Argentinian Company Wants to Build the Amazon of Latin America
summary: MercadoLibre Inc., an Argentinian e-commerce company, is striving to become the "Amazon of Latin America." To achieve this, it is investing $2 billion in logistics and payments infrastructure to serve a market where many customers lack traditional banking access. The company aims to strengthen its regional foothold and defend against competition from e-commerce giants Amazon and Alibaba.

title: Netflix is valued like a tech company, but its CEO just said it was a media company
summary: Netflix CEO Reed Hastings stated that the company is a media company rather than a tech company, primarily due to its significant spending on content. This stance deviates from other major tech firms that prefer to label themselves as "platforms." Hastings' comments came in response to questions about regulating tech companies, potentially allowing Netflix to avoid some scrutiny faced by its peers.

title: Why Now Might Be a Good Time to Buy QQQ
summary: This article discusses reasons why the Invesco QQQ ETF could be a good investment. It highlights QQQ's focus on large-cap growth, particularly in technology and related sectors, its strong historical performance relative to the S&P 500, and its high liquidity. The article also touches on potential risks like sector concentration and higher volatility compared to broader market indices.

title: How Netflix plans on owning your kids’ screen time
summary: Netflix is heavily investing in children's animation, spending an estimated $1.1 billion this year, to appeal to its broad global subscriber base and fend off competition. Unlike traditional studios, Netflix aims for a diverse range of content without a singular "brand" to cater to every household member's viewing preferences. The company is encouraging creators to pursue unique visions and is experimenting with new interactive features to engage young viewers.

title: Walmart is beating Amazon in a business worth $35B
summary: Walmart and other traditional retailers are significantly outperforming Amazon in the rapidly growing click-and-collect business, which is estimated to reach $35 billion in sales in the U.S. by 2020. Walmart's grocery pickup program is a major contributor to its U.S. comparable sales growth, while Amazon's efforts in this hybrid online and physical shopping model are described as tentative and lacking a cohesive strategy. The article suggests that Amazon's delayed entry into robust click-and-collect services could lead to lost customer loyalty to competitors and warns that pickup service may be a lasting consumer preference, especially in suburbs.

title: Walgreens Trims Its Fiscal Year Forecast After a Challenging Quarter
summary: Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc. reduced its earnings outlook for the fiscal year after a difficult second quarter, missing Wall Street estimates for both earnings per share and revenue. The company cited pressure from insurers, a weak cold and flu season, and declining tobacco sales for the profit drop. CEO Stefano Pessina vowed a quick response to address these challenges and return to growth, while also acknowledging increased competition from Amazon.

title: Walgreens sees Kroger partnership as a way forward
summary: Walgreens plans to lean on its partnership with Kroger and private label health and beauty offerings to strengthen its business following disappointing Q2 results. The company aims to accelerate digitalization, transform retail offerings, modernize pharmacy, and implement a cost management program. While the Kroger partnership currently involves a small fraction of Walgreens locations, an expanded collaboration could boost grocery capabilities and revenue for both companies.

title: CVS spreads same-day prescription deliveries to 36 states
summary: CVS Health is expanding its same-day prescription delivery service nationwide, covering 36 states and Washington D.C., from 6,000 locations. This move is part of drugstores' efforts to compete with online retailers like Amazon and cater to customers who prefer online shopping and home delivery. The service, costing about $8, also allows for the delivery of other health and baby products, with orders placed through the company's app, text, or phone call, and delivered by Shipt.

title: WWD: Retailer of the Year
summary: American Eagle Outfitters Inc. Executive Chairman and CEO Jay Schottenstein discusses the company's success in navigating the evolving retail landscape, emphasizing its ability to thrive in both brick-and-mortar and e-commerce eras. The article highlights American Eagle's 16 consecutive quarters of comparable sales gains, particularly Aerie's double-digit increases, and its recognition as the American Apparel and Footwear Association’s Retailer of the Year. Schottenstein attributes this success to technological investment, deep customer understanding through analytics, and Aerie's authentic approach to body positivity.

title: CVS to offer same-day prescription delivery via Target-owned Shipt
summary: CVS Health is expanding its same-day prescription delivery service nationwide through a partnership with Target-owned Shipt. This marks Shipt's first entry into the pharmacy space, while CVS is broadening its delivery options beyond its existing one or two-day service. Customers can get same-day delivery for $7.99, or subscribe to Shipt for $99 annually for broader delivery services.

title: Qualcomm Announces New AI Chip for Cloud Data Center Servers
summary: Qualcomm Inc., a leader in smartphone technology, is entering the crowded market for AI chips used in cloud data centers. The company plans to leverage its mobile expertise and advanced manufacturing to deliver power-efficient products, aiming for a share of a market projected to reach $17 billion by 2025. This move positions Qualcomm to compete with established players like Intel, Nvidia, and cloud providers already developing AI components.

title: Stanley Black & Decker CEO: 'Things are going great with Craftsman'
summary: Stanley Black & Decker CEO James Loree claims that the Craftsman brand, acquired from Sears, is performing exceptionally well despite Sears' continued sale of its own Craftsman tools. Loree highlights improvements in product quality and expanded distribution through retailers like Lowe's and Amazon, anticipating significant revenue growth. The company is also in a legal dispute with Sears over the marketing and sale of competing Craftsman products.

title: Twice as many companies paying zero taxes under Trump tax plan
summary: A new analysis by the Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy (ITEP) reveals that 60 large U.S. companies paid no federal income taxes in 2018, more than double the average in previous years, despite earning billions in profits. This increase is largely attributed to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, which significantly lowered the corporate tax rate and introduced new tax breaks. Companies like Amazon, Netflix, Chevron, Eli Lilly, and Deere & Co. are among those that effectively paid zero taxes, leading to a substantial impact on the federal budget.

title: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos jabs eBay in shareholder letter over third-party sales
summary: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos criticized eBay in his annual shareholder letter, claiming Amazon's third-party sales growth has significantly outpaced eBay's due to superior seller tools. This led to a stock dip for eBay and a retort from its CEO, Devin Wenig, who highlighted eBay's focus on customers and lack of competition with its sellers. Bezos also challenged other retailers to match Amazon's $15 minimum wage, drawing a response from Walmart.

title: 2018 Letter to Shareholders
summary: Jeff Bezos's 2018 Letter to Shareholders details Amazon's remarkable growth, particularly highlighting the success of third-party sellers on the platform, which now account for 58% of physical gross merchandise sales. Bezos emphasizes Amazon's culture of invention, wandering, and customer obsession, citing examples like AWS, Amazon Go, and Alexa. The letter also addresses Amazon's focus on employee investment, including raising the minimum wage to $15 an hour and supporting education and veterans, while challenging other retailers to match their benefits.

title: Jumia Surges on U.S. Debut as Africa's Amazon Goes Public
summary: Jumia Technologies AG shares soared 75% on their first day of trading in New York, with investors eager to back the company's expansion of online shopping services across Africa. The stock traded at $25.46, valuing the company at over $1.9 billion, after Jumia raised $196 million through the sale of 13.5 million American depositary receipts. This successful debut signifies strong investor interest in "Africa's Amazon."

title: Publicis Buys Alliance Data’s Epsilon for $4.4 Billion in Cash
summary: Publicis Groupe SA is set to acquire Alliance Data Systems Corp.'s digital marketing firm Epsilon for $4.4 billion in cash, marking its largest takeover to date. This move aims to bolster Publicis's presence in the digital marketing sector amid a competitive landscape against tech giants and consulting firms. The acquisition is intended to be fully debt-financed, leading Publicis to suspend its share buyback program.

title: Ulta Beauty’s Canadian expansion plan adds more competition to crowded sector
summary: Ulta Beauty Inc. is planning to expand into Canada as early as late 2020 or early 2021, posing a significant challenge to existing beauty retailers like Hudson's Bay, Shoppers Drug Mart, and Sephora. The U.S. cosmetics giant aims to capitalize on Canada's lucrative beauty market through its distinctive model, which includes in-store salons and a wide range of products from both mass-market and prestige brands. This expansion could also benefit Canadian retail landlords by filling vacant spaces left by struggling merchants.

title: Del Monte Foods makes SAP ERP migration to AWS
summary: Del Monte Foods migrated its SAP ERP system to Amazon Web Services (AWS) to consolidate IT systems, reduce costs, and gain flexibility. This move, driven by prior acquisition challenges, allowed them to cut IT costs by about 35% without disrupting business processes. Analysts noted Del Monte is ahead of the curve in fully moving core ERP to the cloud, as many companies remain on-premises or in vendor-hosted environments.

title: Reliability at heart of Lyft and Uber’s tech, IPOs reveal
summary: This article examines the critical role of reliable technology for rideshare giants Lyft and Uber, as revealed in their IPO filings. It compares their cloud strategies, infrastructure, workforce, and cybersecurity approaches, highlighting how technological reliability underpins their operations and growth in competitive markets. Both companies emphasize data-driven insights and scalable platforms, while also navigating significant challenges like security breaches and regulatory complexities.

title: Best Buy CEO Hubert Joly is stepping down
summary: Hubert Joly, credited with turning around Best Buy Co. Inc., is stepping down as CEO this summer. Chief Financial Officer Corie Barry will succeed him in June. Joly's strategy included utilizing Best Buy's physical space by creating mini-showrooms for other companies, which helped the retailer compete with Amazon.

title: Cloud Computing: The Digital Infrastructure Powering Today's Businesses
summary: This article discusses how cloud computing has fundamentally transformed business IT, moving from on-premise infrastructure to remote, scalable services. It highlights the financial advantages, ease of management, flexibility, platform power, interoperability, and enablement of emerging technologies as key drivers of its growth. The article concludes that while cloud adoption is still relatively early, it is becoming a foundational tool for businesses of all sizes, with increasing spending and widespread implementation expected.

title: Logitech Harmony Express Brings Effortless Voice Control and Easy Navigation to Your Home Entertainment
summary: Logitech announced Harmony Express, a new universal voice remote with built-in Amazon Alexa, designed to simplify home entertainment control. Users can control TV, streaming apps, and smart home devices using voice commands. The remote also features a "remote finder" function through its mobile app or existing Alexa devices.

title: Why O'Reilly Automotive Stock Smashed the Market in 2018
summary: O'Reilly Automotive (ORLY) stock rose significantly in 2018, outperforming the market due to solid same-store-sales growth, a defensive market shift toward recession-resistant stocks, and an aging vehicle fleet. The article highlights that the auto-parts sector's strong performance also eased fears about competition from Amazon.com. Investors are now watching to see if these companies can meet expectations in 2019 after strong 2018 valuations.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper partners to deliver an Adrenaline Shoc to the energy drink category
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper has partnered with beverage entrepreneur Lance Collins to launch Adrenaline Shoc, a new energy drink targeted at the after-workout crowd. This sugar-free beverage, containing 300 mg of caffeine and natural energy boosters, aims to compete in the increasingly crowded energy drink market. Despite a slowdown in the category's growth rate, Keurig Dr Pepper hopes to differentiate Adrenaline Shoc with its "better-for-you" ingredients and premium pricing.

title: Netflix is opening a production hub in NYC
summary: Netflix is expanding its presence in New York City by opening a new production hub, which is expected to create hundreds of jobs and involve up to $100 million in investments. This move follows Amazon backing out of Long Island City and comes as Netflix faces increased competition from other streaming services like Disney, demonstrating its strategy to grow beyond Hollywood. The state of New York is offering Netflix up to $4 million in performance-based tax incentives for job creation.

title: Snap has three years to make a profit before it runs out of money
summary: Snap, once valued at $24 billion upon its 2017 IPO, has just over three years to become profitable before it runs out of cash, according to a Financial Times analysis. Despite a struggling stock price, executive exodus, and a disastrous app redesign, the company is attempting a turnaround by cutting costs and boosting user numbers. Snap faces intense competition from Facebook and needs to broaden its appeal beyond its young demographic to older users and expand its advertising base.

title: Amazon plans to shut down China marketplace in rare retreat
summary: Amazon plans to shut down its Chinese marketplace business in July, shifting its focus to offering mainland consumers overseas products rather than goods from local sellers. This retreat highlights the challenges American tech companies face in competing with strong local leaders like Alibaba and JD.com in China's retail market. While Amazon will maintain other business operations in China, this move signifies a strategic shift to focus on markets like India where it sees a better chance of becoming a dominant player.

title: Kohl's greatly expands partnership with Amazon and offers stock to digital giant
summary: Kohl's is significantly expanding its partnership with Amazon by accepting returns from Amazon customers at all 1,150+ Kohl's stores nationwide, causing Kohl's stock to jump nearly 12%. The department store chain has also granted Amazon the right to buy 1.7 million Kohl's shares, about 1% of outstanding shares. This move follows a successful pilot program in Chicago where Kohl's stores accepting Amazon returns saw an 8% revenue gain compared to 2% elsewhere.

title: Robots in the Permian? Climate concerns drive innovation
summary: Oil supermajors like Chevron and Exxon Mobil are heavily investing in the Permian Basin, using advanced automation, cloud computing, and AI to maximize oil extraction. This strategy is seen as a hedge against future climate change regulations and potential drops in oil demand, allowing for quick returns and flexibility. However, environmentalists criticize the focus on fossil fuels, and some experts question the feasibility of the desired automation and the long-term sustainability of shale production.

title: Ford to Invest $500 Million in Rivian, a Tesla Rival (Published 2019)
summary: Ford Motor has agreed to invest $500 million in Rivian, an electric-car start-up seen as a potential rival to Tesla. This partnership aims to accelerate Ford's electric vehicle development and streamline its operations, while Rivian prepares to launch its own electric pickup truck and SUV. The investment highlights the changing dynamics in the auto industry with newcomers gaining ground through technological advancements.

title: Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) earnings Q3 2019
summary: Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT) exceeded revenue and earnings estimates for Q3 2019, causing its shares to rise by 3% in aftermarket hours. The company reported strong growth across its segments, including Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing, driven by demand for cloud offerings and increased engagement in LinkedIn and Xbox Live. Microsoft's CFO highlighted that commercial cloud revenue reached $9.6 billion, marking a 41% year-over-year increase.

title: Variety, iHeartMedia Launch New Film Podcast ‘The Big Ticket’ With Marc Malkin
summary: Variety and iHeartMedia have launched a new weekly film-focused podcast called "The Big Ticket," hosted by Marc Malkin. The podcast will feature interviews with Hollywood stars and filmmakers, with its debut episodes focusing on "Avengers: Endgame" and upcoming guests including Halle Berry and Keanu Reeves. This partnership aims to expand the reach of Variety's journalism to wider audiences through iHeartMedia's platforms.

title: Deal of the Year: Amazon HQ2
summary: The article discusses the significant effort and collaboration involved in securing Amazon's HQ2 for Greater Washington. It highlights the Amazon deal as one of the largest ever for the region and includes related news about Amazon's real estate activities and development efforts by JBG Smith and Brookfield.

title: Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) earnings Q1 2019
summary: Amazon.com Inc. surpassed Q1 2019 earnings estimates, with revenues aligning with expectations. Net sales increased 17% year-over-year to $59.7 billion, and net income rose significantly to $3.6 billion. The company provided Q2 2019 sales and operating income guidance and announced expanded YouTube and Prime Video app availability on various devices.

title: Five fund buyers reveal their favourite tech ETFs
summary: This article compiles the favorite tech ETFs of five different fund buyers, highlighting various approaches to gaining tech exposure, including robotics and automation, pure-play sector exposure, and broad Nasdaq 100 coverage that includes FAANG stocks. Each fund buyer explains their rationale for choosing particular ETFs, considering factors like methodology, diversification, liquidity, and how well the ETF captures the evolving definition of "tech."

title: Off-White is Claiming Legal Rights in Quotation Marks and Red Zip Ties, and Suing Over Them
summary: Off-White is asserting exclusive common law trademark rights in its use of quotation marks and red zip ties on its products, and has initiated multiple lawsuits against companies, including Rastaclat, for unauthorized use. The brand's attempt to secure federal registration for the red zip tie has been preliminarily rejected by the USPTO due to concerns about similarity to existing trademarks, functionality, and lack of inherent distinctiveness. The article discusses the challenges Off-White faces in proving that these elements are source-identifying to consumers, rather than merely decorative.

title: Amazon to give Prime customers one-day shipping, cutting free delivery time in half
summary: Amazon.com Inc. plans to reduce its free delivery time for Prime subscribers from two days to one day. This change is expected to negatively impact profits in the second quarter as the company implements the new shipping model.

title: Chewy to fetch $1B in IPO
summary: Chewy.com, acquired by PetSmart, is preparing for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) that is expected to exceed $1 billion, significantly higher than initial estimates. The pet e-retailer will list under the ticker "CHWY" despite not yet being profitable, and PetSmart will retain control through Class B common stock. Analysts highlight Chewy's strong market share against Amazon and positive signs from its private label brands, despite the challenge of Amazon's expedited shipping.

title: HPE opens new headquarters in north San Jose
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise officially unveiled its new headquarters in north San Jose, bringing 1,300 workers to the America Center complex. San Jose Mayor Sam Liccardo lauded HPE's commitment to the community. The company also announced new corporate initiatives, including enhanced parental leave benefits and flexible work options, aiming to attract and retain top talent.

title: Kroger Co. beefs up bonuses for highest-paid bosses
summary: Kroger's top executives received significant compensation increases in 2018, primarily driven by larger cash bonuses tied to the company's "strong performance on adjusted earnings per share." CEO Rodney McMullen's total compensation rose 19 percent to $11.7 million, including a $2.7 million bonus. This occurred as Kroger adapted to increased competition and invested heavily in technology and store remodeling under its Restock Kroger initiative.

title: Cereal Killer: Kellogg’s Must Transform Its Company to Survive—Will It Succeed?
summary: This article analyzes Kellogg's need for significant transformation to survive and thrive amidst changing consumer preferences and declining U.S. cereal demand. It discusses CEO Steve Cahillane's "Deploy for Growth" strategy, recent divestitures and acquisitions, and proposes bold recommendations including divestment of most U.S. cereal brands, capabilities-driven M&A, and radical innovation in food production and delivery, emphasizing a shift from a "Day Two" to a "Day One" company culture.

title: Amazon Can't Duck Williams-Sonoma Suit Over Furniture Sales
summary: Amazon.com Inc. failed to dismiss a trademark infringement lawsuit filed by Williams-Sonoma. Williams-Sonoma alleges that Amazon's "Rivet" line includes products "strikingly similar" to its West Elm brand and that Amazon's website misleads customers into thinking it's an authorized reseller. A judge ruled that the trademark-infringement claims are a "close call," allowing the suit to proceed to determine if consumers are confused by Amazon's listings.

title: Target rebrands digital-advertising business as Roundel
summary: Target has rebranded its digital advertising business from Target Media Network to Roundel, signaling an aggressive push into the digital advertising sector. The company aims to leverage its customer data and "exceptional branding" to offer personalized ad campaigns for its 1,000 clients, including major brands like Disney and Coca-Cola. This move positions Target to compete more directly with other retailers like Amazon and Walmart, which have also seen success in their advertising businesses.

title: Major Carriers Strive to Automate Loading and Unloading Trucks
summary: Major carriers like FedEx and UPS are investing in automation to streamline the crucial but challenging process of loading and unloading trucks, particularly due to the varied nature of packages. Honeywell and Siemens AG have developed distinct solutions: Honeywell's mobile unit uses suction cups, while Siemens' system requires a permanent rolling belt in the trailer. These innovations aim to improve efficiency and employee satisfaction, though market availability dates are yet to be announced.

title: Robots edging closer to the key task of unloading trucks
summary: FedEx and UPS are investing in robots to automate truck unloading as e-commerce surges and Amazon expands its logistics. Companies like Honeywell and Siemens have developed machines that can unload trucks as fast as humans, mitigating the strenuous nature of the job. While unloading is closer to being solved, companies like Dorabot are also making progress on the more complex task of automating truck loading.

title: QEDIT Partners With Ant Financial, VMware, RGAX, Raises $10 Million
summary: QEDIT, a company specializing in privacy layers for enterprise blockchain networks, has announced partnerships with Ant Financial, VMware Inc., and RGAX. Simultaneously, QEDIT closed a $10 million Series A funding round led by MizMaa Ventures, with participation from its new partners and other investors. This funding will support the development of its privacy protocol and expand sales and partnerships, aiming to enhance data protection and efficiency in the finance and insurance industries.

title: Teamsters Call for XPO Logistics to Separate Board Chairman, CEO Roles
summary: The International Brotherhood of Teamsters is urging XPO Logistics to separate the roles of board chairman and CEO, advocating for an independent director to chair the board. This comes after XPO's stock plunged and the company lost significant business, leading the Teamsters to express concerns about concentrated power in one individual, current Chairman and CEO Bradley Jacobs. Two shareholder advisory firms, Glass Lewis & Co. and Institutional Shareholder Services, are supporting the Teamsters' resolution.

title: Synchronoss teams with Amazon to provide integration service to operators
summary: Synchronoss Technologies has partnered with Amazon to streamline the way mobile operators offer Amazon's services to their customers, integrated directly into carrier billing systems. Utilizing its Digital Experience Platform (DXP), Synchronoss will act as an integrator to make the process more efficient for both Amazon and global carriers. This collaboration aims to simplify customer journeys and accelerate the time to market for Amazon services through a carrier's existing infrastructure.

title: Former Humana employee pleads guilty to federal fraud charges
summary: A former Humana employee, Nitin More, pleaded guilty to federal fraud charges. The charges relate to More copying thousands of Amazon access codes that were intended for use as rewards in Humana's Go365 fitness program.

title: 20s Jonathan Morley
summary: Jonathan Morley, a lead software engineer at CME Group, is recognized for his contributions to emerging technologies including supporting the rollout of bitcoin futures.
