He is also noted for his passion for learning and teaching, having authored books on blockchain and Big Data, and for his leadership in establishing CME's employee networking group PRIDE. His ability to bridge technology and business perspectives, along with his community involvement, distinguishes him in his field.

title: Supermicro moves production from China
summary: Supermicro is reportedly moving its production facilities out of China due to lingering customer concerns about embedded spy chips in its motherboards, despite being cleared by investigations. This decision also serves to mitigate the impact of the U.S.-China trade war. The company is expanding manufacturing in Taiwan and California to increase self-reliance and meet customer demand.

title: QVC chief says ‘we’re living in a changing world’ as shares plunge on disappointing results
summary: Qurate Retail, Inc. (QRTEA) shares plunged nearly 27 percent after the company reported a disappointing 4 percent decrease in overall revenue for the first quarter, totaling about $3.1 billion. CEO Mike George attributed the decline to a changing retail and media landscape, including shifts in consumer shopping habits and the integration challenges of the HSN acquisition. An analyst noted that these market trends have been ongoing for years, questioning why their impact was more pronounced in the first quarter for Qurate's brands like QVC, HSN, Zulily, and Cornerstone Brands.

title: Supreme Court Deals Blow to Apple in Antitrust Case
summary: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that App Store customers have the standing to sue Apple for antitrust violations, rejecting Apple's argument that customers purchase apps from third-party developers directly. The decision allows a 2011 lawsuit alleging Apple drives up app prices through a 30 percent commission to proceed, potentially impacting other companies that operate as marketplaces. The ruling clarifies the "direct purchaser" principle under antitrust law but does not overturn the Illinois Brick doctrine.

title: Exploring the Republic Services of Southern Nevada Recycling Facility
summary: This article details a tour of the Republic Services of Southern Nevada recycling facility and learning center. It highlights the facility's operations, advanced technologies for sorting materials, educational challenges in an "immature recycling market," and its commitment to sustainability. The facility processes 2 million pounds of materials daily, separating commercial and residential streams and employing optical sorters and quality control measures.

title: Enabling digital success with APIs and Microservices
summary: This article discusses how APIs and microservices are crucial for digital success in modern organizations by enabling collaboration, innovation, and scalable, resilient systems. It highlights the challenges of legacy IT assets and provides an approach for successful API and microservices implementation based on five key pillars. The piece also explains the roles of APIs and microservices in driving better customer experiences and achieving zero-downtime service availability.

title: Disney to buy full control of Hulu from NBC owner Comcast
summary: Disney is taking full operational control of the streaming service Hulu from Comcast in a deal that values Hulu at $27.5 billion U.S. This move positions Disney to better compete with Netflix, especially as Disney prepares to launch its own streaming service, Disney+. The agreement allows Disney to acquire Comcast's remaining 33 percent stake after January 2024.

title: Dolby Appoints Anjali Sud to its Board of Directors
summary: Dolby Laboratories, Inc. announced the appointment of Anjali Sud, CEO of Vimeo, to its Board of Directors as a new independent director, effective May 13, 2019. Sud brings extensive knowledge of the technology industry and operational experience, filling a vacancy left by the passing of former director Nicholas Donatiello, Jr. Her background at Vimeo and Amazon.com is expected to greatly strengthen the Board.

title: Vanguard ESG U.S. Stock ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (BATS:ESGV)
summary: This article provides detailed information on the Vanguard ESG U.S. Stock ETF (ESGV), including its current price, key statistics, fund overview, expenses, and recent news headlines. It highlights ESGV's investment strategy, which focuses on U.S. all-cap companies screened for environmental, social, and corporate governance criteria, and lists its top holdings and sector exposure. The fund, managed by Vanguard, has assets under management of $11.58 billion and a net expense ratio of 0.09%.

title: NICE Acquires Brand Embassy
summary: NICE has acquired Brand Embassy, a Prague-based company specializing in omnichannel cloud-based customer service platforms. Brand Embassy's technology integrates social media, messaging, live chat, and AI-powered chatbots, serving approximately 80 customers including Telefonica O2 and Vodafone. This acquisition will enable NICE inContact to adopt a digital-first approach within its CXone platform, de-coupling voice from digital channels and creating new sales opportunities for enterprises looking to unify digital engagement solutions.

title: Stanley Black & Decker investing $90M to shift more Craftsman production back to US
summary: Stanley Black & Decker is investing $90 million to open a new 425,000-square-foot facility in Fort Worth, Texas, to bring more Craftsman production back to the U.S. This initiative aims to revitalize the iconic American brand and expand its manufacturing heritage, with the goal of reaching $1 billion in incremental revenues by 2021. The plant will employ about 500 full-time workers and incorporate advanced manufacturing technologies.

title: Microsoft, Sony partner on streaming games, chips and AI
summary: Microsoft and Sony have announced a strategic partnership where Sony will leverage Microsoft's cloud services, specifically Azure, for game and media streaming. The collaboration also extends to co-developing image sensors and integrating Microsoft's AI technology into Sony's consumer products. This deal aims to bolster Microsoft's cloud business and provide Sony's gaming platform with enhanced streaming capabilities, especially as its PlayStation 4 nears the end of its lifecycle.

title: JP Morgan buys health-care payments firm InstaMed in the bank's biggest acquisition since the financial crisis
summary: J.P. Morgan Chase is acquiring InstaMed, a healthcare payments technology firm, for over $500 million, making it the bank's largest acquisition since the financial crisis. This move aims to deepen J.P. Morgan's presence in the $3.5 trillion U.S. health-care spending market and underscores the bank's aggressive strategy in the evolving world of payments. InstaMed, founded in 2004, automates medical billing and processed $94 billion in transactions last year.

title: JPMorgan to buy healthcare payments technology firm InstaMed
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced its plan to acquire InstaMed, a U.S. healthcare payments technology firm, for over $500 million. This acquisition is part of JPMorgan's deeper dive into the $3.5 trillion healthcare market, aiming to expand its payment services for healthcare consumers, providers, and payers, and to leverage InstaMed's established network and platform to address inefficiencies in healthcare payments. The deal is expected to integrate JPMorgan’s payment infrastructure into InstaMed, potentially also leveraging the bank's healthcare venture, Haven, with Amazon and Berkshire Hathaway.

title: Cray, the Seattle-based supercomputer pioneer, sold to HPE for $1.3 billion
summary: Seattle-based supercomputer maker Cray has agreed to be acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) for $1.3 billion, or $35 per share, representing a 17.4% premium. This acquisition aims to combine Cray's supercomputing expertise and market position in academia and government with HPE's broader portfolio, bolstering HPE's capabilities in high-end computing and next-generation technology development, especially in the context of cloud computing and AI. The deal, which is subject to shareholder and regulatory approval, is intended to help Cray address challenges of scale and investment in its "exascale" systems roadmap, despite recent contract wins.

title: Walmart’s digital efforts paying off in battle with Amazon
summary: Walmart's first-quarter results indicate its digital efforts are successfully gaining e-commerce market share against competitor Amazon.com Inc. The company reported a 37% growth in e-commerce sales and an increased inventory to support fulfillment centers, as CEO Doug McMillon emphasized Walmart's evolution into "more of a digital enterprise." These strategic moves, including new online brands and improved customer interfaces, highlight Walmart's commitment to strengthening its online presence.

title: Colgate-Palmolive tops Gartner’s 2019 Supply Chain rankings
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has secured the top position in Gartner’s 2019 Supply Chain Top 25 rankings, moving up from fourth place in 2018 due to strong financial performance and focus on corporate social responsibility. Alibaba and Akzo Nobel also made their debut on the shortlist. Unilever joined the "Masters" category after consistently ranking in the top five for seven consecutive years, recognized for its advanced digital supply chain processes and use of emerging technologies.

title: Coca-Cola Will Revive New Coke in Alliance With Netflix, ‘Stranger Things’
summary: Coca-Cola is reviving New Coke for a limited time as part of a partnership with Netflix, integrating the infamous beverage into the third season of "Stranger Things," which is set in 1985. This marketing initiative aims to promote both the return of the series and gives Coca-Cola a unique way to connect with streaming audiences, despite New Coke's historical marketing failure. Coca-Cola will make 500,000 cans available online and in select locations, also releasing limited-edition original Coke with "Stranger Things" designs.

title: Lions Gate is still interested in selling Starz to CBS — then might have to merge with MGM to stay relevant
summary: Lions Gate is still interested in selling its premium entertainment network Starz to CBS, with talks expected to continue. If the Starz sale goes through, Lions Gate may consider a merger with MGM to gain scale and remain relevant as a standalone public company. The consolidation trend among smaller media companies is driven by competition from tech giants like Netflix and Amazon.

title: Baidu Tops China’s Smart Speaker Market and Enters Top 3 Globally in First Quarter
summary: Baidu, Inc. emerged as the top smart speaker vendor in China and a global top-three player in Q1 2019, according to Canalys and Strategy Analytics, driven by the strong performance of its DuerOS conversational AI system. China has surpassed the U.S. as the largest smart speaker market with 500% year-on-year growth. Baidu's DuerOS voice assistant base reached 275 million users, with monthly voice queries increasing significantly, indicating strong user engagement and product innovation.

title: This millennial used scholarship money to buy property in college—now his real estate company is worth $3.8 billion
summary: Eric Wu, co-founder and CEO of Opendoor, used his college scholarship money to buy his first property at age 19. He expanded his real estate portfolio to about 25 properties by the time he graduated, leveraging equity and rental income. This early venture into real estate and tech led him to co-found Opendoor, a real estate startup now valued at $3.8 billion.

title: How Costco uses $5 rotisserie chickens and free samples to turn customers into fanatics
summary: Costco cultivates immense customer loyalty through strategic design elements including exclusive memberships, extreme value (like $5 rotisserie chickens), and an engaging "treasure hunt" shopping experience. The company's low prices, unique store layout, free samples, and popular Kirkland Signature brand contribute to high customer retention and strong financial performance. Ultimately, Costco's business model focuses on providing high-quality products at low prices while making a fair return, leading to billions in revenue.

title: Monro expands partnership with Amazon with 800 Monro centers
summary: Monro Auto Service and Tire Centers announced the expansion of its partnership with Amazon.com, allowing tire installation services at over 400 additional retail locations. This expansion more than doubles the number of service locations to over 800 stores across 21 states, representing approximately two-thirds of Monro's store base. The collaboration has received an average 4.6-star rating and is a key initiative in Monro's omni-channel strategy.

title: Lands’ End to take final steps away from Sears
summary: Lands' End is nearing its complete separation from Sears by exiting its remaining store-within-a-store locations. The apparel retailer plans to open 40 to 60 owned stores in the coming years and has expanded its online presence, including selling on Amazon and Walmart.com. Analysts widely support this move, citing Sears' declining relevance and the benefits of Lands' End strengthening its own brand and direct-to-consumer channels.

title: Palo Alto Networks Introduces Prisma: The Secure Way to Cloud
summary: Palo Alto Networks announced Prisma, a new cloud security suite designed to provide simpler, more secure, and comprehensive cloud security. Prisma consolidates and expands on existing cloud security products, offering solutions for secure access, data protection, and application security across various cloud environments. With approximately 9,000 enterprise customers, Prisma aims to be the largest cloud security business globally.

title: Palo Alto Networks Acquires Cloud Container Security Provider Twistlock: Report -
summary: Palo Alto Networks has reportedly acquired Twistlock, an Israel-based cybersecurity startup specializing in container, serverless, and public cloud system protection, for an estimated $450 million to $500 million. This acquisition comes just before Palo Alto Networks' Ignite19 conference and follows other strategic moves to expand its MSSP-centric partner program. Twistlock's technology protects major cloud systems like Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Docker, Kubernetes, and Pivotal.

title: SETTING THE STAGE
summary: The article discusses the resurgence of film and television production in Los Angeles, driven by streaming services and tax incentives, which has led to a boom for soundstage owners. It highlights that studio spaces are near 100% occupancy, making it a lucrative but operationally intensive business for property owners. Key players like Hudson Pacific Properties, Occidental Entertainment Group, and Hackman Capital are expanding their soundstage portfolios, with long-term leases becoming more common due to high demand.

title: 'Merch by Amazon' t-shirt business increasing orders from Disney to Dr. Seuss
summary: Amazon's 'Merch by Amazon' on-demand t-shirt printing service is increasingly being used by major entertainment companies like Walt Disney Co and Dr. Seuss. This service allows brands to produce merchandise closer to the point of sale, eliminating the need for large upfront inventory commitments and traditional supply chains. The trend is contributing to Amazon's growing influence in the clothing industry and allows for more niche and timely product offerings.

title: Exclusive: Amazon interested in buying Boost from T-Mobile, Sprint - sources
summary: Amazon.com Inc is reportedly interested in acquiring Boost Mobile from T-Mobile US Inc and Sprint Corp, according to sources familiar with the matter. The potential deal would allow Amazon to utilize the new T-Mobile's wireless network for at least six years and could also include the divestment of wireless spectrum. This move comes as T-Mobile and Sprint look to sell assets like Boost to gain regulatory approval for their planned $26 billion merger.

title: Meet the billionaires of the new cloud boom
summary: The growth in cloud software has created a new wave of billionaires, with founders of companies like Atlassian, Zoom, Shopify, and Dropbox amassing significant wealth. This trend highlights investors' interest in "land and expand" business models and recurring revenue, making cloud software a fertile ground for new tech giants. While Salesforce's Marc Benioff was once the dominant figure, many new billionaires now rival or exceed his net worth in the cloud industry.

title: Blackstone to buy warehouse network in record $18.7 billion deal
summary: Blackstone Group LP is set to acquire a network of U.S. industrial warehouses from Singapore-based GLP for a record-breaking $18.7 billion, including debt. This deal marks the largest private real-estate transaction ever and highlights the growing interest in warehouse properties fueled by e-commerce expansion. Blackstone outbid Prologis Inc. for the portfolio, which comprises approximately 180 million square feet of space.

title: Elon Musk Reveals Tesla Pickup Truck's Price: ‘Well Under $50,000’
summary: Elon Musk has revealed the anticipated price point for Tesla's upcoming electric pickup truck, stating it will be "well under $50,000," possibly starting at $49,000. This pricing strategy aims to challenge rivals like Rivian's R1T, which has a higher price tag, and target a broader demographic. Musk also detailed some expected features, including high towing capacity, long range, and advanced technology, positioning it against traditional pickups and sports cars.

title: Blackstone bets big on Amazon, e-commerce with $18.7-billion acquisition
summary: Blackstone Group is making an $18.7-billion acquisition of 179 million square feet of urban logistics properties from Singapore's GLP, significantly expanding its U.S. industrial footprint. This move capitalizes on the increasing demand for warehouse space driven by the growth of Amazon and other e-commerce companies, with properties concentrated in high-growth metropolitan areas. The deal highlights a significant investment trend towards logistics real estate as online shopping continues to reshape retail.

title: Walmart CEO Calls for Raising the Federal Minimum Wage
summary: Walmart CEO Doug McMillon has called for Congress to raise the federal minimum wage, stating the current $7.25 is "too low" and that a thoughtful plan should be put in place. This marks the first time in over a decade a Walmart CEO has specifically demanded new legislation on the matter, despite the company having raised its own starting wage to $11 an hour. The announcement coincided with Senator Bernie Sanders campaigning at Walmart's annual meeting, advocating for a $15 an hour living wage for Walmart workers.

title: Jamie Dimon shows the JPMorgan Chase flag at Philly’s big BIO meeting
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon spoke at the BIO 2019 conference in Philadelphia, expressing concerns about the "self-inflicted" U.S.-China trade war and the potential for a broader "economic war." He also discussed his company's expansion in Philadelphia, efforts to cut healthcare costs, and the importance of immigration reform and higher minimum wages. Dimon touched on the soundness of the U.S. financial system despite problematic government policies and the need for stronger leadership and tougher journalists.

title: How International Is Your Foreign-Stock Fund?
summary: This article examines the true international exposure of foreign-equity funds by analyzing revenue streams by region rather than traditional business country allocation. It reveals hidden U.S. and emerging-markets exposures in several large foreign stock funds, highlighting how relying solely on a company's headquarters can misrepresent a fund's geographical diversification. The piece uses Morningstar's Revenue Exposure by Region dataset to offer a more nuanced understanding for investors assessing diversification benefits.

title: Commentary: Why Upwork Scratched College Degree Requirements From Our Job Descriptions
summary: Upwork CEO Stephane Kasriel explains why the company removed college degree requirements for all positions. He argues that the rising cost of tuition and the failure of traditional education to keep pace with job market changes are creating a talent gap. The article suggests that businesses should look for alternative ways to identify skilled workers, such as vocational training and apprenticeships, which are more inclusive and relevant to current industry needs.

title: Amazon unveils a chopper-plane mashup to deliver packages
summary: Amazon unveiled a new drone design for its Prime Air fleet, a hybrid helicopter-plane mashup designed for package delivery. The drone features AI and takes off vertically before flying horizontally like a plane. Amazon aims to use these drones for test deliveries of household goods, with the goal of delivering packages within 7.5 miles of a warehouse within 30 minutes, handling items up to five pounds.

title: The Garmin® DriveSmart 65 with Amazon Alexa brings the ultimate voice-controlled navigator to the 2019 Drive series
summary: Garmin International announced the Garmin DriveSmart 65 with Amazon Alexa, a voice-controlled portable navigator. This device integrates Alexa functionality for navigation, music, news, and tasks, enabling hands-free use and maintaining driver focus. It also offers smart notifications, real-time traffic, weather, parking details, and map updates.

title: Amazon CEO confronted by protester in Las Vegas
summary: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos was confronted by an animal rights activist, Priya Sawhney, during a conference in Las Vegas. Sawhney, identified by Direct Action Everywhere, was protesting conditions at a California poultry farm that supplies Amazon. The incident highlights the company's security spending, which according to Bloomberg News, is about $1.6 million annually for Bezos.

title: Scars finally healing decade after Garner ConAgra plant explosion
summary: A decade after a deadly explosion at the ConAgra Foods Inc. plant in Garner killed four people, the community is moving forward with the site now home to a new Amazon distribution center. The 2009 blast, caused by a natural gas leak, led to the plant's eventual closure, but the town of Garner turned the tragedy into an opportunity for economic growth. The article reflects on the immediate aftermath, the plant's closure, and the subsequent redevelopment of the site, marking a healing process for the town.

title: Amazon launches a credit card for the 'underbanked' with bad credit
summary: Amazon, in partnership with Synchrony Financial, has launched "Amazon Credit Builder," a secured credit card program aimed at individuals with no credit history or bad credit. This initiative offers the same 5% cash back perks as the popular Amazon Store card and includes financial literacy tools, allowing users to build credit and eventually "graduate" to an unsecured card. The program addresses a significant market segment of underbanked Americans and comes with a 28.24% APR for the starter card.

title: Synchrony launches Amazon-branded credit card
summary: Synchrony and Amazon have launched a private-label credit card, Amazon Credit Builder, aimed at consumers looking to improve their credit. This no-annual-fee card offers benefits like 5 percent back on purchases for eligible Amazon Prime members and various financing options. The new partnership helps Synchrony offset business lost from Walmart and contributes to its goal of becoming a major digital-payments player.

title: Amazon launches co-branded credit card with Synchrony for the underbanked
summary: Amazon has partnered with Synchrony Financial to launch the Amazon Credit Builder, a co-branded credit card designed for underbanked consumers. This secured card offers similar benefits to Amazon's existing co-branded card, including 5% cashback for eligible Amazon Prime members, and allows cardholders to build credit with an initial deposit ranging from $100 to $1,000. Cardholders can qualify for a regular card after demonstrating responsible payment behavior, with reviews for upgrade starting as soon as seven months after account opening.

title: Target boosts worker benefits, including paid family leave
summary: Target Corp. announced a series of expanded benefits for its full- and part-time workers, including paid family leave and emergency child care, to attract and retain employees in a competitive labor market. The new policies include doubling paid leave to four weeks, extending subsidized backup care to all employees, and increasing adoption and surrogacy reimbursement to $10,000. These moves reflect a broader retail trend of enhancing wages and perks to address workforce challenges like turnover and absenteeism.

title: AWS Recognizes SAIC as ‘Premier’ Consulting Partner; Dave Levy Quoted
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has recognized Science Applications International Corp. (SAIC) as a "premier" consulting partner under the AWS Partner Network. This top-tier designation acknowledges SAIC's efforts in assisting customers with cloud computing technology. David Levy, VP of the U.S. government business at AWS, expressed excitement about helping government customers achieve their missions faster and more securely through this partnership.

title: FedEx opt out of Express contract with Amazon may be good thing, analysts say
summary: Analysts believe FedEx's decision not to renew its U.S. domestic Express contract with Amazon.com is a positive move for the delivery service company in the long term, despite potential short-term challenges. This move allows FedEx to widen its focus on e-commerce growth across the broader retail sector. Moody's senior vice president Jonathan Root supports this decision, emphasizing the strong e-commerce growth expectations.

title: Amazon Prime Restaurants to shut down restaurant food delivery service in U.S.
summary: Amazon is discontinuing its 4-year-old U.S. restaurant delivery service, Amazon Restaurants, on June 24th due to fierce competition and a small market share. Despite this closure, Amazon recently invested in British food delivery company Deliveroo, suggesting it may not be entirely abandoning the food delivery sector. The news of Amazon's exit caused shares of competitors like Grubhub Inc. to increase by 7%.

title: Amazon Is Shutting Down Its Restaurant Delivery Service In The U.S.
summary: Amazon is shutting down its restaurant delivery service in the U.S. after four years due to intense competition from rivals like Uber Eats and DoorDash. The service, Amazon Restaurants, previously operated in over 20 U.S. cities and expanded to the UK before being closed there last year. Despite this closure, Amazon still shows interest in meal delivery, as evidenced by its recent investment in British food delivery company Deliveroo.

title: Jeff Bezos’ Amazon unveils a credit card for people with no credit history or bad credit
summary: Amazon has launched a new credit card in partnership with Synchrony Financial, called Amazon Credit Builder, aimed at individuals with no credit history or bad credit. The card has an annual percentage rate (APR) of 28.24% and requires users to deposit an equal amount of money for equivalent credit, helping them build a positive credit history to eventually qualify for an unsecured Amazon credit card. This initiative seeks to provide credit facilities to an underserved population.

title: Kohl's adds adaptive clothing to its three top kids' brands
summary: Kohl's has launched a new line of adaptive clothing for children across its three largest kids' brands: Jumping Beans, SO, and Urban Pipeline. This move makes Kohl's one of the largest retailers to enter the growing adaptive clothing market, estimated to reach nearly $289 billion globally this year. The adaptive apparel, designed for easier wear by children with disabilities, aims to boost confidence and independence, offering features like magnetic closures, tagless designs, and softer materials.

title: PetSmart's Chewy gets Wall Street tails wagging with $1 billion IPO
summary: Chewy Inc. priced its initial public offering at $22 per share, exceeding its target and valuing the online pet products retailer at $8.77 billion. The IPO generated funds to help PetSmart manage its debt, demonstrating investor interest in the rapidly growing, albeit loss-making, e-commerce company within the substantial U.S. pet industry. Chewy's sales have surged from $26 million in 2012 to $3.5 billion in 2018, with its net losses narrowing significantly.

title: Chewy raises $1 billion in IPO, and stock soars in trading debut
summary: Chewy Inc. had a successful trading debut after raising $1.02 billion in its initial public offering, with shares soaring by as much as 88% and closing up 59%. The company, backed by PetSmart, plans to expand its private-label products and health services, including prescription drugs, leveraging the consistent growth in pet spending even during economic downturns. This IPO provides significant financial relief for PetSmart, which is burdened with over $8 billion in debt.

title: Tech titans fuel a scramble to build large-scale offices
summary: Tech giants like Google, Amazon, and Netflix are driving a massive scramble for office space in Los Angeles, leading to billions of dollars in new construction and radical redevelopments. These "content creators" prefer large-scale, campus-like facilities with unique amenities over traditional high-rise offices, focusing their hubs in areas like Hollywood, Culver City, and Playa Vista. This trend is sparking an economic boom and attracting a multiplier effect of smaller service providers looking to be near these major players.

title: Domino’s Pizza plans robot deliveries with self-driving minivans in 2019
summary: Domino's Pizza is partnering with Nuro to begin robot deliveries using self-driving R1 minivans in Houston later in 2019. This trial builds on Nuro's previous autonomous grocery deliveries and Domino's ongoing efforts to integrate robotic solutions into its delivery operations, with the R1 vehicles operating on public streets without a human operator. Customers in a designated Houston store will receive a PIN to access their pizza from the self-driving van.

title: Ant Financial's Ability to Disrupt Could Boost EMQQ ETF
summary: The article discusses how Ant Financial's disruptive capabilities, particularly in fintech and now healthcare, could benefit the Emerging Markets Internet & Ecommerce ETF (EMQQ). EMQQ holds Alibaba Group, a majority stakeholder in Ant Financial, positioning the ETF to capitalize on Ant Financial's innovative strategies in emerging markets. The piece highlights the rapid growth in the financial technology space and Ant Financial's expansion into health insurance with its Ziang Hu Bao program, attracting millions of participants.

title: JBG Smith accused of not honoring housing vouchers in Shaw
summary: JBG Smith is accused of not honoring housing vouchers at its Atlantic Plumbing apartments in Shaw, Washington D.C. Resident Regina Williams claims she was denied housing because the property allegedly does not accept vouchers. This accusation comes despite JBG Smith's own initiatives to support affordable housing.

title: Amazon pulls back from original kids programming
summary: Amazon Studios is reportedly scaling back its investment in original animated shows for young children, shifting its focus to content for families to view together and for young adult audiences. This strategic change comes amidst executive changes and internal debates over the value of kids' programming in driving Prime memberships, especially as competitors like Netflix, Disney, and Apple continue to invest heavily in the children's content space. The company will continue to produce existing kids' animated series but will prioritize licensing kids' content and developing more mature animation, including young adult animated series.

title: CIO Hall Of Famer Harry Moseley Puts Zoom On Track To Scale
summary: Harry Moseley, a CIO Hall of Famer, came out of retirement to become Zoom Video Communications' first-ever CIO in late 2017. He describes his 16 months in the role, highlighting Zoom's strong culture, innovative technology, and the refreshing experience of working in a digital-native organization. Moseley also shares insights on board memberships and future tech trends like AI and 5G.

title: Simplify Data Management Across Public or Private Clouds with NetApp Cloud Volumes
summary: NetApp is enhancing data management across public and private clouds by offering a feature-rich portfolio of cloud data services. The article details NetApp's public cloud offerings like Azure NetApp Files, Cloud Volumes Service for Google Cloud and AWS, and Cloud Volumes ONTAP, alongside on-premises solutions such as NetApp HCI and Cloud Volumes Service On-Premises. These solutions aim to provide enterprise-class file services, high performance, and simplified data management, catering to various cloud strategies and regulatory requirements.

title: Automatically Tier Your Data to Amazon S3 Glacier with NetApp StorageGRID
summary: NetApp StorageGRID now supports automatic tiering of data to Amazon S3 Glacier, offering customers more flexibility in managing rapidly growing unstructured data across hybrid multi-cloud environments. This integration, part of StorageGRID 11.2, allows users to leverage intelligent, policy-driven data management for cost savings and simplified archiving, ensuring data is in the right place at the right time with appropriate performance and resiliency. The update also brings additional simplicity, security enhancements like multifactor authentication, and higher performance for small object workloads.

title: Fluent acquires AdParlor, a social ad specialist previously owned by Adknowledge, for $10M
summary: Fluent, a marketing company, has acquired AdParlor, a social advertising specialist, for $10 million. AdParlor, originally a major Facebook Ads API vendor, was previously owned by AdKnowledge (now V2 Ventures). This acquisition aims to integrate AdParlor's social media advertising expertise across various platforms into Fluent's existing marketing technology stack.

title: Work on Boston’s tallest office building in 25 years has started
summary: Construction has begun on One Congress, a 600-foot-tall skyscraper in Boston, set to become the city's tallest office building in 25 years. The building, scheduled to open in 2022, will serve as the new headquarters for State Street Corp., which has leased about half of its 1 million square feet. This project is part of a larger redevelopment of the Government Center Garage area and signifies continued growth in Boston's downtown job market.

title: Alibaba and JD.Com to Combine Facial Recognition With Data in Bid for Merchant Loyalty
summary: Alibaba and JD.com are integrating facial recognition and deep customer data to enhance merchant loyalty and diversify revenue streams amidst slowing e-commerce growth in China. This "new retail" approach offers personalized marketing and operational efficiencies, benefiting brands like Bestore and Nestle, while raising questions about data management and retailer dependency.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper withdraws Peñafiel bottled water from US for high arsenic levels
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper withdrew Peñafiel spring water products from the U.S. market due to arsenic levels exceeding the FDA's 10 parts per billion limit, a problem highlighted by a Consumer Reports investigation. The company stated it has notified retailers and installed enhanced filtration systems to ensure current production meets regulatory guidelines, but faces potential lawsuits and scrutiny for the delay in withdrawal. This incident raises questions about bottled water safety and the adequacy of current federal arsenic level standards, similar to challenges faced by other food and beverage companies regarding chemical residues.

title: Crate & Barrel buys up S.F.-based home furnishings company
summary: Crate & Barrel has acquired Hudson Grace, a San Francisco-based home furnishings brand, to expand its portfolio. Hudson Grace, which has five stores in California, will continue to operate as a standalone business under the international retailer. This strategic acquisition aims to complement Crate & Barrel's existing labels.

title: FedEx slashes two-day air prices to match ground rates to fill its planes
summary: FedEx is cutting prices for two-day air service to match ground shipping rates for some customers of its Express network. This strategy aims to attract online merchants, especially as the company ends its air-shipping contract with Amazon.com Inc., and to boost its flagging Express network by filling its planes. The move comes as FedEx anticipates a doubling of daily packages shipped in the U.S. by 2026 due to the growth in online shopping.

title: Cloud Services Starting To Overtake On-Prem Database Management Systems
summary: A new report by Gartner Inc. indicates that cloud services are rapidly overtaking on-premises solutions in the database management system (DBMS) market, accounting for 68% of the market's 18.4% growth from 2017 to 2018. Gartner predicts that on-premises DBMS will become a "legacy" approach, with significant growth driven by Amazon Web Services and Microsoft's cloud offerings. The shift is attributed to factors like Software as a Service applications, pay-as-you-go pricing, and innovation primarily occurring in cloud DBMS.

title: Blockchain Could Make You—Not Equifax—the Owner of Your Data
summary: This article discusses how blockchain technology can empower individuals to own and monetize their personal data, challenging traditional data brokers like Equifax. It explains how blockchain-based solutions use cryptography, such as keys, hashes, and smart contracts, to create a decentralized system for data exchange, giving users control over who accesses and profits from their information. The piece also addresses the challenges of scalability and storage within blockchain technology but highlights its potential to disrupt the current data economy.

title: 4 Reasons the Stock Market's Outlook Is Bright: Goldman
summary: Goldman Sachs identifies four key reasons for a bullish stock market outlook, including a strong start to the year, upward earnings revisions, investor caution, and low odds of a NAFTA breakup. They also highlight that stocks with strong secular revenue growth are best positioned to outperform. The S&P 500's performance, corporate earnings growth, and specific stock recommendations are discussed.

title: Target kicks off back-to-school season with new clothes, college departments and more
summary: Target is expanding its back-to-school offerings with new uniform items under its Cat & Jack brand and launching a new '"More Than Magic" tween girl brand. The retailer is also introducing "Back to College" sections in over 700 stores near college campuses and enhancing its School List Assist service. These initiatives aim to provide a broader range of products and convenience for both K-12 and college shoppers for the upcoming season.

title: Can Adobe's Digital Experience Revenues Exceed Digital Media Revenues By 2025?
summary: This article examines whether Adobe's Digital Experience revenues can surpass Digital Media revenues by 2025, noting the former's faster growth rate. While Digital Experience is expanding rapidly, driven by market growth and strategic acquisitions, Digital Media is expected to remain the larger segment through 2025 due to its established market share and steady expansion. The analysis provides detailed forecasts and market share projections for both segments.

title: JPMorgan Chase expands Seattle engineering center to 100 people, plans to add hundreds more
summary: JPMorgan Chase is significantly expanding its technology engineering center in Seattle, growing to 100 people in its first year and signing a new lease to accommodate hundreds more. This expansion is part of the financial services giant's major investment in cloud technology, partnering with AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud, and signals Seattle's growing potential as a fintech hub. The bank's CEO, Jamie Dimon, initially skeptical, is now fully committed to cloud adoption and integrating AI into operations.

title: Expedia shows off $900M Seattle waterfront campus as thousands of employees prepare to move in
summary: Expedia showcased its new $900 million Seattle waterfront campus as thousands of employees prepare to move in. The campus, located in the Interbay neighborhood, is a sprawling space with stunning waterfront views, featuring biophilic design and a mix of renovated and new buildings. The move signifies a major shift from its former Bellevue headquarters, with the company implementing solutions to mitigate traffic impacts and aiming to house over 8,000 workers eventually.

title: Domino’s CEO Doesn’t Want a Robot Making Your Pizza
summary: Domino's CEO Ritch Allison believes pizza will endure, but acknowledges a high-tech shift in its creation and delivery. While the company is exploring innovations like driverless delivery and digital assistants for ordering, Allison expresses reservations about robots making pizzas. Domino's (DPZ) faces increasing competition from other delivery services in the quick-service restaurant industry.

title: Apple Leases 635 KSF Office Campus in Seattle
summary: Apple has signed a long-term lease with Kilroy Realty Corp. to fully occupy 333 Dexter, a 635,000-square-foot campus in Seattle’s South Lake Union. The two-tower project, Kilroy Realty's first ground-up development in the city, is scheduled for completion in late 2019. Apple plans to hire over 2,000 employees in the city within the next five years for this new location.

title: PetSmart upgraded thanks in part to Chewy IPO
summary: PetSmart's credit rating has been upgraded by Moody's Investor Service and S&P Global, partially due to the success of Chewy's initial public offering. The IPO proceeds allowed PetSmart to repay debt, improving its leverage and overall financial outlook. This upgrade comes despite an increasingly saturated pet retail market.

title: Elastic SIEM woos enterprises with cost savings
summary: Elastic SIEM is gaining interest from enterprises, especially former Splunk users, due to its promise of cost savings and its ability to centralize security analytics and IT monitoring data. The tool standardizes data schemas and offers a competitive alternative to established players like Splunk and AWS in the security analytics market. Its future integration with Endgame, an endpoint security company, is seen as a significant long-term appeal for the application.

title: GIC to Fuel Equinix’s Hyperscale Market Ambition
summary: Equinix, the world’s largest data center provider, is partnering with GIC, Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund, in a $1 billion joint venture to build and operate hyperscale data centers for major digital platforms. This initiative, branded xScale, aims to address the growing demand from tech giants like Alibaba, Amazon, and Microsoft for large-scale data center capacity, especially in Europe. The move allows Equinix to expand into the hyperscale market without cannibalizing its core retail colocation business, leveraging GIC’s capital for significant investments.

title: Interview with Thomas M. Siebel on Digital Tranformation
summary: Thomas M. Siebel, Chairman and CEO of C3.ai, discusses his entrepreneurial journey from Oracle to Siebel Systems and now C3.ai, highlighting the impact of digital transformation driven by elastic cloud computing, big data, AI, and IoT. He shares insights on building a company culture, the potential negative impacts of AI, and the thesis of his book "Digital Transformation," urging business leaders to adapt to an existential shift in the corporate world. Siebel also touches on entrepreneurial philanthropy and offers advice to young professionals.

title: In Court Filing, Prime Inc. Says Amazon’s Use of ‘Prime’ Causes Confusion
summary: Prime Inc. has filed a complaint against Amazon, alleging that Amazon’s use of "Prime" on its shipping vehicles creates a likelihood of confusion with Prime Inc.'s trucking business. Prime Inc. claims Amazon's trademark registration should be canceled due to fraud, as Amazon did not transport goods itself at the time of its 2005 application. Prime Inc. is seeking injunctive relief, damages, and attorneys' fees in addition to trademark cancellation.

title: Amazon can be held liable for third-party seller products: U.S. appeals court
summary: A federal appeals court has ruled that Amazon.com Inc can be held liable for defective products sold by third-party vendors on its platform, a decision that departs from previous court rulings. This ruling, based on Pennsylvania law, stemmed from a lawsuit filed by a customer who was injured by a retractable dog leash purchased via Amazon's website. The court highlighted that Amazon's business model can obscure third-party vendors, leaving injured customers without direct recourse.

title: Mark Shuttleworth sold a tech startup he built in his garage for $575 million and used the money to visit space
summary: Mark Shuttleworth, founder of Thawte, sold his tech startup for $575 million in 1999 and used $20 million to finance a trip to space in 2002. He later founded Canonical, an open-source software provider, which he fully funded himself. Shuttleworth details his journey from starting Thawte in his parents' garage to his space adventure and his vision for open source through Canonical.

title: Report: Amazon Founder Bezos’ Divorce Final; Settlement $38B
summary: Amazon.com Inc. founder Jeff Bezos and MacKenzie Bezos have finalized their divorce, with MacKenzie set to receive $38.3 billion in Amazon stock. Jeff Bezos will retain voting control of her shares and remains the world's richest person with a 12% stake. MacKenzie Bezos has pledged to give half of her fortune to charity as part of the "Giving Pledge."

title: Razer Chroma lighting comes to AMD Ryzen 7 and 9 Wraith Prism fans
summary: Razer has partnered with AMD to integrate Chroma RGB lighting into the Wraith Prism fans included with AMD's new 3rd Gen Ryzen 7 and 9 CPUs. This collaboration allows users to synchronize the lighting of their CPU cooler with other Razer Chroma accessories through the Synapse software, enhancing the aesthetic consistency of gaming setups. The 3rd Gen Ryzen 3000 Series CPUs, with prices starting at $200, are now available, though Chroma integration is exclusive to the Ryzen 7 and 9 chips.

title: Prime, Inc. trucking sues Amazon Prime for use of name
summary: Prime, Inc., a Springfield-based trucking company, is suing Amazon Prime for alleged trademark infringement. Prime, Inc. claims Amazon's use of "Prime" on its tractor-trailers causes confusion and economic loss, despite being notified over two years ago. The lawsuit seeks significant damages, arguing Amazon's infringement is "intentional, willful, and malicious."

title: Here is What You Need to Know About Douyu, Chinese Streaming Unicorn Eyeing US IPO
summary: Douyu, a leading Chinese game streaming unicorn backed by Tencent, is preparing for a US IPO with an expected valuation between $3.73 billion and $4.54 billion. The company reported a profitable Q1 2019, with revenues soaring 123.4% year-on-year and a significant increase in paying users to over 6 million, surpassing its rival Huya. Despite its success, concerns remain about Douyu's long-term growth and its reliance on user tips, differing significantly from Twitch's more diverse revenue streams.

title: Piper Jaffray announces $485M deal for Sandler O'Neill, new name
summary: Piper Jaffray Cos. announced it will acquire fellow investment bank Sandler O'Neill for $485 million. The combined entity will operate under the new name Piper Sandler Cos. Chad Abraham, CEO of Piper Jaffray, will lead the new firm.

title: Prime seeks damages in Amazon trademark dispute
summary: Springfield-based trucking and logistics company Prime Inc. is suing Amazon.com Inc. for trademark infringement, seeking damages equal to three times Amazon's profits or Prime Inc.'s losses. The lawsuit alleges customer confusion due to Amazon's use of "Prime" for its shipping services, which Prime Inc. claims to have used since 1980. Prime Inc. argues Amazon's Prime logos are "confusingly similar" and impact its reputation in the transportation sector.

title: IBM closes $34 billion deal to buy Red Hat to boost cloud business
summary: IBM has completed its $34 billion acquisition of Red Hat Inc., marking its largest-ever deal, to significantly bolster its cloud computing business. This strategic move aims to help companies transition to hybrid cloud environments, offering a mix of public and private cloud applications. Red Hat will operate as a distinct unit within IBM, maintaining its headquarters and management, with no immediate job or cost cuts planned.

title: Prime Inc. sues Amazon Prime for trademark infringement
summary: New Prime Inc., a trucking company, has filed a lawsuit against Amazon for trademark infringement, alleging that Amazon's "Prime" logos and services have caused customer confusion and harmed its business. Prime Inc. claims to have used the "Prime Inc." phrase for nearly 40 years and that Amazon falsely represented its shipping services when it sought to register the Prime word mark. The lawsuit seeks injunctive relief, actual damages, attorney's fees, and the cancellation of Amazon’s U.S. Patent and Trademark Office registration for "Prime."

title: Springfield trucking company sues Amazon over use of 'Prime'
summary: Springfield-based trucking company Prime Inc. is suing Amazon for its use of "Prime" on shipping vehicles, claiming it causes confusion and irreparable damage to its brand. Prime Inc., which has used the "Prime Inc." logo since 1980, alleges Amazon's similar "Amazon Prime" logo on tractor trailers violates federal trademark law and misleads consumers. The lawsuit argues that consumers might associate negative experiences with Amazon with Prime Inc., harming its reputation and goodwill.

title: Prime, Inc. takes Amazon to court over retailer’s use of ‘Prime’ on its trucks
summary: Prime, Inc., a Springfield, Missouri-based trucking company, has filed a lawsuit against Amazon, seeking to revoke Amazon’s "Prime" trademark and claim damages. Prime, Inc. argues that Amazon's use of "Prime" on its trucks creates public confusion and negatively impacts its reputation and bottom line. The lawsuit contends that Amazon falsely represented its services in its trademark application and that Prime, Inc. had established prior common law rights to the name since 1970.

title: Big tech company to move HQ from Sunnyvale to San Jose
summary: Rambus Inc. is relocating its headquarters from Sunnyvale to North San Jose, acquiring 90,000 square feet at 4453 North First St. The move is driven by the desire for a more modern workspace, lower lease costs, and proximity to employee housing, reflecting a broader trend of tech companies moving to San Jose as the Peninsula's commercial vacancy rates tighten. This shift highlights San Jose's growing appeal for tech companies, demonstrated by other recent moves like HPE and McAfee, and ongoing development in the area.

title: Prime, Inc. sues Amazon over trademarked "Prime" logo
summary: Prime, Inc., a trucking company, has filed a lawsuit against Amazon, alleging trademark infringement over Amazon's use of the "Prime" logo on its trucks and trailers. Prime, Inc. claims to have used its name and logo on their vehicles for over 40 years and holds the trademark for "transportation services by truck." The lawsuit seeks monetary damages and an injunction against Amazon's continued use of the logo on its trailers.

title: Prime, Inc. takes Amazon to court over use of ‘prime’ on trailers
summary: Prime, Inc., the 14th largest trucking company in the U.S., has filed a lawsuit against Amazon alleging trademark infringement over the use of the word "prime" on Amazon's trailers. Prime, Inc. claims to have used its name and logo on trucks and trailers for over 40 years and holds trademarks for "transportation services by truck." The lawsuit seeks monetary damages and an injunction against Amazon's continued use of the "Amazon Prime" logo on its trailers.

title: Cloud Volumes ONTAP: Experience the Benefits of ONTAP Across Azure, AWS, and GCP
summary: NetApp has expanded its Cloud Volumes ONTAP (CVO) offering to include Google Cloud Platform (GCP), making it available across all three major cloud providers: Microsoft Azure, Amazon AWS, and Google Cloud Platform. CVO offers full ONTAP features in the cloud, enabling use cases like multi-cloud disaster recovery, cost-efficient storage for cloud-native applications, and persistent storage for Docker and Kubernetes. The article differentiates CVO (IaaS, user-managed) from Cloud Volumes Service (CVS) (PaaS, fully managed).

title: Alexa co-creator: Digital world forgot importance of real dialogue
summary: Alex Spinelli, former global head of Alexa for Amazon and current LivePerson CTO, states that the digital world has become too focused on interfaces and has lost sight of using technology to truly connect with and understand consumers. He suggests that this focus has detracted from the original purpose of digital interaction, which should be about real dialogue.

title: Investors Use Indexes to Play in the Video Game Business (Published 2019)
summary: The video game industry, transitioning from arcades to mobile and streaming, presents significant investment opportunities. Big tech companies like Microsoft, Google, and Amazon are entering the streaming video game market, alongside equipment makers and game publishers set to capitalize on new capabilities. The industry is projected to reach $180 billion in annual sales, with investors increasingly using exchange-traded funds to gain exposure.

title: Amazon's top cardboard box makers face challenges from plastic mailers
summary: Cardboard box manufacturers, including suppliers to Amazon like Westrock and International Paper, initially benefited greatly from the boom in e-commerce, especially Amazon Prime's growing package volume. However, Amazon is now shifting towards plastic mailers and bags for smaller products to cut costs and speed up delivery, posing a new challenge for the cardboard industry. This move comes after the industry found a saving grace in e-commerce following a decline in demand for traditional paper products and the impact of the Great Recession.

title: Blackstone buys warehouse assets for $18.7bn
summary: Blackstone Group LP has acquired the US industrial warehouse properties of Singapore-based logistics provider GLP for $18.7 billion, marking the largest private real estate transaction globally. This deal significantly expands Blackstone's US industrial footprint, nearly doubling its existing assets and making it the largest US owner and operator of warehouses focused on e-commerce. The acquisition builds on Blackstone's strategy to invest in logistics as a key global investment theme, leveraging the growing demand driven by e-commerce.

title: Target launches 'tween' brand in time for back-to-school rush
summary: Target has launched a new "tween" brand called "More than Magic" just in time for the back-to-school season. This multiproduct line, designed for 9- to 13-year-old girls, includes apparel, electronics, and school supplies, with most items under $30. The move aims to capture the back-to-school market and cater to an underserved demographic as many mall-based specialty "tween" stores are closing.

title: This new business from Amazon represents a '$100 billion opportunity,' Morgan Stanley says
summary: Morgan Stanley estimates that Amazon's Project Kuiper, a planned network of 3,236 satellites to provide global high-speed internet, could represent a "$100 billion opportunity." This projection is based on the firm's expectation that the overall space economy will grow to over $1 trillion in the next 20 years. Project Kuiper positions Amazon to compete with companies like SpaceX in the race to build next-generation internet satellite networks, with analyst Adam Jonas highlighting Jeff Bezos's increasing financial commitment to space ventures through Blue Origin.

title: How Amazon Prime Day uses your psychology to get you to buy
summary: Amazon Prime Day leverages various psychological tactics to encourage purchases, transforming a simple sale into a major shopping holiday. Key strategies include creating exclusivity for Prime members, employing scarcity and urgency through limited-time deals and countdown clocks, and fostering a viral social media environment. While effective, these tactics can lead to buyer's remorse or "inaction inertia" if consumers miss out on deals and later devalue products at regular prices.

title: Milwaukee seeks to expand Century City Business Park -- even as it struggles to attract north side development
summary: The City of Milwaukee plans to expand its Century City Business Park by purchasing 13.7 acres for $250,000, despite previous difficulties attracting development. The expansion aims to increase visibility with more Capitol Drive frontage and provide additional space, making it more attractive to potential businesses. While the city has invested significantly in the park, it has struggled to secure tenants, with several large companies opting for other locations.

title: Disney Content Sales President Janice Marinelli to Depart
summary: Janice Marinelli, President of global sales and marketing at Walt Disney’s direct-to-consumer and international segment, announced her departure after a 34-year career. She cited the integration of 21st Century Fox and the rapid industry changes as factors in her decision. Marinelli oversaw significant operations including the distribution of Disney's film and TV programming and spearheaded the development of Movies Anywhere.

title: Great Deals On Jessica Alba’s Honest Beauty And Baby Products On Amazon Prime Day
summary: Jessica Alba's Honest Company is offering significant discounts on its beauty and baby products for Amazon Prime Day. Fans can get up to 20 percent off items like the Vitamin C Radiance Serum and the Gently Nourishing Face and Body Lotion, along with a vegan leather backpack that doubles as a diaper bag. The Honest Company, founded in 2011, focuses on eco-friendly and safe consumer products, and has expanded into beauty items while previously lobbying Congress for stricter chemical input testing.

title: Walmart CEO McMillon says the retailer has been playing ‘catch up’ in e-commerce
summary: Walmart CEO Doug McMillon admits the retail giant has been "playing catch up" in e-commerce, specifically against Amazon.com Inc. McMillon stated at Fortune's Brainstorm Tech conference that Walmart has been undergoing a transformation to meet evolving consumer shopping demands. This acknowledges the company's efforts to adjust and progress in the digital retail space after an initial lag.

title: Microsoft, AT&T sign cloud deal worth more than $2 billion
summary: Microsoft and AT&T have signed a multi-year cloud deal valued at over $2 billion, making Microsoft AT&T's "preferred" cloud vendor. AT&T will utilize Microsoft's Azure cloud service and Microsoft 365 for its workforce and will collaborate with Microsoft on edge computing for its 5G network. This agreement marks a significant shift for AT&T towards a "public cloud first" strategy and strengthens Microsoft's position in the competitive cloud services market.

title: Amazon: Prime Day sales were bigger than Black Friday and Cyber Monday combined
summary: Amazon announced that its 2019 Prime Day sales surpassed the combined sales of Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2018, with members purchasing 175 million items globally. This two-day event also marked the biggest two days ever for new Prime member signups. The article notes Prime Day's growing influence, attracting competing retail sales and drawing attention to Amazon's employee wages.

title: eBay Welcomes Pete Thompson as Chief Product Officer; Mazen Rawashdeh promoted to Chief Technology Officer
summary: eBay announced new leadership appointments, welcoming Pete Thompson as Senior Vice President and Chief Product Officer and promoting Mazen Rawashdeh to Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer. Both executives will report to President and CEO Devin Wenig, with Thompson focusing on personalizing the shopping experience and Rawashdeh leading platform engineering and architecture. Additionally, Scott Gaffney joins as VP, Search Engineering, and Steve Metz returns as VP, Product Analytics, further strengthening eBay's leadership in product and technology.

title: Etsy to acquire music gear marketplace Reverb for $275M
summary: Etsy announced its definitive agreement to acquire Reverb Holdings, a musical instrument marketplace, for $275 million in cash. Reverb will operate as a standalone business, and its founder, David Kalt, will step down as CEO. The acquisition aims to leverage synergies between the two companies, with Etsy's CFO Rachel Glaser highlighting Reverb's similar business model and strong brand in a large market.

title: Target’s Small-Format Stores Are Its Biggest Weapon Against Amazon and Walmart
summary: Target's strategy of opening smaller-format stores in urban areas and college campuses is proving highly successful in its competition against Amazon and Walmart. These tailored stores, which are Target's most productive, are integrated into a strong delivery network, offering convenience like same-day delivery via Shipt, and bolstering customer loyalty and financial performance. This approach leverages Target's brand appeal and proximity to customers, resulting in significant growth in sales and stock performance.

title: Amazon, Realogy team up to help you buy your next house and get free stuff in the process
summary: Amazon and Realogy Holdings Corp. have launched "TurnKey," a new platform designed to streamline the home-buying process and offer incentives. The program connects homebuyers with local Realogy-affiliated agents and provides free Amazon smart home products and services worth $1,000 to $5,000, depending on the home's purchase price. This initiative aims to reduce stress for buyers while increasing sales for both companies and is available in 15 U.S. cities.

title: Kroger churns out new ice cream flavors to drive its sales
summary: Kroger is expanding its private label ice cream offerings, introducing exotic new flavors like Unicorn Swirl and Black Cherry Root Beer Float to boost sales and compete in the grocery market. These house brands are a significant part of Kroger's $22 billion private label business, providing both lower-cost and unique options to customers. The strategy is proving successful, with the Unicorn Swirl flavor quickly becoming a top seller, and overall ice cream innovations credited for generating $225 million in new sales this year.

title: Weis Markets Expands Weis 2 Go Program
summary: Weis Markets is expanding its Weis 2 Go online ordering service to 61 additional stores, bringing the total to 150 stores in seven states. This service allows customers to pick up groceries at designated locations or have them delivered to their homes, offering a seamless shopping experience through mobile ordering and online at WeisMarkets.com. For a limited time, the $4.95 curbside pick-up fee is waived, and customers can use coupons and Weis Preferred Shopper cards to save and earn rewards.

title: Apple Is Now the Most Valuable Brand Ever, Thanks to This 1 Thing. (The Good News Is You Can Totally Do It Too)
summary: Apple has become the most valuable brand globally, valued at $205 billion, largely due to its commitment to delighting customers beyond expectations. While the iPhone's success contributes, the core reason for its brand value lies in fostering positive feelings through every customer interaction. The article suggests that any business can achieve similar brand success by focusing on unexpected customer delight rather than just meeting expectations.

title: Off-White Voluntarily Dismisses Trademark Lawsuit Over Allegedly Infringing Bracelets
summary: Off-White has voluntarily dismissed its trademark infringement lawsuit against bracelet-maker Rastaclat, almost three months after filing the complaint. The lawsuit, centered on Rastaclat's use of red zip ties and quotation marks, was likely settled out of court, leading to the removal of the allegedly infringing products from Rastaclat's website and other retailers. This dismissal follows complications with Off-White's own trademark application for the red zip tie, which the USPTO preliminarily rejected on grounds of being confusingly similar to existing marks, functional, and lacking inherent distinctiveness.

title: Amazon’s run of record earnings comes to an end, and the stock is falling
summary: Amazon's streak of record quarterly profits has ended, with the company reporting a decline in second-quarter earnings despite strong sales growth. The e-commerce giant's stock fell in late trading as earnings of $2.6 billion, or $5.22 a share, missed analysts' estimates of $5.56 a share. Revenue, however, exceeded expectations, reaching $63.4 billion.

title: Report: Amazon Web Services Expands in Herndon
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is expanding its presence in Northern Virginia by leasing 13820 Sunrise Valley Drive in Herndon, adding to its significant footprint in the region. This expansion comes as AWS continues to pursue major federal government contracts, including the Department of Defense's $10 billion JEDI cloud contract. The company has leased close to 852,800 square feet in Northern Virginia, cementing its status as one of the fastest-growing tenants.

title: Louis Theroux leaving BBC to form production company; Netflix and Amazon circling (exclusive)
summary: Documentary filmmaker Louis Theroux is reportedly forming an independent production company after his current deal with the BBC ends, leading to a bidding war between Amazon and Netflix for a production deal. Theroux, who is collaborating with BBC Studios executive Arron Fellows on the new venture, is also considering continuing to make documentaries for the BBC in an independent capacity. His new company is expected to enter the podcast space alongside film production.

title: Capital One Data Breach Compromises Data of Over 100 Million (Published 2019)
summary: Capital One experienced one of the largest bank data thefts, compromising the personal data of over 100 million people. A software engineer, Paige Thompson, was arrested and charged with computer fraud and abuse after boasting about the hacking online. Thompson, a former Amazon Web Services employee, left an extensive digital trail that led to her identification and arrest.

title: FOX NFL Thursday Adds Another Hall of Famer to Star-Studded Lineup
summary: Tony Gonzalez, Class of 2019 Pro Football Hall of Famer, is joining the FOX NFL THURSDAY pregame show for the NFL's 100th season, starting September 26th. He will appear regularly alongside Michael Strahan, Terry Bradshaw, and Howie Long, with Strahan hosting the show. FOX Thursday Night Football games will be available on Amazon Prime Video, Twitch, and various NFL and FOX digital properties.

title: No more cardboard boxes? 3M invents an ingenious new way to ship products
summary: 3M has introduced Flex & Seal Shipping Roll, a new packaging material designed to replace cardboard boxes for items under 3 pounds. This innovation aims to reduce packing time, material waste, and shipping space by 50%, offering a self-sealing, tear- and water-resistant alternative for e-commerce shipments. While it offers efficiency and tamper protection, its recyclability currently requires specialized retail drop-offs, a challenge 3M is working to address.

title: As rural India develops taste for chocolate, Mondelez extends its reach
summary: Mondelez is significantly expanding its reach into rural India to capitalize on the growing taste for chocolate, driven by rising disposable incomes and a recent tax cut. The company is investing heavily in distribution networks, including refrigerated trucks and a database to track sales, aiming to reach up to 100,000 villages in the next three years. This strategic move aims to solidify Mondelez's dominant position in the burgeoning Indian confectionery market against competitors like Nestle SA and Hershey Co.

title: Africa’s Amazon Looks to Solve Addresses Problem With Vivo Tieup
summary: Jumia Technologies AG, often called Africa's Amazon, is partnering with Vivo Energy Plc to address the challenge of a lack of formal addresses for deliveries in less developed parts of Africa. Vivo Energy's 2,100+ Shell and Engen-branded service stations will serve as pick-up points for Jumia-bought goods, where customers can also pay. This collaboration aims to expand Jumia's reach, especially in remote areas, and boost Vivo's non-fuels business.

title: Gartner Says Worldwide IaaS Public Cloud Services Market Grew 31.3% in 2018
summary: The worldwide Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) market experienced significant growth in 2018, increasing by 31.3% to reach $32.4 billion. Amazon maintained its position as the leading vendor, followed by Microsoft, Alibaba, Google, and IBM, indicating a consolidation trend favoring major providers who can invest heavily in scalable data center infrastructure and offer a rich feature set.

title: Capital One Data Breach Impacts 106 Million Customers
summary: Capital One announced a massive data breach affecting 106 million customers and applicants in the U.S. and Canada, exposing personal details like names, social security numbers, and income. The alleged hacker, a former Amazon Web Services employee, has been arrested. Capital One is offering free credit monitoring and identity protection to those impacted, advising customers to monitor their accounts for suspicious activity.

title: Capital One Breach Shows a Bank Hacker Needs Just One Gap to Wreak Havoc (Published 2019)
summary: The Capital One data breach, which exposed the personal information of over 100 million people, highlights how a single vulnerability can be exploited by hackers despite robust cybersecurity measures. A former Amazon software engineer, Paige Thompson, allegedly gained access to Capital One's network through a "configuration vulnerability." This incident underscores the ongoing challenge financial institutions face in defending against persistent cyberattacks, needing only one lapse in security to succeed.

title: Paige Thompson, Suspect in Capital One Data Breach, Left a Trail Online (Published 2019)
summary: Paige Thompson, a 33-year-old software developer, was arrested for allegedly obtaining the personal data of over 100 million people from Capital One. Her extensive online presence, including social media posts and activity on developer platforms, created a digital trail that helped authorities track her down. Thompson had a history of software engineering jobs, including at Amazon Web Services.

title: About one million Canadian social insurance numbers compromised in Capital One data breach
summary: A massive data hack at Capital One Financial Corp. compromised the personal data of roughly six million Canadians and exposed one million social insurance numbers, making it one of Canada's largest security breaches. The incident, which also affected 100 million U.S. clients, led to the arrest of alleged hacker Paige A. Thompson. Capital One is notifying affected individuals and offering free credit monitoring and identity theft insurance.

title: Tractor Supply’s BOPIS strategy pays off in rural communities
summary: Tractor Supply's buy-online-pickup-in-store (BOPIS) strategy is proving highly successful in rural communities, with over 70% of online orders fulfilled in-store. This approach helps the company save on supply chain costs and boosts sales, particularly as rural customers often face challenges with fast and affordable last-mile delivery options. The strategy also positions Tractor Supply to compete effectively with e-commerce giants like Amazon in less densely populated areas.

title: Capital One shares dive after data breach affecting 100 million
summary: Capital One shares fell after the company disclosed a data breach affecting 100 million individuals, compromising Social Security numbers and bank account numbers for some customers. Analysts express concern over potential reputational damage and regulatory actions, with initial cost estimates for Capital One ranging from $100 million to $150 million. The FBI arrested a former Amazon Web Services employee in connection with the breach.

title: Former Amazon worker is accused in cloud hack of Capital One
summary: A former Amazon Web Services employee, Paige A. Thompson, has been accused of illegally accessing data from approximately 100 million U.S. Capital One customers and 6 million Canadian customers. The breach occurred due to a misconfigured firewall, Capital One stated, and the stolen data includes personal information, Social Security numbers, and bank account numbers. Capital One's stock fell following the announcement, and Thompson faces charges of computer fraud.

title: Capital One Data Theft Impacts 106M People
summary: Federal prosecutors charged a Seattle woman, Paige A. Thompson, with stealing data from over 100 million Capital One credit applications, impacting 106 million people in the U.S. and Canada. The breach exposed names, addresses, dates of birth, incomes, approximately 140,000 Social Security numbers, and 80,000 bank account numbers, although Capital One stated no credit card numbers or login credentials were compromised. The incident highlights misconfiguration issues in cloud platforms and the vulnerability of personal data, with Thompson allegedly discussing her activities on social media.

title: Capital One hack snags data on 106 million people — including 6 million in Canada
summary: A security breach at Capital One Financial compromised the personal information of about 106 million people, including 6 million in Canada, with some Social Security and bank account numbers obtained. The alleged hacker, Paige A. Thompson, was charged with computer fraud and abuse after federal agents tracked her online. Capital One's stock dipped six percent following the news, and the company plans to offer free credit monitoring to those affected by what is considered one of the largest security breaches of a major U.S. financial institution on record.

title: Capital One Reports Data Breach Affecting 100 Million Customers, Applicants
summary: Capital One Financial Corp., the fifth-largest U.S. credit-card issuer, reported a data breach affecting approximately 106 million customers and applicants. A former Amazon Web Services employee, Paige A. Thompson, has been arrested in connection with the hack. The incident is considered one of the largest-ever data breaches for a major bank.

title: A hacker gained access to 100 million Capital One credit card applications and accounts
summary: A hacker gained access to over 100 million Capital One customer accounts and credit card applications, exposing sensitive personal and financial data. The suspect, Paige Thompson, a former Amazon Web Services software engineer, was arrested and accused of exploiting a misconfigured web application firewall. Capital One estimates the breach will cost between $100 million and $150 million and is offering free credit monitoring to affected individuals.

title: Netflix is not a tech company
summary: Benedict Evans argues that Netflix, despite its reliance on technology, is fundamentally a TV company, much like Sky was in its time. He uses "technology as a crowbar" as a metaphor to explain how companies leverage tech to disrupt traditional industries, but their core business remains within that industry. The article emphasizes that for Netflix, the critical questions are "TV questions" related to content, rights, and industry dynamics, rather than "tech questions" typical of Silicon Valley.

title: Capital One touted the data cloud’s safety. Then a hacker breached it
summary: Capital One, a prominent advocate for cloud-based data storage, experienced a significant data breach affecting over 100 million customers. The incident, which involved a former Amazon Web Services employee exploiting a misconfigured firewall, has raised concerns about the security of financial data in the cloud despite Capital One's assertions of its safety and benefits. The breach is expected to cost Capital One between $100 million and $150 million, primarily for credit monitoring and legal support.

title: The Capital One breach was preventable, experts say. Here’s what to do now.
summary: Cybersecurity experts suggest that the Capital One data breach, which exposed over 100 million people's personal information, was preventable due to a misconfigured firewall. Former Seattle software engineer Paige Thompson was arrested after boasting about the data theft, which Capital One estimates will cost between $100 million and $150 million. The incident highlights concerns about cloud security, human error, and the transparency of companies in communicating breaches to affected customers.

title: Stock of the week: United Parcel Service
summary: United Parcel Service (UPS) recently experienced significant stock gains following a strong second-quarter 2019 earnings report, driven by better-than-expected performance and increased sales and profits. The company's ongoing transformation process, focusing on automation and increased sorting/shipping capacity, is showing positive results, helping to improve margins and mitigate risks from a slowing global economy. Despite being a cyclical business susceptible to trade issues, UPS's dividend yield and strategic investments in e-commerce infrastructure position it well for future growth.

title: Kroger Is Upping Its Advertising Game
summary: Kroger, the nation's second-largest food retailer, has hired global advertising agency DDB as its creative "agency of record" to burnish its brand identity and enhance its consumer-experience focus. This move aims to drive more customers to choose Kroger across its stores and online, especially as part of its "Restock Kroger" initiative, which focuses on technology and omnichannel experiences. The company is investing in digital sales, aiming for $9 billion in annual returns, and exploring innovations like driverless car deliveries, while facing challenges with its diverse brand portfolio and the cost-effectiveness of online grocery shopping.

title: Could Amazon Lose the Pentagon JEDI Project?
summary: The Pentagon's new Secretary of Defense Mike Esper announced a review of the bidding process for the $10 billion JEDI cloud computing contract, raising concerns for Amazon. This review follows protests from Oracle and IBM, as well as doubts expressed by President Trump about the competitive bidding process. The news caused Amazon's stock to slide, highlighting the significance of the contract and the political scrutiny surrounding it.

title: IBM fired as many as 1,00,000 employees in recent years to make itself look 'cool' and 'trendy', finds lawsuit
