summary: IBM has reportedly fired as many as 100,000 employees in recent years to appear "cool" and "trendy" to millennials, according to a former vice president's deposition in an age discrimination lawsuit. The company, facing multiple lawsuits, aimed to shed its "old fuddy-duddy organization" image to better compete with companies like Amazon and Google. This strategy involved deliberately targeting older workers through rolling layoffs to "correct its seniority mix."

title: IBM fired at least 1,00,000 in recent years to appear 'cool' and 'trendy', lawsuit shows
summary: A former vice president of human resources for IBM testified in an age discrimination lawsuit that the company fired between 50,000 to 100,000 employees in recent years to appear "cool" and "trendy" to millennials, similar to Amazon and Google. This strategy involved targeting older workers through rolling layoffs to "correct" its seniority mix. IBM has faced several lawsuits regarding age discrimination and has seen a 19% reduction in its global workforce since 2013, coinciding with nearly seven years of shrinking revenue.

title: How the Accused Capital One Hacker Stole Reams of Data From the Cloud
summary: Paige Thompson, a former Amazon.com cloud-computing employee, is accused of stealing 106 million Capital One Financial records by exploiting a known cloud vulnerability. This incident highlights ongoing concerns among cybersecurity professionals about the security of cloud-based data. The alleged data theft represents one of the largest bank-data heists in history.

title: U.S. Senator Sends Letter to Amazon CEO on Capital One Hack
summary: Senator Ron Wyden has sent a letter to Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos requesting details about the security of Amazon's cloud service, which was implicated in the recent Capital One hack. The hack involved the theft of 106 million credit-card records stored on Amazon's cloud. This inquiry comes amidst one of the largest bank-data thefts ever recorded.

title: Murphy USA's Loyalty Program Converts 2M Customers to Full Membership
summary: Murphy USA's new loyalty program, Murphy Drive Rewards (MDR), has successfully converted 2.2 million customers to full membership since its national launch in March. President and CEO Andrew Clyde highlighted that the program is driving customer traffic and showing encouraging behavioral changes among loyal customers, with 500,000 new participants joining monthly. The company plans to convert the 7 million non-member participants, seeing significant upside in engaging them.

title: Largest US Beauty Retailer Signs Lease with Largest NYC Landlord
summary: SL Green Realty has signed Ulta Beauty Inc. to a 12,040-square-foot retail space at 2 Herald Square, a prime location in New York City. This deal brings the largest U.S. beauty retailer to a highly trafficked area and fully leases the retail portion of the property, which SL Green recapitalized after acquiring its leasehold interest in 2018. The move underscores the importance of brick-and-mortar presence in key urban markets.

title: Capital One data breach: The main takeaway for consumers
summary: The Capital One data breach, affecting over 106 million customers, highlights the critical need for consumers to actively monitor and protect their financial information. Experts advise regular transaction monitoring, varied passwords, security questions, and suspicious activity alerts to prevent personal financial crises. While consumers have a role, companies are ultimately responsible for data protection and implementing robust cybersecurity measures to prevent such breaches.

title: IBM laid off up to 100,000 workers, Austin man's lawsuit claims
summary: An Austin man's lawsuit claims IBM laid off up to 100,000 workers in recent years, alleging age discrimination. Jonathan Langley, a 60-year-old former cloud salesman, contends he was forced out due to his age as IBM sought to rebrand as a "millennial-centric tech company." This lawsuit is one of several accusing IBM of firing older workers, with reports indicating significant reductions in its global workforce targeting older employees.

title: XPO still working to make up for loss of largest customer
summary: XPO Logistics is still working to recover from the loss of its largest customer, believed to be Amazon, which downsized its operations with XPO in Q4 2018. Despite the impact on revenue growth and the postal injection business, XPO is making progress in replacing lost revenue and is optimistic about growth driven by new technology investments like XPO Smart and XPO Connect. The company also faces challenges from a sluggish freight market but anticipates significant profit growth from its tech initiatives.

title: Future Looks Bright For Decline of Retail Store ETF
summary: The article discusses the increasing challenges faced by traditional retailers due to the growth of online shopping, leading to store closures. It highlights how these trends could benefit the ProShares Decline of the Retail Store ETF (NYSEArca: EMTY), which provides short exposure to traditional retailers. EMTY's strong year-to-date performance is noted, reflecting the continued decline in brick-and-mortar retail and the shift towards e-commerce.

title: FedEx terminates ground delivery of Amazon packages in US
summary: FedEx announced it will not renew its ground-delivery contract with Amazon when it expires at the end of August, further cutting ties with the e-commerce giant which is also a competitor in the logistics sector. This decision follows an earlier move where FedEx's Express unit stopped flying Amazon's packages in the U.S. FedEx states this move aligns with its strategy to focus on the broader e-commerce market, while Amazon continues to build its own extensive logistics network.

title: Mercer Mega Block sale could haul in $143.5 million for city of Seattle
summary: The city of Seattle is negotiating the sale of the Mercer Mega Block for $143.5 million to Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc. The deal, if approved, would allocate nearly $80 million to affordable housing efforts, $5 million to homelessness services, and $25 million to transportation projects. The developer plans to build a life sciences campus, a community center, and 175 units of affordable housing on the 3-acre South Lake Union site.

title: FedEx Amazon contract for ground delivery won't be renewed, FedEx says
summary: FedEx announced it will not renew its ground delivery contract with Amazon, effective at the end of August, citing Amazon's growing internal delivery network as a direct competitor. This decision follows a previous termination of their air delivery contract, though FedEx will continue some international Amazon package deliveries. FedEx stated that Amazon constituted only 1.3% of its total revenue in 2018, or approximately $850 million, and that the e-commerce landscape is shifting with increased priority from retailers like Walmart and Target.

title: Altice partners with Devialet for Alexa speaker that can control your TV box
summary: Altice USA has partnered with French audio brand Devialet to launch its first smart speaker, the Altice Amplify. This Alexa-enabled speaker offers hands-free voice control of the Altice One TV platform in addition to standard smart speaker features. The Altice Amplify will be available later this year, priced at $399 for Altice customers and $499 for non-customers.

title: PepsiCo Executive to Become UPS Finance Chief
summary: United Parcel Service Inc. has appointed Brian Newman, a PepsiCo executive, as its new chief financial officer, effective September 16. Newman will succeed Richard Peretz, who is set to retire at the end of the year. This move comes as UPS aims to capitalize on the strained relationship between FedEx and Amazon and reflects a broader management strategy to bring in outside talent for change.

title: Netflix Global Real Estate Grab: How the Streamer Is Expanding From London to Singapore
summary: Netflix is rapidly expanding its physical presence globally through significant investments in studio facilities and high-end office spaces. The company has acquired or leased properties in major cities worldwide, including Toronto, London, Mexico City, New York, Mumbai, Singapore, and Seoul, to support its booming content production and growing employee base. This expansion reflects a strategic move to establish localized hubs for content creation and corporate operations.

title: Residence Inn next to Amazon’s future HQ sells for $99 million
summary: Host Hotels & Resorts has sold The Residence Inn Arlington Pentagon City for US$99.1 million to an LLC registered to Blackstone’s headquarters. The 23-year-old, 299-key extended stay hotel is adjacent to Amazon’s future HQ and underwent renovation in 2012. This sale is part of Host's strategy to divest properties and buy back its own shares, having sold $609 million in hotel properties in 2019 so far.

title: Postmates cleared for robot deliveries in SF — Marble wants in, too
summary: Postmates has received a permit to begin testing its autonomous delivery rover, Serve, in a limited capacity in San Francisco. The permit allows for testing only three robots at a time in specific industrial areas, at low speeds, and with a human escort within 30 feet. Another robot-delivery company, Marble, has also applied for a permit, indicating a growing interest in autonomous delivery despite past regulatory hurdles in the city.

title: Paycom No. 6 on Fortune’s list of fastest-growing companies
summary: Paycom Software Inc., a provider of cloud-based human capital management software, has been ranked No. 6 on Fortune magazine’s 2019 100 Fastest-growing Companies list. The Oklahoma City-based company, which is the only human capital management provider on the list, also saw its CEO, Chad Richison, recognized among Glassdoor's Top 100 CEOs for 2019. Paycom's strong performance was driven by significant revenue growth, a high employee approval rating, and positive business outlook among its staff.

title: Target CEO Brian Cornell sees turnaround as 'still in early innings'
summary: Target CEO Brian Cornell reflects on his five years leading the company's turnaround, comparing it to the 1969 Mets' Cinderella season. He acknowledges the significant progress made, transforming Target from a struggling retailer into one with robust sales growth and rising traffic, despite initial skepticism from Wall Street. Cornell emphasizes a measured, "go slow to go fast" approach, focusing on store remodels, private-label brands, new services, and a more externally focused leadership team while acknowledging ongoing challenges from competitors and economic factors.

title: Big health plans pledge to look beyond shareholders. Critics aren’t so sure
summary: Major health plans, including CVS Health, Anthem, and Cigna, have signed a Business Roundtable statement indicating a shift from prioritizing only shareholders to considering all stakeholders. However, critics and political figures like Sen. Elizabeth Warren remain skeptical, calling for concrete actions. Kaiser Permanente CEO Bernard Tyson declined to sign, stating that as a non-profit, Kaiser does not have shareholders to prioritize.

title: Costco Children's Golf Classic brings in record sum, country star brings down the house
summary: The Friends of Costco Guild's 20th annual Children’s Golf Classic achieved a record sum. The three-day event, starting August 17, included a VIP party, dinner with entertainment, and a golf tournament across nine local courses. The article highlights the success of this long-standing charity event.

title: Data-Center Market Is Booming Amid Shift to Cloud
summary: The data-center market is experiencing a boom driven by the shift to cloud computing, even as many businesses shed their own facilities. This trend is leading to increased deals and consolidation among data-center landlords and cloud providers as they seek more capacity. Companies like Amazon.com Inc. and Microsoft Corp. are major drivers of this demand for co-location services.

title: Mystery new Sonos Move could be company’s first portable Bluetooth speaker
summary: Sonos is expected to launch its first portable Bluetooth speaker, named the Move, designed to work both within a home Wi-Fi network and as a standalone Bluetooth device. The speaker will feature Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Apple AirPlay 2, and voice control via Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant, along with an Auto Trueplay feature for automatic sound tuning. It will be battery-powered with a charging dock and a USB-C port, marking a significant expansion for Sonos into portable audio.

title: Apple, JPMorgan CEOs Say Companies Must Serve More Than Shareholders
summary: 181 CEOs of major public companies, including Apple, JPMorgan Chase, and Walmart, have declared their companies' purpose extends beyond just shareholders to include all stakeholders like customers, employees, and communities. This new stance, articulated by the Business Roundtable, signifies a shift away from the "shareholder primacy" theory that has guided corporate governance for decades, reflecting growing public and generational expectations for corporate responsibility. The declaration suggests that capitalism, when adjusted, can be a force for broader societal good.

title: Corsair unveils $100 K57 RGB Wireless gaming keyboard with Slipstream tech
summary: Corsair has unveiled its new K57 RGB Wireless gaming keyboard, priced at $100, featuring sub-1ms wireless connectivity via Slipstream tech or Bluetooth 4.2. It boasts 35-hour battery life with RGB LEDs enabled, quiet rubber dome switches with 8-key roll-over, and customizable macro keys, making it a compelling option for gamers. The keyboard also incorporates CAPELLIX LEDs for brighter illumination and less power consumption.

title: Tom Lydon on Varney & Co: Hot Online Retail ETFs
summary: ETF Trends CEO Tom Lydon appeared on Fox Business Network's "Varney & Co." to discuss online retail ETFs, highlighting the decline of big-box retailers and the rise of online sales. He introduced ETFs like ProShares Decline of the Retail Store ETF (EMTY) and ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN), as well as ProShares Long Online/Short Stores ETF (CLIX) for a combined strategy. The article also touches on mixed Q2 earnings for Home Depot and Kohl's, despite the general downturn in traditional retail.

title: Ubiquiti UniFi Review
summary: This article reviews the Ubiquiti UniFi networking system, highlighting its flexibility and user-friendly management through the UniFi Controller. It details the setup, performance, and build quality of the UniFi Security Gateway (USG), Switch 8 150W, and UniFi nanoHD access point, concluding that it's a powerful solution for those serious about their home network.

title: Arbitrator denies Atlas Air’s pilots bid to negotiate; imposes arbitrated settlement
summary: An arbitrator denied Atlas Air pilots' request to negotiate their next contract, instead imposing an arbitrated settlement, a legal victory for Atlas Air Worldwide Holdings, Inc. The decision means the pilots will not be able to vote on or ratify the contract. The union has vowed to pursue all legal options to avoid an arbitrated contract, while pilots argue they are underpaid and their previous concession promises were not kept.

title: Crowds force Costco to shut 1st China store early on opening day
summary: Costco's first store in China, located in Shanghai, was forced to close early on its opening day due to overwhelming crowds and resulting traffic jams. Videos showed thousands of people in the aisles, and local authorities advised residents to shop during off-peak hours for safety. This event occurred as other Western retailers have struggled to gain market share in China against strong local competition.

title: Red Hat CEO Says Acquisition by IBM Will Help Spur More Open-Source Innovation
summary: Red Hat CEO Jim Whitehurst stated that IBM's acquisition of Red Hat will foster more open-source innovation, emphasizing a collaborative "two cultures working together" approach. The acquisition aims to strengthen IBM's cloud business by enabling customers to use Red Hat's open-source software across various cloud providers, including IBM's own cloud, AWS, and Microsoft Azure. Red Hat's technology helps CIOs run applications both in their own data centers and across third-party cloud services, enhancing flexibility and reducing risk.

title: Crocs Are Cool. Yes, Really.
summary: This article argues that despite divided opinions on their appearance, Crocs are an attractive investment due to their increasing popularity and strong sales performance. The author highlights that Crocs are in vogue, with rising search interest and high rankings among best-selling shoes on Amazon.

title: The age of disloyalty: most Singaporean shoppers open to new brands
summary: A new study reveals that brand loyalty is low among Singaporean shoppers, with 78% willing to consider new brands, especially for groceries and apparel. The Criteo S.A. Why We Buy survey found that consumers value good value and wide product selection over traditional loyalty programs. The study emphasizes that brands need to appeal beyond low prices and loyalty points by focusing on brand values and personalized online ads due to Singapore's high internet connectivity.

title: HPE Takes VMware Cloud Users On Its Synergy Journey To Greenlake
summary: HPE is expanding its GreenLake cloud-like IT consumption model by partnering with VMware to integrate GreenLake and HPE Synergy with VMware Cloud Foundation. This collaboration allows joint customers to run VMware Cloud Foundation as a service on GreenLake, offering a cloud-like experience with greater flexibility and cost efficiency in their own datacenters. The initiative is part of HPE's ambitious plan to deliver its entire portfolio as a service by 2022, leveraging GreenLake's metering and capacity management capabilities to optimize IT environments.

title: Gartner Identifies Four Emerging Trends That Will Transform How Marketers Run Their Technology Ecosystems
summary: Gartner has identified four emerging trends in its Hype Cycle for Digital Marketing and Advertising 2019 report that are set to transform how marketers manage their technology ecosystems: Customer Data Platforms (CDPs), AI for Marketing, Blockchain for Advertising, and Real-time Marketing. These technologies are expected to have a significant impact on delivering meaningful customer experiences and driving business value. The report details the current state and future implications of each trend, highlighting ongoing challenges and opportunities for marketers.

title: Click, drive, pick up. Target takes drive-up service nationwide
summary: Target is expanding its drive-up service nationwide, allowing customers to order online and pick up purchases at nearly 1,750 stores across all 50 states. This expansion aims to enhance convenience for shoppers, a strategy increasingly adopted by retailers to compete with Amazon. The service typically allows customers to have their orders brought to their cars within two minutes of arrival.

title: WPP forges closer links to big tech with launch of San Francisco campus
summary: WPP is opening a new campus in San Francisco to better serve major tech clients like Google, Facebook, and Amazon, and to foster collaboration between its agencies and tech platforms. This move is part of CEO Mark Read's three-year turnaround plan, aiming to transform WPP into a "creative transformation company" and address declining sales in key markets. The campus, which will house over 1000 people, is expected to be operational in the third quarter of 2021.

title: DOD awards $7.6B Microsoft Office 365 cloud contract to General Dynamics and partners
summary: The U.S. Defense Department has awarded a $7.6 billion, 10-year contract to General Dynamics Corp. subsidiary CSRA LLC, in partnership with Dell Technologies Inc. and Minburn Technology Group LLC, to standardize its email and collaboration workflows on Microsoft's Office 365. This Defense Enterprise Office Solutions (DEOS) program aims to migrate 1.5 million users to Office 365, with an initial focus on moving personnel off the aging Defense Enterprise Email system. The contract also highlights the requirement for Impact Level 6 certification for Secret-level data, which Microsoft is reportedly still obtaining, using its recently authorized Azure cloud regions.

title: BlackRock in Amazon: ‘World’s largest investor in deforestation’
summary: A report by Friends of the Earth US, Amazon Watch, and Profundo labels BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, as the "world's largest investor in deforestation" due to its extensive investments in companies linked to the destruction of forests in Brazil. The report highlights BlackRock's increased holdings in high-risk sectors such as soy, beef, palm oil, rubber, timber, and pulp/paper, despite the company's commitment to engaging with firms on sustainability. Critics argue that BlackRock's passive investment strategies and reliance on the ESG industry's data fail to adequately address deforestation risks.

title: Why Big Companies Are Thinking Like Startups
summary: Large corporations like JPMorgan Chase are adopting startup methodologies to foster innovation and maintain competitiveness in a rapidly changing market. This involves minimizing waste, maximizing customer value, embracing Agile development, and implementing a "three horizons" framework for innovation, with a focus on continuous customer feedback. These strategies aim to accelerate product development and deliver value faster, much like their smaller, more nimble counterparts.

title: Groceries And Gadgets: The Robots Coming To A Supermarket Near You
summary: This article discusses the increasing presence of robots in supermarkets like Walmart and Stop & Shop, used for tasks such as inventory monitoring, cleaning spills, and unloading trucks. The implementation of these robots raises questions about their impact on labor, with companies like Walmart stating they aim to reallocate employees to customer-focused roles rather than replacing them entirely. Union representatives and technology developers weigh in on the implications of this automation for workers and efficiency in the retail industry.

title: If you invested $1,000 in eBay 10 years ago, here's how much you'd have now
summary: A $1,000 investment in eBay 10 years ago would now be worth over $4,500, representing a 350% return, significantly outperforming the S&P 500 during the same period. The article discusses eBay's evolution from an auction site, its split from PayPal, and its future plans, while also noting PayPal's stronger stock performance since the separation. It concludes with general investment advice about index funds.

title: PD - PagerDuty Announces Second Quarter Fiscal Year 2020 Financial Results
summary: PagerDuty announced strong second quarter fiscal year 2020 financial results, with revenue increasing 45% year-over-year to a record $40.4 million. The company reported over 12,000 customers and highlighted best-in-class gross margins of 85%. PagerDuty also provided financial outlooks for the third quarter and full fiscal year 2020, projecting continued revenue growth and non-GAAP net loss per share.

title: Alibaba has bought a $700m stake in giant music streamer Netease
summary: Alibaba Group has invested approximately $700 million to acquire a minority stake in NetEase Cloud Music, one of China's largest music streaming services. This move strengthens the relationship between the two companies, with NetEase Inc. remaining the majority shareholder. Alibaba also acquired NetEase's e-commerce platform Kaola for $2 billion, integrating it into Tmall while allowing Kaola to operate independently.

title: Apple Inc. v. Pepper: A Case to Watch for Commissions-Based Retailers Selling Directly to Consumers
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled in *Apple Inc. v. Pepper* that consumers could sue Apple for antitrust violations related to its App Store, specifically regarding the 30 percent commission imposed on developers. This decision allows direct purchaser suits against monopolistic retailers using commissions, impacting not just Apple but also other major online marketplaces like eBay, Etsy, Amazon, Jet, Walmart, and Newegg. The article highlights the significant implications for commissions-based retailers selling directly to consumers.

title: Technology firms vie for billions in data-analytics contracts
summary: The article discusses the booming data-analytics market, highlighting companies like C3.ai and Databricks that are vying for billions in contracts. It details the journey of C3.ai's founder, Tom Siebel, and the industry's potential to revolutionize business productivity, despite current challenges in implementing truly sophisticated AI platforms. The piece also notes the significant financial valuations and growth projections for the data analytics sector.

title: We toured an Amazon fulfillment center. Here's what we saw.
summary: The article details a tour of an Amazon fulfillment center, highlighting the extensive use of robots and Amazon's significant presence with over 3,000 employees in its 1-million-square-foot facility. It implies an observation of Amazon's operational scale and technological integration.

title: Amazon Brings Prime Program to Brazil to Outflank Local Rivals
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is launching its Prime membership program in Brazil to gain market share against local competitors like MercadoLibre Inc. and B2W Cia. Digital. The service will offer free unlimited shipping for approximately 500,000 products, two-day shipping in 90 cities, and include entertainment perks like Amazon Music and Prime Video. This expansion marks Brazil as the 19th country to offer Amazon's Prime program, underscoring Amazon's long-term investment strategy in growing e-commerce markets.

title: Integral Ad Science Turns Over Entire Senior Leadership Team
summary: Integral Ad Science (IAS) has seen a near-complete turnover of its senior leadership team since Lisa Utzschneider became CEO in January and Vista Equity Partners acquired the company. Eighteen new executives have been hired, and 15 have left, signaling a strategic shift to scale the company and focus on new areas like OTT/CTV. The new hires are younger, more diverse, and less likely to have advanced degrees compared to their predecessors, reflecting a shift in hiring practices influenced by Vista Equity Partners' playbook.

title: HEINZ Achieves the Impossible With Launch of New HEINZ Tomato Ketchup With a Blend of Veggies
summary: HEINZ has launched a new Tomato Ketchup with a Blend of Veggies, incorporating carrots and butternut squash to offer parents a way to include more vegetables in their children's diets without compromising the classic HEINZ taste. This new product contains 25% added veggies and 25% less sugar than regular HEINZ Tomato Ketchup, making it a healthier option for families. It is available in 20 oz. and 31 oz. squeeze bottles at select retailers and online, supported by a comprehensive marketing campaign.

title: Purpose At Work: Why VF Corp Boycotts Brazilian Leather As Amazon Burns
summary: VF Corporation, which owns brands like Vans and The North Face, has severed ties with Brazilian leather suppliers due to the Amazon fires. This decision aims to avoid contributing to environmental harm and signals to the Brazilian government and industry the importance of environmental action. The article highlights how VF Corp's purpose-driven business strategy sets an example for other companies to operate through the lenses of both purpose and profit.

title: SPS Commerce Acquires Mapadoc For $11.5 Million
summary: SPS Commerce has acquired the Mapadoc EDI division of SWK Technologies for $11.5 million in cash. The acquisition strengthens SPS Commerce's position in cloud-based supply-chain software, giving Mapadoc customers access to SPS's retail trading network and other applications. SWK Technologies plans to use the sale proceeds to accelerate its growth strategies centered on SMB digital transformation.

title: Why Markets Think Trump Tariffs Will Help Apple and Hurt Amazon
summary: This article explores why markets believe tariffs will impact Apple positively and Amazon negatively. It highlights Apple's strong embedded position within the Chinese economy, suggesting that China needs Apple as much, if not more, than Apple needs China, thus incentivizing protection from tariffs. Conversely, Amazon's business model, heavily reliant on Chinese-made goods without a similar indispensable role in China's economy, makes it vulnerable to tariff impacts.

title: HeartFlow Announces FDA Clearance for HeartFlow Planner
summary: HeartFlow Inc. has received FDA clearance for its HeartFlow Planner, a non-invasive, real-time virtual modeling tool designed for coronary artery disease (CAD) intervention. This new interactive tool allows interventional cardiologists to model various treatment strategies and explore clinical scenarios before catheterization lab procedures. The HeartFlow Planner utilizes patient CTA data to create personalized 3-D models and simulate blood flow to help determine optimal treatment courses.

title: Russia’s Largest Social Network Starts Dating App to Rival Tinder
summary: VKontakte, Russia's largest social network, has launched a new dating app called Lovina, which focuses on quick-fire video chats to compete with established dating apps like Tinder. The app aims to provide a more authentic and safer dating experience by using video and artificial intelligence to screen for explicit content, while maintaining user privacy. Lovina will be free to use, generating revenue through in-app purchases for profile promotion and access to expanded features.

title: Target 20 Years of Design for All anniversary collection brings back 20 designers Saturday
summary: Target is celebrating 20 years of designer partnerships by bringing back a collection of nearly 300 popular items from 20 designers, including Missoni and Lilly Pulitzer. The "20th Anniversary Collection" goes on sale Saturday, offering a second chance for shoppers to purchase discounted designer items. Shoppers are advised to prepare for high demand, as previous collaborations have sold out quickly and appeared on eBay at marked-up prices.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper launches new line of coffee makers
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper has launched the K-Duo portfolio, a new line of coffee makers that combine single-serve and drip coffee functionality. These brewers offer convenience and versatility by allowing users to brew a single cup with K-Cup pods or a full carafe of drip coffee. The portfolio includes three models with varying features and price points, catering to different consumer needs and occasions.

title: Kaspi.kz CEO Mikhail LOMTADZE: KASPI.KZ TO HOLD IPO ON THE LONDON STOCK EXCHANGE IN 4TH QUARTER 2019
summary: Kaspi.kz CEO Mikhail Lomtadze announced the company's plans to hold an IPO on the London Stock Exchange in the fourth quarter of 2019. The IPO aims to introduce Kazakhstan's innovative technology company to international investors and support its expansion beyond Kazakhstan, particularly into Azerbaijan and other Central Asian/Caucasus markets. Kaspi.kz, already well-capitalized, views the IPO as a strategic move to boost its development strategy and international recognition, rather than to raise additional capital for its current operations.

title: How Jeff Bezos almost bought Netflix for about $15 million
summary: This article recounts Netflix co-founder Marc Randolph's meeting with Jeff Bezos in 1998 regarding a potential acquisition of Netflix by Amazon for approximately $15 million. During the meeting, Randolph and Bezos bonded over their companies' early launch experiences, while Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings showed impatience, eager to discuss the business proposition. The excerpt highlights the contrasting personalities and priorities during these early discussions.

title: Massive store closures are a strategy, not a sign of a ‘retail apocalypse,’ experts say
summary: Experts suggest that widespread store closures are a strategic repositioning of the retail industry rather than a sign of a "retail apocalypse." David Berliner of BDO views these closures as a "survival of the fittest" scenario, indicating a necessary evolution for retailers. He emphasizes that retail is not dying but adapting to new market realities.

title: Gap Inc. Kicked off NY Fashion Week with Celebration of Inclusion
summary: Gap Inc. celebrated inclusion by kicking off New York Fashion Week with Harlem's Fashion Row, highlighting Black fashion designers and expanding diverse talent recruitment. The event featured discussions with industry leaders and designers of color, emphasizing innovation and the company's commitment to equality. Gap Inc. also signed the "Open to All" pledge, reinforcing its long-standing values of diversity and inclusion, and was ranked among the top ten most diverse companies by Refinitiv's Diversity and Inclusion Index.

title: Canal de Las Estrellas de Televisa ya no será gratis en internet... ¡¿Y las comedias?!
summary: Televisa's Canal de Las Estrellas will no longer be free to stream online starting October 2. Viewers will need to subscribe to either Blim TV or Izzi to access the content. This change is a response to the intense competition in the streaming service market.

title: Blackstone CEO Steve Schwarzman on Bitcoin: “I Was Raised in a World Where Someone Needs to Control Currencies”
summary: Blackstone CEO Steve Schwarzman discusses his views on Bitcoin, artificial intelligence, and investment strategies in an interview with Fortune. He expresses skepticism about cryptocurrencies due to the lack of central control and potential for illicit activities but views blockchain technology favorably for other applications. Schwarzman also highlights AI as a major growth area and discusses the ethical challenges associated with technological advancements.

title: Sally Beauty announces private label credit card
summary: Sally Beauty Holdings announced a new private label credit card program for its Sally Beauty Supply and Beauty Systems Group stores, in partnership with Alliance Data. This initiative aims to enhance its existing loyalty program, which boasts over 15 million members, and is expected to pilot in Q2 fiscal year 2020. The move positions Sally Beauty to compete with rivals like Ulta and Sephora, and also to counter Amazon's recent entry into the professional beauty market.

title: Comcast gives away Xfinity Flex TV device, pounding shares of Roku
summary: Comcast announced it will offer its Xfinity Flex streaming media set-top box for free to internet customers, intensifying competition with Roku Inc. This move caused Roku's stock to tumble nearly 14% as investors reacted to the increased competition from a major player like Comcast, alongside existing rivals Amazon, Apple, and Google. The Xfinity Flex aims to simplify the streaming experience by offering access to various services and free content.

title: Amazon’s order of 100,000 Rivian vans signals the automaker is ‘for real’
summary: Amazon's order of 100,000 electric vans from Rivian, led by a $700-million investment, signals the electric vehicle startup's significant emergence in the automotive industry. This massive pre-production order provides Rivian with a major customer ahead of its consumer vehicle launches and validates its potential as a serious automaker, according to analysts. The custom-built vans will be used for Amazon Prime deliveries, starting in 2021, and will share key components with Rivian's R1T pickup and R1S SUV.

title: Amazon is purchasing 100,000 Rivian electric vans, the largest order of EV delivery vehicles ever
summary: Amazon has placed an order for 100,000 electric delivery vehicles from Rivian Automotive, marking the largest order of EV delivery vehicles to date. This move is part of Amazon's broader plan to transition its fleet to run entirely on renewable energy by 2030, with prototypes expected on the road next year and 10,000 vehicles by late 2022. Despite the massive order, Rivian states it will not impact the production rollout of its R1T pickup and R1S SUV in late 2020.

title: Blockbuster Could Have Bought Netflix for $50 Million, but the CEO Thought It Was a Joke
summary: The article recounts a pivotal 2000 meeting where Netflix co-founders offered to sell their company to Blockbuster for $50 million. Blockbuster CEO John Antioco rejected the offer, dismissing Netflix's business model as unsustainable. This decision ultimately contributed to Blockbuster's demise and Netflix's rise.

title: Netflix Stock Drops After CEO Acknowledges ‘Tough Competition’ Coming From Disney, Apple
summary: Netflix's stock dropped significantly after CEO Reed Hastings acknowledged the upcoming "tough competition" from Disney Plus and Apple TV Plus. Investors were unnerved by his comments, despite Netflix having previously addressed the increased competitive intensity in the streaming sector. An analyst, however, predicted a rebound for Netflix's stock, arguing that new entrants won't necessarily steal existing subscribers.

title: Walmart to Stop E-cigarette Sales in US Stores, Company Memo Says
summary: Walmart announced it will stop selling e-cigarettes and electronic nicotine delivery products in its U.S. stores due to growing regulatory complexity and uncertainty. The decision follows bans on flavored vaping products in several states and federal plans to remove all flavored e-cigarettes from shelves amidst concerns about youth nicotine addiction and vaping-related lung disease. Walmart will exit the category after selling through its current inventory.

title: Avantis U.S. Equity ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:AVUS)
summary: The Avantis U.S. Equity ETF (AVUS) is an exchange-traded fund that tracks the Russell 3000 index, launched on September 24, 2019, and managed by American Century Investments. It features a diversified portfolio of US equities with a bias towards smaller, more profitable, or value companies. As of January 9, 2026, AVUS was trading at $115.05, with $10.80 billion in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 0.15%.

title: Netflix Stock Breaks Down as Competition Heats Up
summary: Netflix stock fell following increased competition from Apple and Disney, causing CEO Reed Hastings to emphasize the company's core strategy of in-house content. Despite concerns about subscriber misses, an analyst suggests that the broader trend of shifting to streaming will outweigh competitive headwinds. Technically, the stock is showing bearish indicators and could see further decline, with its next earnings report due on October 15, 2019.

title: International Coffee Day 2019: 89 Percent of Americans Get their Cup of Joe from Home
summary: A new survey by Reddi-wip, a Conagra Brands product, reveals that 89% of Americans get their coffee from home, citing convenience, cost, and customization as key reasons. To cater to this trend, Reddi-wip is launching a new Barista line of cream-based products, Nitro Creamer and Sweet Foam, designed to offer a coffeehouse experience at home. The survey also highlights that 79% of Americans prefer coffee with add-ins and many look forward to their morning coffee ritual.

title: Amazon buys cloud startup INLT to help merchants import goods
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has acquired cloud startup INLT for an undisclosed amount to help merchants on its online marketplace more easily import goods into the United States. INLT provides software for sellers to manage costs and customs clearance for cross-border shipments, and Amazon plans to offer this technology to its merchants to simplify international sales processes.

title: EBay CEO steps down amid ongoing operating review
summary: EBay Inc. CEO Devin Wenig is stepping down amidst an ongoing operating review, with CFO Scott Schenkel appointed as interim CEO. Wenig, who took over after the PayPal split in 2015, had been under pressure from activist investors to spin off businesses. Despite efforts to modernize EBay and use AI, the company struggled to keep pace with Amazon's growth.

title: Netflix stock turns negative for 2019, but trader sees another big drop ahead
summary: Netflix stock has turned negative for 2019, with one trader predicting a further significant drop due to a lack of support on the charts until $231. This decline is attributed to increasing streaming competition and a recent decrease in subscriber numbers, leading analysts to advise investors to stay away from the stock for the near future.

title: McDonald’s uses Alexa and Google to help with hiring
summary: McDonald's is implementing a new voice-activated job application system using Amazon's Alexa and Google Assistant to streamline hiring. This initiative, dubbed McDonald’s Apply Thru, allows job seekers to start applications through voice commands and is part of a broader technology push by the company to attract employees in a tight job market. The feature is available in multiple countries and aims to help McDonald's fill constant staffing needs across its 38,000 restaurants worldwide.

title: EBay CEO Devin Wenig, at odds with the board, steps down
summary: EBay Inc. CEO Devin Wenig has stepped down amidst pressure from activist investors seeking to break up the company. Scott Schenkel, EBay's CFO, has been appointed interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent replacement. Wenig's departure follows his failure to significantly grow EBay’s marketplace and clashes with the board over the sale of classifieds businesses.

title: EBay CEO resigns as company considers selling assets
summary: EBay CEO Devin Wenig has resigned from his position as the San Jose-based e-commerce company considers selling some of its assets. An interim leader has been appointed following Wenig's departure.

title: Singapore leads in cloud tech
summary: Singapore is leading the cloud computing adoption in Southeast Asia, driven by its advanced digital infrastructure, government support, and high demand for skilled professionals. Despite its leadership, the country faces challenges with cybersecurity, as many firms struggle to keep pace with rapid cloud expansion and data security threats like those leading to data being sold on the Dark Web. However, organizations are encouraged to leverage cloud technology for competitive advantages rather than using it as a mere digital storage solution.

title: 200-acre Synergy Tech Park development in Saratoga County attracting interest from Amazon, UPS and Costco
summary: A 200-acre Synergy Tech Park development in Saratoga County, New York, is drawing interest from major companies like Amazon, UPS, and Costco. The park, located in Clifton Park, is anchored by a new U-Haul regional storage center and is being developed by Mark Rekucki of M.J. Properties Inc. The project aims to create a significant warehouse park in the region.

title: Five Questions with… Bernd Greifeneder, Founder and CTO at Dynatrace
summary: Bernd Greifeneder, Founder and CTO of Dynatrace, discusses the biggest challenges for his clients, which involve transforming into software businesses and moving towards an Autonomous Cloud with automated operations. He expresses excitement about deterministic AI and its application in complex IT environments, highlighting Dynatrace's successful reinvention from application performance management to software intelligence. Greifeneder also shares his greatest success, Dynatrace's IPO, and a lesson learned from a past failure in market analysis.

title: New CEO at Ebay, Microsoft launches its e-commerce tool and international transit time to be reduced in Brazil. E-commerce news by Nabil.
summary: This article covers major e-commerce news including Devin Wenig stepping down as eBay CEO, Microsoft launching its Dynamics 365 Commerce tool to compete in the e-commerce solutions market, and Brazil's national Correios significantly reducing international transit times. It also highlights Rent the Runway's supply chain issues, JD.com's efforts to speed up deliveries, and advancements in drone delivery by FedEx, Walgreens, and Wing Aviation. Additionally, the article notes the U.S. remaining in the Universal Postal Union and Narvar's partnership with Walgreens for Urban Outfitters' pick-up services.

title: Motorola, known for cellphones, is fast becoming a major player in government surveillance and artificial intelligence
summary: Motorola Solutions, the successor to the mobile phone business, is investing heavily in government surveillance and artificial intelligence technologies. The company has spent $1.7 billion since 2017 to acquire or support companies specializing in police body cameras, facial recognition, video analytics, and automated license plate readers. This consolidation of surveillance tools under one corporation raises significant privacy concerns about the government's increasing ability to monitor individuals.

title: Austin: Broadmoor Mixed-Use Project Gains Traction
summary: Brandywine Realty Trust, owner of the 66-acre Broadmoor redevelopment in North Austin, hired Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL) to handle retail leasing and hospitality site sales for the project. Broadmoor is designed as a mixed-use community bringing retail, entertainment, offices, residences, green space, and hospitality to enhance the IBM Research-Austin campus. The development envisions nearly 3,000 apartments and includes renovations of existing IBM buildings, positioning it as "Austin's second downtown."

title: MGM Resorts to Pay 2017 Las Vegas Shooting Victims Up to $800 Million
summary: MGM Resorts International has agreed to pay up to $800 million to settle lawsuits from victims of the October 2017 Las Vegas mass shooting. The settlement resolves "substantially all" claims against the company related to the incident at the Route 91 Harvest country music festival, which killed 58 people. The company's initial aggressive legal strategy, citing a federal law that protected it from liability, drew criticism and likely influenced this settlement.

title: New Disney stores at Target now open, featuring 'Frozen 2' and Star Wars merchandise
summary: Target and Disney have launched 25 new "shop-in-shop" Disney stores within Target locations across the U.S., coinciding with the release of new merchandise for "Frozen 2" and "Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker." These 750-square-foot stores offer over 450 items, including many previously exclusive to Disney retail locations, and are designed to provide an immersive family shopping experience. The partnership plans to expand with another 40 locations by October 2020 and a new Target store near Walt Disney World Resort in 2021.

title: U-Haul breaks ground on Synergy Tech Park site
summary: U-Haul has broken ground on its first facility within the new Synergy Tech Park in Clifton Park, N.Y., a project by MJ Properties. This 155,000-square-foot facility is a significant step for the 200-acre tech park, which represents an $18.2 million investment by MJ Properties to attract corporate, commercial, and light industrial users. The site will offer a full-line moving and storage center with 900 climate-controlled storage rooms.

title: Walmart takes on Amazon in India with enhancements to Flipkart’s ‘Big Billion Days’
summary: Walmart is intensifying its competition with Amazon in India through significant enhancements to Flipkart’s “Big Billion Days” sales event. Flipkart's event, running from September 29 through October 4, has already seen tremendous success, with first-day sales doubling compared to the previous year. This initiative positions "Big Billion Days" as India's version of major global shopping events like Amazon's "Prime Day" and Alibaba's "Singles Day."

title: Naver, Kakao scramble to secure web cartoons
summary: Naver and Kakao are heavily investing in securing intellectual property rights for web novels and cartoons to capitalize on the rapidly growing cultural content market. They are developing these original sources into diverse forms of cultural content like movies and TV shows, with both companies actively holding contests to attract new talent and expand their content libraries. The market for web novels and cartoons in Korea has seen explosive growth, driven by an increasing willingness of users to pay for quality content and the rise of smart devices.

title: Between a Wi-Fi rock and a high-tech place: Expedia preaches connectivity and productivity in new Seattle HQ
summary: Expedia is moving its 4,500 employees into a new 40-acre waterfront campus in Seattle, designed for hyperconnectivity and collaboration. The new office space, a $900 million project, emphasizes an open floor plan, universal desks, and 100% Wi-Fi coverage from 1,200 access points, including hidden ones in fake rocks. An "EG Navigator" app helps employees find their way around the massive campus and locate co-workers, reflecting Expedia's focus on productivity and a consistent global workspace experience.

title: How Data-Driven John Deere Wins the Market
summary: John Deere leverages location intelligence and AI-powered geographic information systems (GIS) to gain a competitive advantage in the agricultural machinery market. The company utilizes vast amounts of data, including sales, demographics, land cover, and satellite imagery, to predict market performance, optimize dealer investments, and understand customer psychographics. This data-driven approach helps John Deere remove guesswork from market development, leading to a healthy retail network and substantial revenue.

title: Target Circle guide: Here's what you need to know about the new shopper loyalty program
summary: Target has expanded its free shopper loyalty program, Target Circle, nationwide. This program allows shoppers to earn 1% on purchases, receive personalized offers like a birthday discount, and help direct Target's charitable giving. While RedCard holders still get 5% off, they can also benefit from other Circle perks, as the new program integrates the former Cartwheel savings tool.

title: Airline seat screens face fight for survival on domestic flights
summary: Airlines are divided on the future of seatback screens on domestic flights, with some carriers removing them in favor of streaming to personal devices, while others like Delta and JetBlue are investing in advanced screen technology. The debate centers on cost, weight savings, technological obsolescence, and providing a "two-screen" experience. Despite differing approaches, all airlines are focusing on improved Wi-Fi to enhance personalized services and leverage passenger data for new revenue streams, including potential in-flight shopping and advertising.

title: IBD Stock Of The Day: ASML Holding Breaks Out To New High
summary: ASML Holding (ASML) broke out to a new high on Thursday from a three-weeks-tight pattern, near a buy point of $252.21. The stock's relative strength line is at a record high, with a Relative Strength rating of 96. This breakout follows previous flat base-on-base and cup-with-handle patterns.

title: HERSHEY'S Chocolate Candy Bar 30 Count Variety Pack $16.88 (only 56¢ each)
summary: This article highlights an Amazon deal for a HERSHEY'S Chocolate Candy Bar 30 Count Variety Pack priced at $16.88, making each bar approximately 56 cents. The pack includes Hershey's Milk Chocolate, Hershey's Milk Chocolate with Almonds, KIT KAT Crisp Wafers, and REESE’S Peanut Butter Cups. The article also mentions various Amazon free trial offers for services like Amazon Music, Kindle Unlimited, Audible, and Amazon FreeTime Unlimited.

title: Uber Acquires Cornershop, a Grocery Delivery Start-Up (Published 2019)
summary: Uber has acquired a majority stake in the grocery delivery start-up Cornershop to expand its food delivery business and diversify beyond ride-hailing. This acquisition follows a previous failed attempt by Walmart to buy Cornershop due to antitrust concerns. Uber plans to expand Cornershop's presence into new markets, including the United States, facing competition from Instacart and Amazon.

title: 2019 Retailer of the Year: Walmart Is Reshaping Grocery From the Ground Up
summary: Walmart was named Progressive Grocer's 2019 Retailer of the Year for its innovative approach to grocery, focusing on saving customers and associates time through advanced technology and omnichannel experiences. The company is experimenting with in-home delivery, autonomous vehicles, and voice ordering, while also investing in its physical stores and employee development, contributing to significant financial growth and market share gains. These efforts highlight Walmart's strategy to lead in the evolving retail landscape by prioritizing convenience, efficiency, and sustainability.

title: Opendoor appoints CFO, CPO
summary: Opendoor has announced a series of key executive and board appointments, including Gautam Gupta as CFO and chief business officer, and Tom Willerer as its first-ever chief product officer. The company also hired Julie Todaro as president of homes and services and added Carrie Wheeler and Jason Kilar to its board of directors. These strategic hires aim to bolster the company as it continues to grow and innovate in the home-selling market.

title: Walmart will subsidize vendors, in first shots of holiday price war with Amazon
summary: Walmart is launching a "Competitive Price Adjustment program" to subsidize third-party sellers on its marketplace, lowering prices for consumers while ensuring vendors receive their original listed amount. This move is a direct response to Amazon's similar programs and intensifying competition for online shoppers, particularly ahead of the holiday season. The strategy aims to attract shoppers with deep discounts, mirroring Amazon's past tactics and current practices under FTC scrutiny.

title: How Amazon.com moved into the business of U.S. elections
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has significantly expanded its presence in the U.S. election technology sector since 2016, with over 40 states using its services for various election-related functions and both major political parties relying on its cloud. While offering secure and cost-effective solutions for election administrators, this centralization raises concerns among security experts about potential vulnerabilities and the impact of a single major breach. Amazon maintains its systems are reliable and faults in past data exposures were due to customer errors, even as it continues to face scrutiny over its growing influence.

title: Cisco veterans, backed by $278M, aim to disrupt Amazon's cloud dominance
summary: A group of former key Cisco executives, backed by $278 million, have unveiled a San Jose-based cloud tech startup after three years of stealth development. They aim to "democratize the cloud" and target Amazon's cloud dominance. The team previously sold billions of dollars worth of businesses to Cisco Systems.

title: Ex-Cisco CEO John Chambers, star team of engineers have a startup targeting Amazon’s AWS
summary: Former Cisco CEO John Chambers has re-teamed with a "star team" of engineers from Cisco Systems Inc. to launch a new startup called Pensando Systems. This ultra-secretive Silicon Valley company aims to challenge Amazon's AWS by developing hardware and software designed to improve the efficiency of computer servers, especially in cloud environments. The move comes as emerging technologies like 5G, IoT, and AI accelerate data growth and alter data consumption and location.

title: Barneys enters deal to sell assets to Authentic Brands, B. Riley for $271 million cash
summary: Barneys New York Inc has agreed to sell its assets to Authentic Brands Group and B. Riley Financial Inc for an estimated $271.4 million in cash, acting as a "stalking horse" bid. The luxury department store chain, which filed for bankruptcy due to rent hikes, is open to further bids until October 22, potentially leading to an auction. This deal aims to prevent the company from winding down its business entirely.

title: PayPal is launching a Venmo credit card to help monetize the payment app
summary: PayPal's Venmo is partnering with Synchrony Financial to launch a Venmo-branded credit card in 2020, aiming to monetize its popular peer-to-peer payments app which has grown to 40 million users but has yet to turn a profit. This move follows the launch of a Venmo debit card last year and is intended to round out its financial offerings, with Synchrony handling the banking side and a profit-sharing agreement in place. The credit card will allow users to manage bills directly through the Venmo app and will explore rewards and cash-back options.

title: A look inside the Sherwin-Williams search for a new world headquarters
summary: This article discusses Sherwin-Williams' nationwide search for a new global headquarters, highlighting the factors they are likely considering as a Fortune 200 public company. Expert John Boyd explains that key drivers for corporate headquarters projects include a strong talent pool, universities enriching the labor market, and a major international gateway airport, putting cities like Dallas, Houston, Charlotte, Atlanta, Chicago, and even Pittsburgh in contention. The process is influenced by the "post-Amazon HQ2 climate," emphasizing the pressure on Cleveland and Ohio to present a compelling case to retain the company.

title: Fox, Charter Strike New Carriage Deal
summary: Fox Corporation and Charter Communications have announced a new long-term carriage deal covering Fox's suite of TV networks, including Fox News Channel, FS1, and BTN. The agreement also includes video-on-demand and TV Everywhere rights, and both companies will collaborate on combating piracy. This pact follows similar recent deals Fox made with Cox Communications and Dish.

title: Can Apple Stock Hold New Highs?
summary: Apple Inc. (AAPL) has rallied to an all-time high ahead of its third-quarter earnings, driven by strong iPhone demand and the upcoming Apple TV+ streaming service. Despite this optimism, trade tensions with China and the reaction to earnings remain key uncertainties. Technical analysis suggests potential for new highs, but also highlights risks if negative catalysts emerge.

title: Amazon Net Income by Quarter: FY Q1 1997 – Q2 2021
summary: This article details Amazon's quarterly net income performance from Q1 1997 to Q2 2021, highlighting key financial milestones such as its first profitable quarter in Q4 2001 and the record-high net income in Q1 2019. It also provides a historical overview of Amazon Inc., including its founding, IPO, and major products. The company reported a 48.4% YoY increase in quarterly net profit in Q2 2021, reaching $7,778 million.

title: Number of Amazon Employees by Year: FY 1996 – 2020
summary: This article details the growth in Amazon's global employee count from fiscal year 1996 to 2020, highlighting key milestones in its workforce expansion. It notes Amazon had 1,298,000 full-time and part-time employees worldwide as of December 2020, representing a 62.66% year-over-year growth. The piece also provides background information on Amazon.com, Inc., including its founding, IPO, major products, and market value.

title: Growth in Amazon Revenue by Quarter: FY Q1 1997 – Q2 2021
summary: This article provides an overview of Amazon's quarterly revenue growth from Q1 1997 to Q2 2021, highlighting key financial milestones. It notes Amazon's highest-ever quarterly revenue of $87.4 billion and an all-time high of $125.555 billion in Q4 2020. The article also includes a brief history of Amazon Inc., its IPO, and major products and services.

title: F5 Networks and Amazon Web Services team up in cloud partnership of Seattle tech giants
summary: F5 Networks and Amazon Web Services have formed a multi-year cloud partnership, bringing together their sales teams and paving the way for future technology integrations. This alliance aims to simplify the creation of cloud-native applications using F5 on AWS and facilitate the migration of existing applications to the cloud. The announcement coincided with F5's strong Q4 2019 financial results, beating Wall Street expectations, despite the ongoing transition from hardware to software and the integration of NGINX.

title: Daytona's Consolidated-Tomoka changes name, creates new company
summary: Consolidated-Tomoka Land Co. is changing its name to CTO Realty Growth Inc. and forming a new company called Alpine Income Property Trust, which will have an initial public offering. Alpine will be a real estate investment trust focusing on single-tenant income properties, while CTO shifts its strategy to acquiring multi-tenant retail and office properties. This move follows CTO's recent sales of undeveloped land and golf courses.

title: Walmart to Close Norwalk Store, Lay Off 197 Workers
summary: Walmart Inc. announced the closure of its Norwalk store on November 1, resulting in the layoff of 197 workers. This marks the first Walmart store closure in the Los Angeles area this year, attributed to the store's overall performance despite the company's broader sales growth and e-commerce expansion. Walmart plans to continue investing in California with remodels and expanded online services, while the broader brick-and-mortar retail sector faces widespread bankruptcies and closures.

title: Amazon's AWS unit gets OK to build $800 million data facility in Argentina
summary: Argentina has approved Amazon's AWS unit to construct an $800 million data facility in a free trade zone near Bahia Blanca. This marks a significant investment for Amazon in South America and follows AWS's previous announcement of a smaller "Edge" location in Buenos Aires. The large investment suggests the facility will be substantial, positioning Argentina and Chile as competitors for a regional data center.

title: Apple Revamping Smart Home Efforts After Falling Behind Amazon, Google
summary: Apple Inc. is increasing hiring for a team dedicated to developing new smart-home software and devices to compete with Google and Amazon.com Inc. This initiative aims to expand Apple's smart-home platform, encourage more third-party accessory integration with the iPhone and Siri, and explore new home device possibilities beyond the HomePod speaker.

title: Korea Telecom Sets Non-Scripted Drama Pact With Discovery
summary: Korea Telecom and U.S. media firm Discovery have formed a joint venture to produce original, non-scripted Korean entertainment content for both Korean and international audiences. This content will be broadcast through KT’s SkylifeTV and Discovery’s global channels network. The joint venture aims to boost the Korean content industry amidst growing competition from streaming platforms.

title: Sorry Bezos, Brazil already has an Amazon.com: MercadoLivre
summary: Amazon faces significant challenges in Brazil, a key international market, despite rolling out its Prime service and Alexa-powered gadgets. Local e-commerce giants like MercadoLibre and Magazine Luiza have a strong grip on the market due to extensive delivery networks, established brands, and a deep understanding of local consumer behavior and logistical complexities. Amazon is adopting a strategy of patient growth, aiming to attract customers through content and services rather than directly competing on delivery infrastructure or product vastness initially.

title: Cisco alums reunite: Prem Jain’s Pensando spins into the edge-computing conversation
summary: Pensando Systems Inc., led by former Cisco executives including Prem Jain and John Chambers, has emerged from stealth mode with an ambitious plan to transform edge computing. The company aims to compete with Amazon Web Services Inc.'s Nitro by bringing critical IT services to the edge using programmable chips, replacing numerous appliances and simplifying architectures. Pensando’s technology leverages a "flow-based" approach, which they believe offers a distinct advantage in the industry.

title: Amazon cuts out fee for grocery delivery — for Prime members, anyway
summary: Amazon has eliminated the additional fee for its grocery delivery service for Prime members, making it a standard benefit. This move comes as Amazon expects to invest an additional $1.5 billion in Prime delivery during Q4. The change aims to enhance the value proposition for its Prime subscribers.

title: Texas signed off on the restoration of this old mine. Now a leaky landfill is contaminating groundwater.
summary: The Texas Railroad Commission approved Alcoa's restoration efforts at its shuttered Sandow Mine site, now marketed for $250 million as Sandow Lakes Ranch. However, groundwater testing has revealed contamination from toxic heavy metals associated with coal ash in a landfill on the property that is owned by Luminant. Environmental activists and former regulators criticize the lax reclamation standards and potential health risks to the community.

title: Cashless no more: Kroger Visa credit card ban ended following year-long fight over fees
summary: Kroger has ended its more than year-long ban on Visa credit cards, now accepting them at all of its stores nationwide. The supermarket giant had previously stopped accepting Visa at some subsidiaries due to "excessive fees," but has since reversed its decision. While the specific terms of the resolution are unknown, analysts view this as a win for Visa and the broader card industry, avoiding potential consumer-unfriendly surcharges or lost sales for merchants.

title: PTC’s Onshape Acquisition: Did SOLIDWORKS Founder Jon Hirschtick Have to Sell?
summary: PTC acquired Jon Hirschtick's cloud CAD company Onshape for $470 million, marking Hirschtick's second major CAD company sale. The article explores whether Onshape *had* to sell due to financial pressures, given its 5,000 paying users falling short of its 10,000 break-even target, or if the sale was a strategic move to leverage PTC's market presence and resources for accelerated growth in the evolving SaaS CAD market. It also discusses the strategic rationale behind PTC's acquisition, driven by CEO Jim Heppelmann's vision for SaaS, cloud-based solutions, and his previous successful bets on IoT and AR/VR.

title: Marin Software Research Finds Significant Growth in eCommerce Spend
summary: Marin Software's Q3 2019 Digital Advertising Benchmark Report reveals significant growth in eCommerce spend, primarily driven by Amazon Advertising and seasonal events like Prime Day, with a 115% year-over-year increase. Mobile search continues to dominate, accounting for nearly half of total search spend, indicating a shift towards localized mobile queries. The report highlights opportunities for marketers to optimize campaigns across various platforms, including non-eCommerce features like Instagram Explore Feed and Facebook Watch, as the industry enters a busy Q4 season.

title: Hershey’s Amazon landing page connects costumes with Halloween candy
summary: Hershey partnered with Rubie’s Costumes and MGM Studios to create a Halloween Headquarters landing page on Amazon, aiming to replicate the in-store experience of buying candy and costumes together. This collaboration, a first for Amazon, provides a holistic shopping experience and offers valuable data insights for Hershey, which is investing heavily in e-commerce strategies. The initiative highlights how digital platforms can drive seasonal sales and personalize consumer engagement while also aiding Hershey's direct-to-consumer loyalty efforts.

title: Kohl's drops Black Friday sale ad with doorbusters and $15 Kohl's Cash deal
summary: Kohl's has released its 64-page Black Friday ad four weeks early, detailing sales and doorbusters that will begin on Thanksgiving Day. Shoppers can earn $15 Kohl's Cash for every $50 spent, a higher rate than usual, with early deals available from November 1-3. The ad also highlights Black Friday week sales from November 25-29 and specific doorbuster deals for November 28-29.

title: Walmart offering alcohol pickup at stores in 29 states
summary: Walmart has expanded its alcohol pickup service to 2,000 stores across 29 states, allowing customers to purchase alcohol through Walmart Grocery Pickup. The service requires valid photo ID upon collection and will also include alcohol delivery in select California and Florida stores. This expansion is a strategic move to compete with other retailers offering similar services and to enhance e-commerce economics, despite local and state regulations.

title: What Has Been Driving Akamai Technologies’ Performance?
summary: Akamai Technologies (NASDAQ: AKAM) exceeded Q3 revenue and EPS expectations, primarily driven by strong growth in its security solutions business. This positive performance led to an upward revision of the company's guidance for Q4 and full-year 2019. The article highlights Akamai's shift from its core content delivery network (CDN) business, which faces competition from large internet players, towards leveraging its network reliability and insights to build a robust security business and become a key player in edge computing.

title: Shopify complaints mount from online retailers and consumers
summary: Online retailers and consumers are increasingly voicing complaints against Shopify, focusing on issues like chargebacks, abrupt account closures, and funds being held hostage. While Shopify provides a vital platform for numerous merchants, its rapid growth has led to accusations of heavy-handed practices regarding fees and dispute resolution. Despite an A+ rating from the BBB, the company faces scrutiny over its handling of customer and merchant conflicts and even rumors of potential class-action lawsuits.

title: UPS Debuts Home Delivery of CVS Medicine by Drone
summary: UPS has expanded its drone delivery services beyond hospital campuses, completing its first revenue-generating home deliveries of prescription medicines from a CVS Health Corp. pharmacy in Cary, N.C. The company used autonomous drones monitored by remote pilots, lowering packages by a winch, and plans to further grow drone deliveries, especially in rural areas, to compete with rivals like Amazon and FedEx. UPS was the first company approved by the FAA for commercial drone flights under the broadest airline rules.

title: Lineage Logistics | Success Story
summary: Lineage Logistics, a company revolutionizing temperature-controlled supply chain and logistics, moved its international headquarters from Irvine, California, to Michigan in 2017. The decision was driven by Michigan's talent pipeline, optimal location to customers, and support from the MEDC, despite competing sites in other states. Since relocating, Lineage Logistics has exceeded its initial job creation promises and significantly boosted its revenue, partly due to its strategic investment in Michigan.

title: How a Houston-area county landed a national retailer's 2M-square-foot, 1,300-job distribution center
summary: Ross Stores Inc. has selected Waller County in the Houston area for a new 2 million-square-foot distribution facility. This development is projected to create 1,300 full-time jobs, marking a significant economic boost for the region. The article details the successful move to attract this national retailer.

title: Calendar: Black Friday is Nov. 29. Target: Eh, close enough
summary: Target Corp. is set to launch a two-day Black Friday preview sale on November 8, three weeks ahead of the actual Black Friday. This move positions Target as the latest retailer to adjust its strategy amidst an unusually short holiday shopping season.

title: Expansion Planned at Culver City's Blackwelder Office Campus
summary: Kilroy Realty Corp. recently purchased the Blackwelder office complex in Culver City for $186 million with plans to significantly expand the existing 19-building, 158,000-square-foot campus. The property, currently fully leased with tenants paying below-market rates, is located in an area benefiting from the growth of content production companies like Amazon, Apple, and HBO.

title: Amazon Web Services Revenue by Year
summary: The article details the historical revenue growth of Amazon Web Services (AWS) from fiscal year 2014 to 2019, highlighting its increasing contribution to Amazon's overall revenue. AWS revenue reached an all-time high of $35.026 billion in 2019, representing 12.5% of Amazon's total revenue, demonstrating consistent strong year-over-year growth. It also provides background information on Amazon.com, Inc., including its founding, IPO, and key products.

title: Amazon Annual Revenue by Products & Services Group
summary: The article analyzes Amazon's annual revenue by product and service groups from 2014 to 2019, highlighting the significant contributions of Online Stores (over half of total revenue) and the rapid growth in Third-Party Seller Services, Subscription Services, AWS, and "Other" services. It also notes a slight decline in Physical Stores revenue in 2019. The report provides detailed financial figures and growth rates for each segment, underscoring Amazon's diverse revenue streams and market leadership.

title: Amazon Annual Revenue by Segment: FY 2001 - 2020
summary: This article analyzes Amazon's annual revenue by segment from FY 2001 to 2020, focusing on North America, International, and AWS. In 2019, Amazon's total revenue reached an all-time high of $280,522 million, with North America contributing over 60%. AWS revenue also saw significant growth, increasing by 36.5% year-over-year.

title: Amazon Annual Revenue By Region: FY 2013 to 2020
summary: This article analyzes Amazon's annual revenue by region from fiscal year 2013 to 2020, highlighting the United States as the largest market. In 2019, the US contributed over 69% of Amazon's total revenue, reaching $193,636 million. Germany, the UK, and Japan are identified as other significant markets for the e-commerce giant.

title: Amazon Annual Revenue from Products and Services
summary: The article details Amazon's annual revenue from products and services, highlighting significant growth. In 2019, Amazon reported its highest-ever annual revenue from products and services, reaching $160.4 billion and $120.1 billion respectively. The company's revenue milestones include crossing $50 billion in product sales in 2012 and exceeding $100 billion in products and $50 billion in services for the first time in 2017.

title: Walt Disney Company’s Investor Call Disney+ Highlights
summary: The Walt Disney Company's recent investor call highlighted details about Disney+, including its launch on Amazon, Samsung, and LG devices, and its European rollout on March 31st. Despite increased direct-to-consumer revenues, the segment operating loss grew due to Hulu consolidation and Disney+ launch costs. CEO Robert Iger also provided updates on the successful Disney+ trial in the Netherlands and mentioned FX content moving exclusively to Hulu.

title: JPMorgan Chase targets gig economy tech firms with e-wallet platform
summary: JPMorgan Chase has developed an e-wallet platform aimed at gig economy companies like Airbnb, Lyft, and Amazon, offering virtual bank accounts and perks to customers. This strategy allows JPMorgan to assume payment processing for these tech firms, addressing the threat of revenue loss to nonbanks and fintech companies. The bank aims to partner with the top 10 e-commerce and gig economy companies, simplifying refund processes and expediting payouts.

title: Google starts construction on $600M data center in unlikely burgeoning tech hub of New Albany, Ohio
summary: Google has begun construction on a $600 million data center in New Albany, Ohio, marking its third major tech facility in the area. The project is expected to be completed by early 2021 and follows investments from Facebook and Amazon, turning central Ohio into a data center hub due to significant tax cuts and strong electrical infrastructure. New Albany offered Google a substantial incentive package, including property tax abatement and waived fees, while the state of Ohio also provides sales tax exemptions for data centers.

title: Netflix co-founder Marc Randolph says company’s ‘secret weapon’ sets itself apart from Disney, other streaming services
summary: Netflix co-founder Marc Randolph believes the company's "focus" on streaming and movies is its "secret weapon" against new competitors like Disney+ and Apple TV+. Despite growing competition and concerns about Netflix's revenue stream, Randolph emphasizes the company's startup mentality and willingness to adapt, assuring its continued presence in the evolving digital streaming landscape.

title: Ralph Lauren offers consumers a DIY counterfeit-checking tool
summary: Ralph Lauren has launched Digital Product Identities, a DIY counterfeit-checking tool allowing consumers to verify product authenticity by scanning a label. This technology also provides product details and styling tips while offering Ralph Lauren real-time tracking and improved inventory management. The launch comes amidst increased attention on anti-counterfeiting technologies following reports of fake goods being sold on resale sites.

title: KKR makes formal approach to Walgreens Boots on record buyout
summary: KKR & Co. has formally approached Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc. regarding a potential deal to take the company private, which could represent the largest-ever leveraged buyout. The transaction faces challenges due to the large amount of financing required, with Walgreens Boots having a market value of about $56 billion and $16.8 billion in debt. This move would allow Walgreens Boots to adapt to a changing retail landscape away from public shareholder demands, especially with pressure from online competitors like Amazon.

title: Kroger launches auto buying program with TrueCar
summary: Kroger has partnered with TrueCar to launch the Kroger Auto Buying Program, offering customers access to pricing information, guaranteed savings on new cars, and discounts on used cars. This initiative is part of Kroger's strategy to provide more services and perks to its customers, mirroring efforts by competitors like Costco and Amazon, and contributes to its alternative profit portfolio which is projected to generate significant operating profit. The program is available to customers of several Kroger-owned grocery chains and aims to provide a more transparent car-buying experience.

title: Is this the peak of Amazon? 3 reasons why growth might be hard to come by
summary: This article explores whether Amazon's rapid growth phase might be peaking, citing three main red flags for investors. These include the increased costs associated with one-day shipping without commensurate profit growth, declining profitability and market share for Amazon Web Services (AWS), and a decrease in consumer preference for Amazon.com over competitors like Walmart.

title: Under the Hood of QRAFT AI Enhanced U.S. Large Cap ETF (QRFT)
summary: The QRAFT AI Enhanced U.S. Large Cap ETF (QRFT) is an actively managed ETF that uses a proprietary artificial intelligence system to select large-capitalization U.S. stocks. The fund aims for long-term capital appreciation by focusing on factors like quality, size, valuation, momentum, and low risk, with AI continuously learning optimal factor weights based on macroeconomic and valuation conditions.
