QRFT may serve as a large-cap equity allocation, offer factor exposure, or act as an alternative investment due to its cutting-edge technology.

title: Under the Hood of QRAFT AI Enhanced U.S. Large Cap ETF (QRFT)
summary: The article explores the QRAFT AI Enhanced U.S. Large Cap ETF (QRFT), highlighting its use of advanced AI and machine learning algorithms to select large-cap U.S. stocks. QRFT aims for long-term capital appreciation by dynamically optimizing factor weights across quality, size, valuation, momentum, and low risk, adapting to macroeconomic conditions. It is presented as a suitable option for investors seeking large-cap equity exposure, factor exposure, or an alternatives allocation based on cutting-edge technology.

title: Nike Pulling Its Products From Amazon in E-Commerce Pivot
summary: Nike Inc. is ending its pilot program to sell sneakers and apparel directly on Amazon's website, a move that follows the naming of a former EBay CEO as Nike's new chief. The athletic brand will cease direct sales on Amazon, which began in 2017, but will continue to utilize Amazon’s web services.

title: Elisa rolls-out industrial IoT to 100 P&G factories, says ‘world will change’ with 5G
summary: Finnish telecoms company Elisa is expanding its industrial IoT monitoring and insights solution to 100 Procter & Gamble factories, building on an initial rollout at 10 sites. Elisa emphasizes the transformative potential of 5G in industrial settings, beyond just speed, by enabling streaming analytics at the network edge. The company offers its data-analytics and digital-twinning recipe to third parties, leveraging its own successful internal digital transformation.

title: Target shoppers can tap the app and get groceries dropped on their porch the same day
summary: Target now offers same-day delivery through its app, allowing customers to order groceries and other items for a $9.99 fee, waived for purchases over $75 from Nov. 17-26. Shipt members receive free delivery, and new users can try a four-week free trial. This move positions Target competitively alongside other retailers like Walmart and Amazon, which also offer various same-day delivery options.

title: Why Costco Is Thriving Even as the U.S.-China Trade War Drags On
summary: Costco is successfully navigating the U.S.-China trade war despite tariffs that are impacting other retailers. The company benefits from its high sales volumes, fast inventory turnover, and a business model that relies on membership fees for a significant portion of its operating earnings, providing stability in a volatile retail sector. Costco's scale grants leverage with vendors, and its strategic expansion and focused inventory management allow it to maintain low prices and strong sales growth, outpacing competitors and the broader retail market.

title: Motorola Solutions Has Made $25 Million This Year Working with ICE and CBP
summary: Motorola Solutions has earned $25 million this year from contracts with ICE and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, providing radio communication services and software. This work has drawn scrutiny given ICE's controversial policies, including family separations and unsanitary detention conditions. The company's corporate responsibility statement emphasizes ethical operation and community support, yet they did not comment on their contracts with VICE.

title: ‘Not on Netflix’ and proud of it, Tubi boasts in ads
summary: Tubi, a free ad-supported streaming service, is launching a new advertising campaign that highlights its content not available on Netflix to attract viewers suffering from "subscription fatigue." The campaign, featuring actor Chris Noth, emphasizes Tubi's free model and its extensive library of movies and TV shows, including a "Not on Netflix" category. Despite some concerns about promoting competitors, Tubi aims to position itself as a complementary service to paid subscriptions.

title: Ubiquiti AmpliFi Alien Wi-Fi 6 router has a big, beautiful color touchscreen
summary: Ubiquiti has released the AmpliFi Alien Wi-Fi 6 router, featuring a large color touchscreen and a design reminiscent of an Amazon Echo. This router boasts 8x8 MIMO Wi-Fi 6 Technology for extended range and speed, supports mesh networking, and includes software features like simple setup and a free VPN service. It is priced at $379 and offers advanced performance optimizations for multiple connected devices.

title: PayPal just struck L.A.’s biggest ever tech deal
summary: PayPal Holdings Inc. announced the acquisition of Honey Science Corp. for $4 billion, marking the largest tech deal in Los Angeles history. Honey, a popular browser extension for price comparison, will be integrated into PayPal and Venmo to extend consumer engagement beyond checkout. This acquisition is seen as transformative, accelerating PayPal's capabilities and market relevance, especially given Honey's profitability and strong growth.

title: Chipotle Announces Alexa Reordering Skill By Giving Away Echo Dots To Rewards Members Named Alexa
summary: Chipotle has launched a new skill for Amazon Alexa, allowing customers to reorder their favorite meals for delivery or pickup. To celebrate this launch and reaching seven million Rewards Members, Chipotle is giving away Amazon Echo Dots to all existing Chipotle Rewards members named Alexa. This initiative is part of Chipotle's broader artificial intelligence strategy, which also includes AI-generated voice assistants in all 2,500 restaurants to streamline the ordering process.

title: Wingstop lets Twitch users order food while watching livestreams
summary: Wingstop has introduced a "Wing Calculator" Twitch Extension that allows users to order food directly while watching livestreams on the platform. This initiative, available through select streamers, aims to capture delivery orders from Twitch's engaged audience, predominantly millennial men who watch others play video games. The campaign highlights Twitch's Extension apps' flexibility for e-commerce, offering a new revenue stream beyond sponsorships and subscriptions.

title: What to look for in a TV on Black Friday?
summary: This article provides comprehensive advice on what to consider when buying a TV during Black Friday sales. It covers key factors such as screen size, resolution (4K vs. 8K), HDR technology, connectivity (HDMI ports), panel type (OLED vs. LCD), and smart TV features. The author also advises on distinguishing between genuine bargains and lower-quality brands.

title: Alexa can remind you to take your medication
summary: Amazon's Alexa has launched new features allowing select customers to set medication reminders and request prescription refills through voice commands, in partnership with Omnicell and Giant Eagle Pharmacy. This initiative aims to simplify medication management at home while prioritizing user privacy and security through voice profiles and personal passcodes. Amazon plans to expand these features to more pharmacies in the future, highlighting the ongoing innovation in voice technology for healthcare.

title: Movado Group struggles as watches become status symbols
summary: Movado Group reported a significant drop in earnings and sales, attributed to a failed marketing campaign and intensifying challenges in the watch market. This contrasts with the strong demand for high-end Swiss luxury watches, which continue to be prominent status symbols, especially in the U.S.

title: Synchrony says suspicious email blast citing Amazon didn't involve a data breach or fraudulent activity
summary: Synchrony Financial clarified that a suspicious email blast sent to customers, which cited Amazon, was due to an internal error and did not involve a data breach or fraudulent activity. Consumers are advised that they do not need to take any action. Amazon also acknowledged the issue, stating the notification was distributed by Synchrony in error.

title: Synchrony Bank apologizes for deposit email
summary: Synchrony Bank issued an apology after mistakenly sending out emails about a small deposit into "Amazon Credit Builder accounts" to people who were not their customers or even Amazon account holders. Many recipients believed the emails were a scam or indicated a data breach. The bank clarified it was an internal error, with a spokesperson from the Better Business Bureau suggesting the affiliation with PayPal might be how email addresses were acquired.

title: TCL 55" Class 6 Series 4K HDR Roku Smart TV (2019) Review
summary: The TCL 55R625 4K HDR Roku Smart TV (2019) offers excellent color accuracy, deep blacks, and an auto game mode, making it a strong contender in the midrange TV market. Despite a 60Hz native refresh rate, its overall performance, especially for gaming and HDR content, is impressive for its $600 price point. The Roku interface is highlighted as intuitive and fast, contributing to a top-tier user experience.

title: Amazon and eBay accused of selling cosmetics containing mercury
summary: Online marketplaces Amazon.com Inc. and eBay Inc. are facing accusations of selling skin-lightening products with high mercury levels, particularly as the holiday shopping season approaches. Activist groups tested 158 products sold on these platforms across 12 countries and found that 60% were contaminated with mercury, which was not listed as an ingredient. This situation highlights the product safety risks associated with the convenience of online shopping.

title: Black Friday Amazon deals' costs: Workers' health, climate change and your own taxes
summary: This article examines the hidden costs of Amazon's convenience, focusing on worker exploitation, environmental impact, and tax subsidies. It highlights the physical dangers faced by Amazon employees due to high-speed quotas, the company's significant carbon footprint, and the financial burden placed on taxpayers through subsidies, while also noting recent worker and activist pushback.

title: Amazon and Walmart Thought India Would Be Their Next Giant Market. India’s Shopkeepers Would Like to Disagree
summary: Indian shopkeepers are protesting against Amazon and Walmart's e-commerce operations, alleging predatory pricing and violation of regulations designed to protect local businesses. This conflict arises as India investigates these allegations, and local merchants, a significant political force, lobby the government to protect their interests from the global giants. The shopkeepers claim that e-commerce deep discounting is driving them out of business, despite earlier regulatory changes aimed at leveling the playing field.

title: Rigetti Quantum Computers Now Available via Amazon Web Services
summary: Rigetti Computing announced its quantum computers are now available through Amazon Braket, a new fully managed Amazon Web Services (AWS) solution. This collaboration significantly expands access to Rigetti's quantum systems, allowing scientists, researchers, and developers to experiment with their 32-qubit superconducting chip technology. Rigetti has also joined the AWS Partner Network to develop quantum computing applications for enterprise customers.

title: Weak Brick-and-Mortar Holiday Shopping Can Fuel "CLIX" ETF
summary: Online shopping surged for Black Friday, leading to a 6% drop in sales for brick-and-mortar stores. This trend suggests potential gains for the Long Online/Short Stores ETF (CLIX), which invests in online retailers and shorts physical stores. The article also mentions the Direxion Daily Retail Bull 3X ETF (RETL) for those bullish on retail sales during the Christmas season.

title: Amazon’s AWS Will Now Power FOX’s Streaming Services Including FOX Sports
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has partnered with FOX to power all of FOX’s streaming services, including the FOX Sports app, and the backend for over 200 affiliate FOX stations. This collaboration aims to enhance the delivery of live sports, news, and entertainment through AWS Media Services, AWS Outposts for on-premises video processing, and AWS analytics and machine learning services for improved user experiences. FOX anticipates increased quality and reliability for its streaming services and affiliates as a result of this extended partnership.

title: Microsoft Security—a Leader in 5 Gartner Magic Quadrants
summary: Microsoft Security has been recognized as a Leader in five Gartner Magic Quadrants across various security areas including Cloud Access Security Brokers (CASB), Access Management, Enterprise Information Archiving, Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) tools, and Endpoint Protection Platforms. This recognition highlights the breadth and depth of Microsoft's security offerings, emphasizing their integrated approach that works across different cloud environments and non-Microsoft solutions. The article details Microsoft's strengths in each of these five categories, showcasing their commitment to providing comprehensive and integrated security solutions.

title: Intel in talks to buy Israeli AI chip co Habana Labs
summary: Intel is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire Israeli AI chip startup Habana Labs for an estimated $1 billion. Habana Labs, founded in 2016, previously raised $120 million, with Intel Capital leading its latest financing round in November 2018. If the acquisition proceeds, it would significantly strengthen Intel's position in the AI chip market, where Habana Labs has developed specialized AI Training and Inference Processors.

title: It’s hard for shoppers to avoid Amazon — even in their investments
summary: This article discusses the pervasive influence of Amazon, suggesting it's difficult for consumers and investors alike to avoid the company. It questions whether one should invest in the consumer discretionary sector, framing it as a decision based on the belief of an incoming economic downturn. The piece highlights the importance of understanding one's investments.

title: iHeartmedia Picks Nashville For Second Headquarters for iHeartRadio Digital
summary: iHeartMedia has announced Nashville, Tennessee, will be the location for its second digital headquarters for iHeartRadio, set to open in 2020. Company officials cited Nashville's thriving technology ecosystem, rich music history, and entrepreneurial spirit as key factors in their decision to expand beyond their New York headquarters. This move is expected to create new jobs in engineering, product development, and data science, further strengthening iHeartRadio's position as a leading audio company.

title: Fox to Use Amazon Web Services for Cable, Satellite Broadcasts
summary: Fox Corp. is partnering with Amazon Web Services for its cable and satellite broadcasts, turning to Amazon's cloud to route video to its customers. This multi-year deal involves AWS Media Services transmitting Fox sports, news, and entertainment content, and also helping power Fox production facilities. The move aims to replace Fox's older video infrastructure with a more agile system capable of adapting to business changes and launching new channels quicker.

title: Goldman Sachs CEO reveals 2020 tech plans at Amazon event, guest DJs
summary: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon addressed attendees at Amazon.com Inc.’s cloud-tech conference in Las Vegas to discuss the bank's 2020 tech plans. He was also guest DJ at the event.

title: How Amazon created AWS and changed technology forever
summary: This article details how Amazon Web Services (AWS) originated from Amazon's internal need to scale its e-commerce operations beyond books. AWS established the cloud computing industry, transforming technology and becoming a multi-billion-dollar market leader. However, it now faces significant competition from Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud.

title: Ross Dress for Less set to grow here
summary: Ross Dress for Less is expanding into Northeast Ohio as part of its Ohio expansion program, with its first store already open in Cuyahoga Falls and additional stores planned for Brooklyn and Mentor. The off-price apparel and home goods chain is seen as a welcome addition to the region's retail real estate market, with estimates suggesting at least nine more stores could open in the Cleveland and Akron areas. This expansion leverages the void left by other retailers and aims to provide an accessible shopping option for consumers.

title: Chesapeake Utilities to buy Elkton Gas for $15M
summary: Chesapeake Utilities Corp. has agreed to acquire Elkton Gas for $15 million from South Jersey Industries (SJI). This acquisition is expected to close in the second quarter of 2020 and will expand Chesapeake Utilities' natural gas service area in Cecil County, Maryland. SJI's sale of Elkton Gas is part of its strategy to refocus on its core business in New Jersey.

title: Kids' Smartwatches Sold on Amazon Can Be Easily Hacked by Strangers
summary: Cybersecurity researchers Rapid7 have found critical security flaws in cheap kids' smartwatches sold on Amazon, allowing strangers to easily track and communicate with children. These devices, which are often white-label rebrands, have ineffective security measures such as faulty whitelists and easily discoverable default passwords. Parents are advised to stick with recognizable brands to avoid these security risks.

title: Teamsters Strike UNFI, Supplier to Whole Foods
summary: Teamsters Local 414 members initiated a strike at a UNFI distribution center in Fort Wayne, Indiana, protesting alleged violations of workers' rights and failure to bargain in good faith. The strike by 158 workers, who supply groceries in six states, highlights UNFI's troubled labor history and its stock decline since acquiring SUPERVALU. As UNFI's largest customer, with 21% of its 2019 revenue, Whole Foods/Amazon will be impacted by the strike.

title: Amazon Logistics parcel volume will surpass UPS and FedEx by 2022, Morgan Stanley says
summary: Morgan Stanley predicts that Amazon Logistics' parcel volume will exceed that of UPS and FedEx by 2022, primarily handling its own orders but also with an expected expansion into third-party logistics. Amazon's current growth rate of delivering its own orders suggests it will overtake legacy carriers despite focusing mainly on densely populated areas. The report also highlights the importance of Amazon's logistics expansion for its profitability and its potential to significantly reduce the market share of traditional parcel carriers.

title: Amazon Is Leaving Rural Deliveries to USPS: Morgan Stanley
summary: A Morgan Stanley report reveals that Amazon Logistics is focusing on lucrative urban and suburban delivery areas, leaving less profitable rural deliveries to the USPS. This strategy helps Amazon slash costs for its expanding transportation network but further strains the financially struggling USPS, which is legally obligated to serve all US addresses. Amazon's "cherry-picking" of dense zip codes means it's avoiding the high costs associated with rural deliveries, putting the USPS in a more difficult financial position.

title: Intel Buys Israeli AI Chipmaker Habana Labs for $2 Billion
summary: Intel Corp. acquired Israeli AI chipmaker Habana Labs for approximately $2 billion to strengthen its position in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence silicon market. This acquisition is part of Intel's strategy to make its offerings essential to major silicon buyers and compete against companies like Alphabet's Google and Amazon's AWS, which are increasingly designing their own chips for data centers. Habana Labs is expected to operate independently for the time being.

title: The Curious Case of Kroger and Walgreens
summary: Kroger and Walgreens have formed an unprecedented Retail Procurement Alliance, leading to speculation about a potential merger between the two companies. Such a merger would create a retail giant with $257 billion in annual revenues and over 12,000 stores, offering significant synergies and enhanced competitiveness against market leaders like Walmart and Amazon. The article draws parallels to Kroger's 1998 merger with Fred Meyer, highlighting a history of strategic deal-making to address competitive threats.

title: Dave Clark: The Man Who Built Amazon’s Delivery Machine
summary: This article profiles Dave Clark, the executive responsible for building Amazon's massive delivery network. It details his aggressive tactics and strategic decisions, including reducing reliance on partners like FedEx and UPS, investing heavily in warehouses and logistics, and grappling with challenges like worker safety and rapid growth. The piece highlights how Clark's vision has shaped Amazon's delivery capabilities, even as the company faces increasing scrutiny and operational hurdles.

title: Amazon hits back at claims it’s abusing open-source software
summary: Amazon Web Services Inc. has responded to criticism that it "strip-mines" open-source software projects by repackaging them as paid services. While AWS claims to be giving customers what they want and contributing significantly to open-source projects, some critics argue this practice undermines the sustainability of open-source companies, forcing them to compete against the very software they developed. Analysts suggest open-source companies must innovate and offer managed versions of their products to succeed against large cloud providers.

title: F5 Networks will acquire Shape Security for $1 billion to bolster online fraud protection services
summary: F5 Networks announced its acquisition of Shape Security for approximately $1 billion to enhance its online fraud protection services and strengthen its application security portfolio. This is F5's largest acquisition to date, following its earlier purchase of NGINX, and is expected to significantly boost F5's software revenue growth. Shape Security brings advanced machine learning and AI capabilities, mitigating over 1 billion fake transactions daily for a clientele including Fortune 50 companies, major banks, and airlines.

title: ETF of the Week: ProShares's ONLN ETF
summary: This article features CEO Tom Lydon discussing the ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN) on his "ETF of the Week" podcast. ONLN tracks a modified market-capitalization weighted index of global online retailers, including major players like Amazon and Alibaba, and aims to capitalize on the increasing trend of online shopping. Lydon highlights the potential for growth in online retail, despite concerns about market fluctuations, suggesting ONLN could be a viable investment for both long-term and shorter-term strategies.

title: Amazon to deliver 3.5 billion packages through own network in 2019
summary: Amazon announced it was on track to deliver 3.5 billion customer packages globally in 2019 through its in-house delivery network, indicating its growing independence from third-party shippers like FedEx and UPS. A Morgan Stanley analysis estimated Amazon's logistics would handle 6.5 billion packages by 2022, surpassing both UPS and FedEx. The company also confirmed it now has 150 U.S. delivery stations employing over 90,000 people.

title: Urban Edge acquires Wonderland Marketplace for $24.1 million - Heald and Angelone of JLL represent the seller
summary: Urban Edge Properties has acquired Wonderland Marketplace, a 139,507 s/f shopping center in Revere, MA, for $24.1 million. JLL's Nat Heald and Chris Angelone represented the seller in the transaction. This acquisition marks Urban Edge's first substantial entry into the Boston Metro area, with plans to benefit from the region's growth and potential future redevelopment.

title: TiVo inks $3B merger with Xperi to create new ‘amazing entertainment platform’
summary: TiVo and Xperi are merging in a $3 billion all-stock transaction to create a new "amazing entertainment platform." The deal combines TiVo's content aggregation with Xperi's reach into home, automotive, and mobile tech markets. The new company aims to leverage its combined 10,000 patents to transform the entertainment experience and compete with other content aggregators like Roku and Amazon.

title: Tech innovation is changing the world, and this fund manager has big bets on how it’s going to work
summary: This article highlights Catherine Wood, founder and CEO of ARK Invest, and her investment strategy focused on disruptive technologies. Wood makes her bets in exchange-traded funds, using an "open-source research ecosystem." Her approach to public markets contrasts with traditional venture capitalists.

title: Rivian Gets $1.3 Billion Investment in Electric Truck Venture (Published 2019)
summary: Rivian, an electric-vehicle start-up backed by Amazon and Ford, announced a $1.3 billion investment led by T. Rowe Price. This funding round, the largest for Rivian to date, brings its total investments for 2019 to $2.85 billion as it prepares to launch its truck and SUV and compete with Tesla. The investment highlights confidence in Rivian's strategy and products, but also its significant capital needs.

title: Joseph Segel: QVC founder has died at 88; he also founded more than 20 other companies, including The Franklin Mint
summary: Joseph Segel, the "quintessential entrepreneur" and founder of the home-shopping network QVC, has died at 88 due to congestive heart failure. Segel, who also founded over 20 other companies including The Franklin Mint, was remembered as a visionary who changed the way the world shops. He retired from QVC in 1993 but remained an adviser until 2013, leaving a legacy of innovation and customer focus.

title: Rivian announces $1.3 billion funding round led by T. Rowe Price
summary: Rivian has closed a $1.3 billion investment round led by T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc., with participation from Amazon, Ford Motor Company, and BlackRock. This funding marks Rivian's fourth investment announcement of 2019, highlighting strong investor confidence in the electric vehicle manufacturer's team, products, technology, and strategy. The company is preparing to launch its R1T and R1S vehicles, with customer deliveries expected to begin at the end of 2020.

title: Electric-Truck Maker Rivian Raises $1.3 Billion in New Funding
summary: Electric-truck startup Rivian Automotive Inc. has raised an additional $1.3 billion in funding led by T. Rowe Price, bringing its total raised in 2019 to $2.85 billion. This investment, also involving Amazon.com Inc., Ford Motor Co., and BlackRock, aims to support the company's upcoming vehicle rollouts.

title: Joseph Segel, QVC founder, dies at 88
summary: Joseph Segel, the visionary entrepreneur who founded the home-shopping network QVC, has died at 88 due to congestive heart failure. Segel, who also founded the Franklin Mint, was remembered as an innovator whose ideas changed the way the world shops and whose focus on the customer profoundly influenced QVC's culture. He retired as QVC chairman in 1993 but remained an adviser until 2013 and was recognized as one of the greatest business leaders and most influential alumni by Harvard Business School and Wharton School respectively.

title: That U-Haul in your neighborhood may very well be carrying your gift order
summary: During the peak holiday season, delivery companies like UPS resorted to renting U-Haul trucks to manage the surge in package volumes. This strategy allowed them to temporarily expand their fleets and ensure deliveries, supplementing their own drivers and seasonal hires. Amazon also experienced a record-breaking holiday season, with significant increases in Prime Free One-Day and Same-Day delivery services, necessitating a boost in its seasonal workforce.

title: Amazon boxes a holiday gift for paper mills
summary: U.S. paper mills are capitalizing on the "Amazon effect" this holiday season by recycling a surge of used cardboard boxes into new paper products, transitioning from newsprint to containerboard demand driven by e-commerce giants. This shift is crucial following China's 2018 ban on contaminated recyclable imports, which caused a domestic oversupply of cardboard and prompted significant foreign investment in U.S. paper mills. Despite challenges with contamination, the paper industry achieved a record 96% recycling recovery rate for cardboard boxes in 2018, highlighting a successful circular economy model.

title: Kornit Digital CEO: We're aiming for $1b annual sales
summary: Kornit Digital CEO Ronen Samuel outlines an ambitious goal of reaching $1 billion in annual sales, driven by new product launches, geographical expansion, and a focus on sustainable, on-demand digital textile printing. The company aims to capture a 2% share of the 15 billion annual textile printings market by 2023, while also exploring non-organic growth through acquisitions in workflow solutions and machine-related technologies. Samuel emphasizes the company's commitment to growth as an Israeli manufacturing entity, rather than seeking an exit.

title: Lands' End sees positive results in a return to its classic roots
summary: Lands' End is experiencing positive results by returning to its classic roots after previous attempts to become a high-fashion brand failed. Under CEO Jerome Griffith, the company has seen improved sales, a growing customer base, and strategic expansions, including selling on Amazon and opening more standalone stores. Analysts generally express optimism about the brand's "rebirth," though some caution that its future success in 2020 and 2021 remains to be seen.

title: Could Amazon Buy eBay In A 2020 Cash Deal?
summary: This article explores the possibility of Amazon acquiring eBay in a cash deal in 2020, analyzing eBay's struggles, the impact of activist investors, and Amazon's financial capacity. It discusses how eBay's asset-light model offers attractive margins and could complement Amazon's third-party seller services, despite potential antitrust scrutiny. The author also details eBay's history of leadership changes and activist intervention, highlighting the company's declining market share against growing competition.

title: After its strongest year in a decade, Apple stock is historically expensive on a price-to-earnings basis
summary: Apple's stock concluded its strongest year in a decade with its price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio reaching a historic high of 24.7, up from just over 13 at the beginning of 2019. This elevated P/E ratio makes Apple historically expensive compared to its past performance, although it remains below the average for the S&P 500 information technology index and many other megacap tech stocks. Factors like improved iPhone 11 expectations, anticipation of the 5G 2020 iPhone cycle, and strong wearable device performance have contributed to the increased valuation, according to Deutsche Bank analyst Jeriel Ong.

title: Investors Love Thematic ETFs and Mutual Funds, but They Aren’t Always Loved Back - WSJ
summary: This article discusses the popularity of thematic ETFs and mutual funds among investors, despite their potential for disappointment. It highlights how these funds allow investors to target specific industries like space, AI, or clean energy. The article also mentions the performance of several thematic funds through October, suggesting that investors should approach them with caution.

title: UPS expects a record-breaking 1.9 million returns on National Returns Day
summary: UPS forecasts a record 1.9 million returns on National Returns Day, marking a 26% increase from the previous year. This will be the seventh consecutive record broken on National Returns Day, driven by the ongoing growth of e-commerce activities. The article highlights how Amazon's convenient delivery and return services contribute to this trend.

title: Fiserv and ExxonMobil will Enable Consumers to Fill Up by Asking Alexa to Pay at the Pump
summary: Fiserv and ExxonMobil announced a partnership to allow consumers to pay for fuel at over 11,500 Exxon and Mobil stations using Amazon Alexa. This new voice-activated payment method, powered by Fiserv's digital commerce technology and Amazon Pay, will be available later in 2020 and demonstrated at CES 2020. It aims to provide a frictionless and secure transaction experience for consumers in Alexa-enabled vehicles or using other Alexa mobility devices.

title: FedEx Begins Construction on Distribution Facility in Florida
summary: FedEx has started construction on a new 42,000-square-foot distribution center near the Gainesville, Florida airport, a project expected to cost around $9 million and add 20 jobs. This new facility will replace a currently leased FedEx location and is strategically located to cater to the growing online commerce in the area. Other major logistics players like Amazon and UPS are also expanding or considering expansion in Gainesville and Ocala, highlighting the region's importance for distribution.

title: 19 Top Identity Management Solutions
summary: This article identifies 19 top identity management solutions, explaining their role in modern cybersecurity, particularly within a "zero trust" framework. It details the features and benefits of each solution, highlighting how they enhance security by managing user access and credentials. The solutions discussed range from multi-factor authentication tools to comprehensive IT-HR platforms designed to streamline access control and improve data protection.

title: MTBC Acquires Cloud-based EHR Platform CareCloud - Healthcare M&A
summary: MTBC, a provider of cloud-based healthcare IT and revenue cycle management solutions, announced the acquisition of CareCloud, a cloud-based practice management EHR platform. This acquisition aims to accelerate MTBC's strategic roadmap by integrating CareCloud's advanced technology and expanding its network of healthcare providers. The deal was completed on a cash-free, debt-free basis and is expected to drive growth and operational efficiencies for the combined entities.

title: New FIS headquarters in Brooklyn wins conceptual design approval
summary: The proposed Fidelity National Information Services Inc. (FIS) world headquarters in Brooklyn received unanimous conceptual design approval. The 12-story, 350,000 square-foot office tower will include an eight-story parking garage with mixed-use office and retail space, though its public accessibility was a point of discussion. The project, valued at $145 million, aims to consolidate FIS's Jacksonville operations and create 500 new jobs by 2022.

title: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos to Face Protests From ‘Enraged’ Local Merchants During India Visit
summary: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos is expected to encounter significant protests from local merchants during his visit to India. These merchants, organized under the Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT), plan sit-ins and rallies across 300 cities to protest Amazon's pricing and exclusive selling practices, which they argue harm small businesses. The protests coincide with Bezos's participation in Amazon India’s "smbhav" event, highlighting growing resentment against the company's business model in a critical market.

title: Amazon lifts ban on FedEx Ground for third-party Prime shipments
summary: Amazon has lifted its ban on FedEx Ground for third-party Prime shipments, nearly a month after imposing it. The decision comes after Amazon notified its third-party merchants that they could once again use FedEx's service. This change follows Amazon's assessment that FedEx's service levels have improved since the Christmas rush.

title: Target was strong where it needed strength, and that bodes well for the rest of the year
summary: Target's 2019 holiday sales missed expectations, causing a stock selloff, primarily due to weakness in electronics, toys, and home goods. Despite the overall miss, the company showed strength in key investment areas like apparel, beauty, and food, which analysts believe bodes well for its long-term strategy and profitability. CEO Brian Cornell expressed confidence, maintaining the retailer's earnings outlook due to strong gross margin mix and effective digital fulfillment.

title: Can Baby Yoda save Build-A-Bear?
summary: Build-A-Bear, once a successful toy company that went public in 2004, has seen its financial fortunes decline significantly due to struggles in brick-and-mortar retail. The company's stock, which once hit $36.90, averaged $4.37 over the last year, leading to predictions of zero growth or a small drop for the fiscal year 2019. However, the announcement of a Baby Yoda plush toy, a collaboration with Disney's popular "The Mandalorian" series, caused Build-A-Bear's stock to skyrocket 15%, offering a potential lifeline for the struggling retailer.

title: San Jose city, business leaders announce new ‘Innovation Zone’
summary: San Jose city officials and business leaders have announced a new "innovation zone" on the city's west side, encompassing parts of District 1 and District 6. This zone will allow companies like Bird, Siemens, Amazon Web Services, and Verizon to test new technologies, with early pilots including "anti-sidewalk" technology for scooters. Additionally, discussions are underway to convert the historic Century 21 theater building into an "Innovation Hub."

title: Moderna Partners with AWS to Explore the ‘Software of Life’
summary: Moderna is partnering with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to accelerate the development of personalized therapies, particularly for cancer, by leveraging AWS's cloud computing platforms for gene sequencing. Moderna's CEO, Stephane Bancel, likens messenger RNA (mRNA) to "software of life" and highlights its potential in directing the body to produce therapeutic proteins. The collaboration aims to speed up the drug development process from preclinical to clinical phases and is already being used for over a dozen drug candidates.

title: Austin-based Wikibuy is Booming Since its Acquisition by Capital One
summary: Austin-based Wikibuy has experienced significant growth and success since its acquisition by Capital One in November 2018. The company has expanded its employee base and user count, evolving from a comparison-shopping engine to include features like automatic coupon application and cash-back rebates. Wikibuy continues to operate from Austin, contributing to the city's booming e-commerce sector.

title: Intel Board of Directors Elects New Chairman and New Director
summary: Intel Corporation announced that Andy D. Bryant stepped down as chairman of the board, and Dr. Omar Ishrak was elected to succeed him as independent chairman, effective immediately. Additionally, Alyssa Henry was elected to Intel’s board, marking the seventh new independent director added since 2016. Bryant will remain on the board until the 2020 annual stockholders’ meeting to facilitate a smooth transition.

title: Tesla created demand for electric cars, but only for Teslas
summary: Despite a surge in new electric vehicle models hitting the market, Tesla remains the dominant player and virtually the only car company profiting from EV sales. Traditional automakers are hesitant to fully embrace EVs due to high costs, range anxiety among consumers, and the expectation that supply will outpace demand. While government mandates are driving EV adoption in other regions, the US market is slower to shift, with hybrids still preferred by many consumers over pure electrics.

title: Top 16 best datacenter service providers in India
summary: This article lists the top 16 data center service providers in India, highlighting the booming demand for data center infrastructure driven by increasing internet users and cloud adoption. It details each company's offerings, locations, and key features to assist businesses in choosing a suitable provider. The list includes both global and local players, detailing their services and infrastructure.

title: The five biggest tech companies now make up 17.5% of the S&P 500 — here's how to protect yourself
summary: The five largest tech companies (Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Facebook) now comprise 17.5% of the S&P 500, leading to potential overexposure for passive investors. Financial advisors are suggesting strategies like equal-weighted funds, specialized tech ETFs focusing on emerging areas, and ESG investments to diversify portfolios. While Big Tech's dominance has driven strong returns, advisors emphasize balancing diversification with access to growth, cautioning against timing the market with large active bets.

title: Which tech stock is best? Here’s how the ‘big five’ companies stack up as they report earnings
summary: This article examines how the "big five" U.S. tech companies are positioned as they prepare to report their quarterly earnings. It highlights Amazon as the favorite among analysts, while Apple is deemed the "cheapest" despite its recent stock performance. The article sets out to compare some of their key numbers ahead of Apple kicking off the earnings season.

title: IBM's Ginni Rometty stepping down as CEO for cloud computing chief
summary: Ginni Rometty is stepping down as CEO of IBM, with Arvind Krishna, the current senior vice president for cloud and cognitive software, set to take over on April 6. Rometty will remain executive chairman until the end of the year. James Whitehurst, CEO of Red Hat, will become president of IBM.

title: FedEx Has a Plan to Battle Amazon Shipping, CEO Says
summary: FedEx CEO Fred Smith outlines his strategy for battling Amazon in the shipping industry and overcoming recent setbacks. He plans to position FedEx as an anti-Amazon ally for retailers, aiming to surpass UPS in size and become the most cost-efficient ground courier. Smith expresses confidence his plan will prove successful despite past challenges and current skepticism from analysts.

title: IBM CEO Ginni Rometty stepping down, cloud boss Arvind Krishna to succeed
summary: Ginni Rometty is stepping down as CEO of IBM after eight years, with cloud boss Arvind Krishna set to succeed her in April. Rometty, a 40-year IBM veteran, spearheaded numerous acquisitions, including the $34 billion Red Hat deal, as the company worked to catch up in the cloud services market. Despite a recent revenue growth, IBM's stock value declined about a quarter during her tenure, and the company's turnaround remains ongoing.

title: Go behind the scenes as Amazon develops a new electric vehicle
summary: Amazon and Rivian are collaborating to introduce thousands of custom electric delivery vans to 100 U.S. cities by the end of the year, aiming to build the world's most sustainable transportation fleet. This initiative is part of Amazon's commitment to The Climate Pledge, an effort to become net zero carbon by 2040 and reduce millions of metric tons of carbon annually by 2030. The new vehicles emphasize driver safety, optimize technology and design, and integrate Amazon's logistics management and Alexa for a seamless delivery experience.

title: IITian Arvind Krishna to be new IBM CEO, replacing Ginni Rometty
summary: International Business Machines Corp. has named Arvind Krishna as its new chief executive officer, succeeding Ginni Rometty. Krishna, previously head of IBM’s cloud and cognitive software unit, was a key architect of the Red Hat acquisition and will take over after Rometty retires later this year. The announcement was well-received by the market, with shares rising 5% in extended trading, as analysts view the leadership change as a positive and overdue step for the company's innovation in hybrid cloud.

title: IIT Kanpur graduate Arvind Krishna is new IBM CEO
summary: Arvind Krishna, an IIT Kanpur graduate and head of IBM’s cloud business, will take over as CEO from Ginni Rometty in April. Rometty, who led the company for eight years and oversaw the $34 billion Red Hat acquisition, will continue as executive chairman until the end of the year. The transition comes as IBM continues its efforts to rejuvenate and boost its cloud services business.

title: Arvind Krishna, the man who helped buy Red Hat, now wears the CEO hat at IBM
summary: Arvind Krishna has been named the new CEO of IBM, replacing Virginia Rometty. Krishna, known for being the principal architect behind IBM’s $34 billion acquisition of Red Hat, will lead the company as Rometty retires after nearly 40 years. This leadership change is seen as a welcome move to accelerate IBM's focus on hybrid cloud and AI after years of declining sales under Rometty.

title: Arvind Krishna named IBM CEO as company fights for cloud business spot
summary: IBM has named Arvind Krishna as its new CEO, taking over from Ginni Rometty, as the company intensifies its efforts to compete in the cloud services market. IBM was a late entrant to this sector, which is currently dominated by Amazon and Microsoft. Rometty's tenure was marked by 65 acquisitions, including the significant $34 billion Red Hat deal, aimed at boosting IBM's cloud presence.

title: Sierra-Cedar to Sell Workday, Salesforce, and U.S. MuleSoft Practices to Accenture
summary: Sierra-Cedar announced an agreement to sell its Workday, Salesforce, and U.S. MuleSoft practices to Accenture, with approximately 275 professionals joining Accenture. The transaction allows Sierra-Cedar to enhance its focus and investment in core growth areas like Oracle Cloud and AWS, while its Indian MuleSoft practice remains unaffected. Sierra-Cedar will continue to operate as a dedicated technology partner to Oracle and AWS, led by CEO Cal Yonker.

title: IBM replaces CEO: Ginni Rometty is on her way out
summary: IBM has named Arvind Krishna as its new chief executive officer, replacing Ginni Rometty, who will transition to executive chairman before retiring at the end of the year. Krishna, a key architect of the Red Hat acquisition, will lead IBM's focus on hybrid cloud and AI. Rometty, the company's first female CEO, staked IBM's future on hybrid cloud and oversaw the $34 billion Red Hat purchase, though the company's market value and revenue declined during her tenure.

title: IBM’s new CEO Arvind Krishna is mastermind behind cloud strategy for growth
summary: Arvind Krishna, IBM’s new CEO, is credited with conceptualizing the company’s hybrid cloud strategy in 2017, a move that revitalized the 108-year-old tech giant. His vision led to the acquisition of Red Hat and a strategic shift towards cloud computing, similar to Satya Nadella's successful leadership at Microsoft. Analysts and former colleagues believe Krishna is well-suited to transform IBM and steer it towards future growth in the competitive tech market.

title: Goldman Sachs in talks with Amazon to offer small-business loans
summary: Goldman Sachs is reportedly close to a deal with Amazon to offer small-business loans to Amazon's U.S. customers, aiming to expand its reach onto Main Street. This move aligns with Goldman's strategy to diversify beyond trading and investment banking, while Amazon benefits by extending its lending platform without incurring significant credit risk or regulatory obligations. The partnership would leverage Goldman's financial services expertise and Amazon's vast network of small and medium-sized sellers, further solidifying both companies' ventures into new market segments.

title: IBM replaces Ginni Rometty, names Arvind Krishna as CEO
summary: IBM has named Arvind Krishna, head of the company's cloud business, as its new CEO, succeeding Ginni Rometty. The leadership change, announced on January 31, 2020, comes amidst fierce competition from Microsoft Azure and Amazon AWS, and surprised some Wall Street analysts. Krishna, credited with IBM's $34 billion acquisition of Red Hat, will assume the role in April.

title: Starbucks improves customer experience with AI
summary: Starbucks is enhancing its customer experience through the deployment of AI-equipped hardware and analytics. The company plans to install 4,000 AI-enabled Mastrena II espresso makers in 2020 and is leveraging its Deep Brew AI engine to understand customer preferences better and increase efficiency. These efforts, combined with significant growth in its loyalty program and digital customer base, are contributing to improved service, brand loyalty, and new offerings.

title: Virgin Galactic Stock: A Unique High-Flying Infrastructure Stock to Watch in 2020
summary: Virgin Galactic Holdings (SPCE) is presented as a unique infrastructure stock with significant growth potential in the burgeoning space economy, estimated to reach $1.5 trillion by 2040. The company aims to be the world's first commercial spaceline, launching paying passengers into suborbital space. Despite being speculative and not yet profitable, Virgin Galactic has made progress with test flights and plans to reopen ticket sales, making it a stock worth watching for risk-tolerant investors.

title: STARZ AND LIONSGATE INK OUTPUT DEAL FOR SPLIT THEATRICAL STREAMING WINDOW IN THE UK
summary: STARZPLAY has entered a multi-year theatrical output deal with Lionsgate for split first-pay streaming rights in the UK. This agreement will bring Lionsgate's recent and upcoming feature films, including "Knives Out" and "Bombshell," to STARZPLAY subscribers just six months after their Amazon Prime Video debut in the territory. The deal aims to enhance STARZPLAY's content offering and support its international expansion.

title: Amazon Revenue vs Net Income by Quarter
summary: This article details Amazon's quarterly revenue and net income performance from Q1 1997 through Q4 2019, highlighting key financial milestones. It notes Amazon achieving a record high revenue of $87,437 million in Q4 2019 and its first profitable quarter in Q4 2001. The article also provides a brief overview of Amazon Inc., its history, and major products.

title: Are QVC and HSN Destined to Die?
summary: This article questions the future of home shopping networks QVC and HSN in an era dominated by online retail and changing consumer preferences. Despite declining stock prices and revenue, the author highlights QVC's efforts, including a merger with HSN, improved online sales, flexible payment options, and strong customer service, suggesting these strategies might help them survive. The piece ultimately expresses hope for their continued existence.

title: eBay is more like the NYSE than Amazon, says Intercontinental Exchange CEO Jeffrey Sprecher
summary: Jeffrey Sprecher, CEO of Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), argued that eBay, an e-commerce giant, more closely resembles the New York Stock Exchange than Amazon. He suggested eBay should be viewed as a 25-year-old cash market for collectible goods, emphasizing business model similarities like matching buyers and sellers, data collection, and third-party partnerships. This perspective emerged as ICE clarified its discussions with eBay, which it ultimately ceased pursuing for strategic opportunities.

title: Uber is ready to join the FANG camp, analyst says after earnings
summary: Following its latest earnings report, an analyst suggested that Uber Technologies Inc. is ready to join the ranks of major internet companies like Facebook, Amazon, Netflix, and Google. RBC Capital Markets analyst Mark Mahaney proposed the acronym FANGU, adding Uber, as the company works towards profitability and leverages its scale. This optimism led to an 8% increase in Uber's stock price on Friday morning.

title: Matt Desch, CEO of Iridium Communications, Named to 2020 Wash100 for Driving Revenue, Tech Advancement
summary: Matt Desch, CEO of Iridium Communications, has been inducted into the 2020 Wash100 Award for his continuous efforts in driving revenue and advancing satellite, IoT, and cloud technologies. This marks his sixth consecutive Wash100 award, highlighting his significant impact on the government contracting sector through initiatives like Iridium's L-band broadband service, partnerships with Satelles and Amazon Web Services, and authorization for GMDSS satellite services. His leadership has led to substantial growth for Iridium, including a 12 percent revenue increase in Q1 2019 and a 25 percent rise in commercial IoT data subscribers.

title: Are video games a worthwhile investment?
summary: Raj Lala, CEO of Evolve ETFs, discusses the investment potential of the video game industry, explaining why he launched the HERO ETF to provide exposure to major gaming companies. He highlights the significant evolution of the industry's revenue model beyond simple sales, citing in-app purchases, subscriptions, and esports as key drivers. Lala emphasizes that gaming fits into Evolve's strategy of investing in disruptive technologies that will shape the future and advises financial advisors to understand the full ecosystem of the market.

title: Amazon’s Total Stock-based Compensation Expense, by Quarter
summary: This article analyzes Amazon's total stock-based compensation expense by quarter from 1998, highlighting significant increases, such as $1,840 million in Q4 2019, a 29.9% year-over-year rise. It notes Amazon's substantial workforce of approximately 798,000 employees as of December 2019 and provides background on Amazon's history and key offerings.

title: Tyler Technologies Tops $1B in Annual Revenue for First Time
summary: Tyler Technologies announced its annual revenue surpassed $1 billion for the first time in 2019, reaching $1.068 billion, a 16.2 percent increase from 2018. The company, a leading provider of public sector software, expects continued double-digit growth and aims for $2 billion in annual revenue, supported by its Connected Communities vision and strategic investments in cloud technologies and acquisitions.

title: Oracle’s Larry Ellison makes friends with his enemy’s enemy, hosting a fundraiser for President Trump
summary: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison is hosting a fundraiser for President Donald Trump, aligning with a shared adversary of Amazon and its CEO Jeff Bezos. Ellison's company has a fierce rivalry with Amazon's cloud computing wing, and Trump has openly expressed a desire to "screw Amazon." This move places Ellison among a few Silicon Valley figures who have publicly supported Trump, despite potential backlash from the tech industry.

title: How Blackstone became the world’s biggest corporate landlord
summary: Blackstone has grown to become the world's largest corporate landlord, accumulating $325 billion in real estate assets through strategic investments since going public in 2007. The firm employs both "opportunistic" (BREP) and "Core+" (BREIT) funds, focusing on distressed properties and stable rental income, respectively, while increasingly targeting warehouses in "last-mile infill" areas due to the e-commerce boom. Its ability to raise massive funds allows it to make large-scale deals with limited competition, shaping its investment strategy around fast-growing "knowledge centers."

title: This Growth ETF Continues Winning
summary: The article discusses the continued outperformance of growth stocks over value stocks in early 2020, driven by technology and consumer discretionary sectors. It highlights the SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 Growth ETF (SPYG) as a strong performer, noting its impressive year-to-date gains compared to the broader S&P 500 and S&P 500 Value Index. The piece also contrasts growth and value investing strategies and mentions significant inflows into SPYG.

title: Israeli VC Firm Grove Ventures Closes $120M Fund For Deep Tech Startups
summary: Israeli VC firm Grove Ventures announced the closure of its Grove Ventures II Fund (Grove II), raising $120 million to invest in early-stage, deep tech startups in Israel targeting European and US markets. The fund, which was oversubscribed, focuses on companies developing "hard-to-replicate solutions" across various sectors, led by serial entrepreneur Dov Moran. Grove Ventures aims to empower deep tech entrepreneurs to build international companies and address significant industry challenges with innovative technology.

title: Franklin-Legg Mason combo could produce nontransparent ETF powerhouse
summary: The pending merger of Franklin Resources and Legg Mason, while having a relatively small combined ETF asset base, could position them as a significant player in the nontransparent ETF space. This potential stems from Legg Mason's majority stake in Precidian Investments, a company licensing nontransparent ETF structures, which could give the merged entity a first-mover advantage as these new fund types are expected to launch soon. Nontransparent ETFs offer a new avenue for active mutual fund managers to enter the ETF market with potential benefits like lower costs and greater tax efficiency.

title: Piedmont Pays $396M for Dallas Galleria Office Towers
summary: Piedmont Office Realty Trust acquired the three distinctive Galleria office towers in Dallas for $396 million, marking the largest Dallas-Fort Worth office sale of the year. The transaction included over 1.4 million square feet of Class A office space, associated parking garages, and a 1.9-acre land parcel. This acquisition means Piedmont now owns the entire Galleria portfolio in Dallas, having previously acquired Galleria properties in Atlanta.

title: Beyond ESG: How Individuals Can Influence Corporations
summary: This article discusses how individuals can influence corporations beyond traditional ESG investing by leveraging their consumer choices, employment decisions, and advocacy. It highlights the rise of stakeholder capitalism and provides examples of how customers, employees, suppliers, communities, and shareholders have successfully pressured companies to adopt more responsible practices, leading to positive corporate behavior and potentially superior stock returns.

title: Expedia cuts 3,000 jobs, including 500 at new Seattle HQ — read the internal email to employees
summary: Expedia Group is laying off 3,000 employees, or 12 percent of its workforce, including 500 at its new Seattle headquarters, as part of an effort to "streamline and focus" the company under chairman Barry Diller. These cuts follow the ouster of the CEO and CFO and a commitment to address an "unhealthy and undisciplined" growth strategy, aiming for $300 to $500 million in annual cost savings. The layoffs are not linked to the coronavirus outbreak, though the company expects related profit reductions and will incur $135 million to $185 million in pre-tax charges this year.

title: Checkup for $30, Teeth Cleaning $25: Walmart Gets Into Health Care
summary: Walmart is entering the healthcare market by offering low-cost medical services such as $30 checkups and $25 teeth cleanings in its new Walmart Health centers. This initiative aims to capture a share of the $3.6 trillion health spending by leveraging its large customer base and providing accessible care, even for those without insurance. The retail giant's move positions it as a competitor to existing healthcare providers like CVS and Amazon in communities nationwide.

title: Comcast acquires free video streaming service Xumo
summary: Comcast announced its acquisition of Xumo, a free, ad-supported streaming service, positioning itself to compete in the growing ad-supported streaming market. This strategic move comes ahead of NBCUniversal's launch of its own streaming service, Peacock, which will also offer free, ad-supported content. The acquisition highlights the increasing trend of media companies investing in streaming services as consumers shift away from traditional pay TV.

title: Kraft Heinz invests in $110m Series B for cloud retail robotics startup Fabric
summary: Kraft Heinz, through its venture arm Evolv Ventures, invested in a $110 million Series B round for the cloud retail robotics startup Fabric. Fabric's technology provides automated fulfillment solutions for retailers facing increasing demand for fast e-commerce delivery. The funding will support Fabric's US expansion, aiming to address the challenges retailers face in efficient order fulfillment.

title: Prudential buys local Amazon distribution hub
summary: PGIM Real Estate, a branch of Prudential, has acquired a new Amazon distribution hub located in Antioch, Nashville. This 517,500-square-foot industrial building was developed speculatively, indicating strong confidence in the demand for industrial space in the Nashville market. Amazon is the current tenant, leasing the facility.

title: Walmart is developing a membership program to rival Amazon Prime
summary: Walmart Inc. is developing a new paid membership program called Walmart+ to compete directly with Amazon Prime. This service will expand on Walmart's existing grocery-delivery subscription and aims to attract and retain shoppers who might otherwise turn to Amazon. The initiative highlights Walmart's efforts to counter Amazon's dominance in online retail and customer loyalty.

title: Building operators eager for coronavirus info as one Seattle tower closed Monday
summary: F5 Tower in Seattle was closed for one day due to coronavirus concerns after an employee had contact with someone who tested positive for the virus. This closure highlights the growing concern among building operators seeking information as authorities anticipate an increase in cases.

title: HPE Confirms Discover Conference Still On, Cancels ‘Most’ Events Through April
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has decided to proceed with its annual Discover Las Vegas and Discover More London conferences, despite canceling or postponing most other events through April due to coronavirus concerns. Partners have expressed support for HPE's decision, emphasizing the need to continue business while taking prudent precautions. The company plans to shift resources to digital engagement for customers and partners.

title: Target's online sales surge as shoppers opt for pick up, delivery
summary: Target announced a 20% surge in digital sales, driven by increased use of its pick-up and delivery services. The retailer plans to expand its online offerings to include perishables like milk, wine, and beer for drive-up pickup, and will also experiment with even smaller store formats. Target also addressed concerns regarding the coronavirus, stating its impact on performance is not notable, but they are preparing for potential supply chain delays.

title: Carlyle Group’s $1.4 Billion Folly: Inside The Biggest Buyout Loss In Washington, D.C. Firm’s 33-Year History
summary: Carlyle Group's $1.4 billion equity investment in Acosta was completely wiped out, marking the biggest buyout loss in the firm's 33-year history. Acosta, a food broker, faced declining revenues due to shifting consumer preferences and aggressive cost-cutting by clients, leading to a bankruptcy filing despite Carlyle's efforts. The article highlights the growing trend of private equity firms trading companies among themselves and the risks associated with high debt levels in such deals.

title: Lawmakers ask Amazon, EBay to crack down on counterfeit sales
summary: House lawmakers are urging Amazon.com Inc. and EBay Inc. to take stronger action against third-party vendors selling fake, stolen, or unsafe goods on their platforms. The bipartisan request follows concerns about organized retail crime and counterfeit products, especially those originating from China. Both Amazon and EBay executives testified that they are investing in tools and supporting law enforcement to combat fraudulent listings.

title: Theme Lab: A Look Inside An Amazon Fulfillment Center
summary: This article details a "Theme Lab" visit to an Amazon Fulfillment Center, showcasing how robotics, IoT, AI, and human labor collaborate in the Stowing, Picking, Packing, and Shipping phases. It highlights the critical synergistic roles of these technologies and human expertise in achieving efficiency in e-commerce fulfillment. The article concludes by discussing related ETFs that track these disruptive technologies.

title: Watch Jessica Alba Put Her Product Prowess to the Test in ELLE's Beauty Haul
summary: Jessica Alba, co-founder of The Honest Company and Honest Beauty, takes on ELLE's "Beauty Haul" challenge. She demonstrates her clean beauty routine, shopping for products with a $150 budget and applying a full face of makeup in under 30 minutes. Alba highlights her favorite Honest Beauty products and explains her approach to clean beauty, emphasizing natural ingredients and avoiding fragrances.

title: Alliance Data: Is Three a Charm with a New CEO?
summary: Alliance Data, a private label credit card company, is facing significant challenges, including a ten-year stock low and rising charge-off rates, as a new CEO, Ralph Andretta, takes the helm. The article highlights the company's reliance on proprietary credit scores instead of FICO, a lack of innovation compared to competitors like Synchrony, and the need for a strategy to convert weaker credit accounts to branded network cards. The new CEO has initiated a "listening tour" to develop a strategic plan for the struggling firm.

title: Costco sales surge 11% as coronavirus fear prompts stockpiling
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported an 11% surge in sales due to customer stockpiling of essentials amid coronavirus fears, forcing frequent replenishment of items. The company also exceeded holiday-quarter expectations with a 28% increase in e-commerce sales and strong membership revenue, while acknowledging the continued rise in traffic into March. Analyst Garrett Nelson of CFRA Research considers Costco a primary beneficiary of coronavirus-related consumer stockpiling.

title: Champion Jumps to Amazon From Target for Discount C9 Brand
summary: Champion, owned by Hanesbrands Inc., has moved its C9 apparel line to Amazon.com Inc. after its agreement with Target Corp. ended. Amazon has entered into a two-year deal to offer the C9 line, marking the first time C9 will be available globally.

title: Burlington Stores walks away from e-commerce
summary: Burlington Stores is winding down its e-commerce operations, citing the difficulty of making a profit on low-priced items online, the challenge of replicating the "treasure hunt" experience digitally, and the strong performance of its physical stores. This decision comes despite the growth of e-commerce in other retail sectors, as Burlington focuses its resources on brick-and-mortar growth. The move sparks debate among experts about its long-term implications for the off-price retailer.

title: NetApp sinks claws into Talon Storage
summary: NetApp has acquired Talon Storage, a company specializing in caching software that connects branch offices to public cloud file servers. The acquisition aims to provide a unified footprint for unstructured data, enabling seamless access for users regardless of their geographical location. Talon's FAST software will allow NetApp to offer an indirect remote office/branch office (ROBO) presence without requiring on-premises NetApp filers.

title: HanesBrands Launches Popular C9 Champion Brand With Amazon in Multiyear Exclusive Agreement
summary: HanesBrands has launched its popular C9 Champion performance athleticwear exclusively on Amazon Fashion worldwide through a multiyear agreement. The value-priced line, which includes activewear, innerwear, and accessories for the whole family, aims to reach a broader global consumer base and complement the existing mainline Champion brand on Amazon.

title: Costco tells office workers
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is requiring its head office employees in Issaquah to report to work, despite public health requests to allow remote work. CEO W. Craig Jelinek stated that this decision is based on equity and fairness, as the majority of Costco employees work in stores and warehouses and do not have the option to work from home. This contrasts with companies like Amazon and Microsoft, which have allowed many office workers to work remotely amid coronavirus concerns.

title: Starbucks stores may go drive-thru only or limit seating to address coronavirus concerns
summary: Starbucks announced that some of its stores in the U.S. and Canada might transition to drive-thru only or limit seating to address concerns about the coronavirus pandemic. The company plans to make these decisions on a store-by-store basis and may temporarily close stores as a last resort. Starbucks has also expanded catastrophe pay for employees affected by the virus, and its shares have significantly dropped amid the outbreak.

title: Zero-Day Bug In Verisign And IaaS Services Allowed Registering of Malicious Domains With Homoglyph
summary: A zero-day bug found in Verisign and various IaaS services allowed cybercriminals to register malicious domains using homoglyphs, making them appear visually identical to legitimate sites. A researcher exposed the flaw, which had been actively exploited since 2017, and successfully registered imposter domains for major companies. While Verisign and Amazon have implemented mitigations, other services have yet to address the vulnerability.

title: Synchrony Financial agrees to 10-year deal to stay in Kettering
summary: Synchrony Financial, a major employer in Kettering, has secured a 10-year agreement to remain in the Kettering Business Park. The city extended a $675,000 Economic Development Incentive Grant for a five-year lease with a five-year option, with the company committing to maintain 1,900 full-time equivalent positions. This deal highlights Synchrony's significance to the local economy and the city's efforts to retain key businesses.

title: Bill Gates steps down from Microsoft board
summary: Bill Gates announced he is stepping down from the boards of Microsoft and Berkshire Hathaway to dedicate more time to philanthropy, focusing on global health, education, and climate change through the Gates Foundation. He will continue to serve as a technology advisor to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. Gates, who co-founded Microsoft in 1975, remains one of the world's richest individuals.

title: WeRide resumes robotaxi service in China after COVID-19
summary: WeRide, an L4 AV smart mobility company based in Guangzhou, China, has resumed its robotaxi service with strict precautions after COVID-19. The company has implemented measures such as nucleic acid tests for safety drivers, daily health checks, mandatory mask-wearing, and vehicle sanitization after every two trips to ensure the safety of riders and drivers. WeRide, which partners with Amazon's AWS, emphasizes its R&D and claims to have one of the largest autonomous vehicle fleets among Chinese startups, having covered over 1,150,000 kilometers.

title: Amazon to hire 100,000 workers as online orders surge on coronavirus worries
summary: Amazon.com Inc announced plans to hire 100,000 warehouse and delivery workers in the United States to manage a significant increase in online orders due to the coronavirus outbreak. The company will also add $2 to its minimum $15 per hour wage for U.S. workers through April, an initiative expected to cost over $350 million across North America and Europe. Other retailers are also seeking new hires as consumers shift to online shopping and stock up on essential goods.

title: Canadian Solar secures €55m financing to build 151MW solar projects in Italy
summary: Canadian Solar has secured €55m ($60.6m) in financing from Intesa Sanpaolo for the construction of a 151MW portfolio of 12 solar projects in Italy. These projects, located in Sicily, Apulia, and Lazio, are expected to generate 287GWh of clean energy annually and are among the country's first subsidy-free utility-scale solar plants. The company also recently signed a PPA with Amazon for its Gunnedah solar plant in Australia.

title: Coconut water is the pandemic’s newest shortage
summary: Amid coronavirus concerns, sales of coconut water, particularly from Vita Coco, have surged significantly across the U.S., depleting typical stockpiles and straining supply chains. While other bottled waters are also in high demand, this trend raises concerns about potential supply disruptions if borders close, especially since coconuts are not grown in the US.

title: Broadcom Asserts Patents Covering ‘Crucial Aspects’ of Netflix Content Delivery
summary: Broadcom Corporation has filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Netflix, Inc. in the Central District of California, alleging that Netflix's streaming service infringes on nine of Broadcom's U.S. patents. The patents cover technologies crucial for reliable content delivery, efficient server use, and video encoding. Broadcom claims Netflix's infringement has harmed its set-top box business by drawing consumers away from cable television.

title: Reese Witherspoon’s Draper James and Land’s End Dive Into Swimwear
summary: Reese Witherspoon’s Draper James brand partnered with Land's End to launch a limited-edition women's swimwear collection. The collaboration combines Draper James' signature Southern-inspired prints with Land’s End's swim expertise, offering 23 pieces in sizes XS-3X. A portion of the proceeds from the collection will be donated to Girls Inc.

title: Marcus Corp. operates cinemas, hotels and restaurants. Here's how it's weathering the coronavirus pandemic.
summary: Marcus Corp., encompassing hotels and movie theaters, has been severely impacted by the coronavirus pandemic. CEO Greg Marcus is focused on financially preserving the company and supporting laid-off employees while navigating the unprecedented economic shock. Despite the challenges, Marcus believes the company's conservative financial approach will help it survive until business returns to normal.

title: Conduent Collaborates with Amazon Web Services to Help Government Agencies Scale Their COVID-19 Response
summary: Conduent announced that its Maven disease surveillance platform, configured for COVID-19 case management, patient outreach, and contact tracing visualization, is now available on Amazon Web Services (AWS). To support public health agencies, Conduent is waiving the software license fee for the Maven COVID-19 module through June 30, 2020, for qualified state and territorial-level agencies. This collaboration enables rapid and scalable deployment of critical tools to help "flatten the curve" by digitizing contact tracing and reporting.

title: Chipotle joins Starbucks, Amazon with coronavirus pay bump
summary: Chipotle announced a 10 percent pay increase for its hourly employees working between March 16 and April 12, joining companies like Starbucks and Amazon in providing additional compensation during the coronavirus pandemic. This initiative, along with updated emergency benefits, aims to show appreciation for workers during a time when many businesses are shifting to takeout or delivery-only operations. Other companies, including Albertsons, Kroger, Walmart, and McDonald's, are also offering similar support to their employees.

title: Maintaining a high-speed connection: A new playbook for cable growth
summary: This article outlines strategies for the cable industry to maintain growth, focusing on becoming a digital-first enterprise, doubling down on B2B growth, and becoming a leading smart-home player. It highlights the industry's strong current position while addressing looming long-term challenges such as regulatory risks and 5G competition. The authors emphasize the importance of strategic shifts to avoid becoming a "dumb pipe" and to continue increasing the value of customer relationships.

title: Social Media Moves to New Era of Growth
summary: Social media platforms are entering a new era of growth, shifting focus from user acquisition to maximizing revenue per user through targeted advertising and innovative technologies. New avenues like social commerce and AR/VR are being explored to diversify revenue streams. This evolution includes in-app purchases, live-streaming commerce, and augmented reality experiences to further engage users and drive monetization.

title: DoorDash Starts Delivering Toilet Paper and Other Groceries
summary: DoorDash, the largest food delivery app in the U.S., is expanding its services to include deliveries from convenience stores like 7-Eleven and Wawa. This accelerated rollout, prompted by the coronavirus pandemic, allows customers to order essential goods such as toilet paper and other packaged items. The company currently has over 1,800 convenience stores listed on its app across the U.S.

title: Home Depot Halts Sales of N95 Masks Amid Shortage, Company Says (Published 2020)
summary: Home Depot has halted sales of N95 masks at all of its North American stores and redirected them to healthcare providers and emergency responders due to the coronavirus pandemic. Other retailers like Lowe's and Target have also taken similar actions, while 3M, a mask manufacturer, has expressed concern over retailers continuing to sell protective gear. The move aims to address the critical shortage of personal protective equipment for frontline workers.

title: Jessica Alba's The Honest Company Has Donated 3 Million Diapers To Help Families In Need
summary: Jessica Alba's The Honest Company has donated three million diapers, 20,000 wipes, and 20,000 personal care products to families in need during the coronavirus pandemic. Alba emphasized that these donations address the critical needs of families facing difficult choices between essentials like diapers and food. Her husband, Cash Warren, also contributed through his company, Pair of Thieves, by donating profits to purchase relief supplies and masks for front-line workers.

title: EBay pledges $100M to help small businesses move online
summary: eBay has launched its "Up & Running" accelerator program, investing $100 million to help North American small businesses without an online presence transition to e-commerce. The program offers free basic eBay stores for three months, waived selling fees for up to 500 items, and provides marketing tools, discounted shipping, and educational resources. This initiative responds to the increased focus on e-commerce due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with 70% of small businesses reportedly lacking an online presence before the outbreak.

title: Infographic: Retailers’ cage-free egg pledges
summary: U.S. egg producers are converting to cage-free systems as North American retailers commit to sourcing only cage-free eggs. While some retailers already exclusively sell cage-free eggs, many others, including major grocery chains, are still in transition, with most aiming for completion by 2025 or 2026. This shift is also driven by new laws in several U.S. states requiring cage-free egg production and sales.

title: Uber Aids Idled Rideshare Drivers With Job Listings
summary: Uber is launching "Work Hub," an initiative to connect its rideshare drivers, who are experiencing diminished income due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with alternative job listings. These opportunities include roles within Uber, such as Uber Freight or Uber Eats, and with other companies like Domino’s, Shipt, and CareGuide, covering positions in food production, warehousing, and customer service. The company also encouraged drivers to join Uber Eats, which has seen increased demand, and is contributing to a Restaurant Employee Relief Fund.

title: SoFi acquires banking tech firm Galileo for $1.2 billion
summary: SoFi announced its acquisition of Galileo, a banking tech firm that powers companies like Robinhood and Chime, for $1.2 billion. The deal involves $875 million in SoFi shares, $75 million in cash, and $250 million in debt financing. SoFi plans to operate Galileo as an independent entity, providing white-label technology services globally, despite both companies recently experiencing turbulence.

title: BlackBerry uncovers hacker tools that it says opened data servers for a decade
summary: BlackBerry has released a report detailing how five separate groups linked to the Chinese government have been targeting Linux systems for a decade.
